We propose a novel Target self-Attention Spatiotemporal Fusion (TASTF) model that bridges the scale gap between Landsat (30 m) and Global Inventory Modeling and Mapping Studies (GIMMS) (∼8 km) data to generate seamless, 500-m biweekly MODIS-like Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) data dating back to 1984 over the contiguous United States (CONUS). The model integrates a robust optimal image mosaicking method to construct spatially extensive Landsat reference data across CONUS. To enhance spatial continuity, we develop a target self-attention mechanism that embeds patch-wise day-of-year data into the self-attention module to dynamically prioritize target-region pixels, effectively suppressing patch artifacts. Experimental results demonstrate that the TASTF effectively simulates MODIS-like data with accurate spatial details and temporal variations. Post-2000 reconstructions show strong agreement with real MODIS observations, achieving a regional annual root mean square error of 0.089, substantially outperforming GIMMS dataset (0.154). Compared with advanced deep learning models, TASTF results exhibit superior spatial continuity and temporal consistency, achieving a correlation coefficient of 0.993, higher than those of comparison models (0.983 and 0.981). The proposed model and generated MODIS-like data contribute valuable support for long-term, fine-scale land surface monitoring and analysis.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Interannual Dynamics of Boreal Forest Wildfires (2020–2024) Derived from MODIS-Constrained Sentinel-2 Burned-Area Mapping
abstract: Boreal forests are increasingly affected by wildfires, creating a strong need for consistent annual burned-area datasets to support carbon-budget and climate studies. Existing annual burned-area products covering the entire boreal forest are mainly derived from Landsat imagery at 30 m resolution and may still suffer from omission and temporal misallocation in annual mapping. Here, we present BS2BAM, an automated burned-area mapping framework that integrates MODIS fire products and Sentinel-2 time-series imagery for annual mapping across the boreal forest. MODIS active-fire and burned-area products were first used to define wildfire candidate zones (WCZs). Burned and unburned samples automatically generated from the 2023 Canadian fire season were then used to train a random forest model, which estimated burn probability from Sentinel-2 spectral indices within the WCZ. The resulting probability maps were further refined through region growing to produce annual burned-area maps on a 10 m output grid for 2020–2024. Independent validation showed that, relative to Fire_GFL, BS2BAM reduced omission error from 30.82% to 15.98% and improved the Dice coefficient from 73.39% to 86.73%. Spatiotemporal statistics for 2020–2024 indicate that BS2BAM better captured the 2021 Siberian and 2023 Canadian wildfires than Fire_GFL and GABAM. BS2BAM provides a consistent high-resolution annual burned-area dataset for investigating interannual wildfire dynamics in boreal forests and supporting related carbon-cycle and climate studies.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: DBE-Net: a dual-branch bounding box-embedding network for individual tree segmentation from LiDAR
abstract: Individual tree segmentation (ITS) is of great importance for forest resource surveys. Point cloud-based ITS, which uses deep learning methods, has become a research hotspot. However, the state-of-the-art reported works struggle to accurately segment individual trees in scenarios characterized by canopy overlap and low-density point clouds. To address these limitations, we proposed a Dual-branch Bounding Box-Embedding Network (DBE-Net), which adopts the bounding box branch to delimit the spatial extents of individual trees, thereby providing initial segmentation constraints. Subsequently, foreground points and background points are segmented within these bounding boxes to generate candidate results. The motivation for designing the bounding box branch stems from the difficulty in generating high-quality candidate results using offset vectors and corresponding clustering algorithms. The bounding box branch eliminates the need for a time-consuming clustering process and enhances the recognition accuracy of adjacent trees, thereby effectively addressing the under-segmentation and over-segmentation of trees with overlapping crowns. We selected ForAINet, TreeLearn, TD3D, and other representative models as baselines to conduct comparative experiments. The results show that DBE-Net exhibited superior segmentation performance, achieving 84.9% F1-score, 90.5% precision, 81.0% recall, and 73.5% coverage. In terms of predicting candidate results, the bounding box branch is 3.2 times faster than the offset vector branch. Moreover, extensive experiments and visualizations further exhibit the robustness and adaptability of DBE-Net, whose F1-score variation is within 3% under different hyperparameter settings. This study demonstrates that DBE-Net can achieve accurate and efficient individual tree segmentation, thereby providing a solid foundation for subsequent forest surveys. The code can be found at https://github.com/liangwenge740/DBE-Net.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: PMTB-VSRnet: A video super-resolution network with radiometric consistency guidance for Antarctic passive microwave brightness temperature
abstract: Monitoring Antarctic surface melt using satellite-based Earth observation relies heavily on passive microwave data for their all-weather capability; however, their coarse spatial resolution limits the detection of fine-scale melt features. To address this limitation, we propose PMTB-VSRnet, a video super-resolution network with radiometric consistency guidance for Antarctic passive microwave data. In PMTB-VSRnet, neighboring frames are first aligned using Pyramid, Cascading and Deformable (PCD) alignment, while low-frequency Normalized Cross-Correlation (NCC)-guided fusion enhances radiometric feature consistency and suppresses unreliable observations. The aligned features are then propagated bidirectionally to exploit temporal information and reconstruct fine-scale brightness temperature structures. Finally, a radiometric high-frequency constraint is introduced to enhance reconstruction accuracy. Extensive experiments on AMSR2 multi-channel data show that PMTB-VSRnet outperforms all compared methods, improving PSNR over the average performance of the competing methods by 1.57, 2.30, 2.47, and 2.81 dB for the 36.5 H, 36.5 V, 18.7 H, and 18.7 V channels, respectively, under a 4 × super-resolution setting. Additional experiments across diverse Antarctic terrains, seasons, and continent-scale regions further demonstrate the robustness and scalability of the proposed framework. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/jingli1999/PMTB-VSRnet . • Combining PCD alignment and NCC-guided fusion to enhance local radiometric feature consistency. • Integrating local temporal modeling and bidirectional global propagation to improve temporal aggregation and reconstruction robustness. • Introducing a radiometric high-frequency constraint to enhance reconstruction accuracy. • Achieving consistent improvements across regions, seasons, and channels, with scalability to continent-scale observations.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: STARS: Shared-specific Translation and Alignment for missing-modality Remote Sensing Semantic Segmentation
abstract: Multimodal remote sensing technology significantly enhances the understanding of surface semantics by integrating heterogeneous data such as optical images, Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), and Digital Surface Models (DSM). However, in practical applications, the missing of modality data (e.g., optical or DSM) is a common and severe challenge, which leads to performance decline in traditional multimodal fusion models. Existing methods for addressing missing modalities still face limitations, including feature collapse and overly generalized recovered features. To address these issues, we propose STARS ( S hared-specific T ranslation and A lignment for missing-modality R emote S ensing), a robust semantic segmentation framework for incomplete multimodal inputs. STARS is built on two key designs. First, we introduce an asymmetric alignment mechanism with bidirectional translation and stop-gradient, which effectively prevents feature collapse and reduces sensitivity to hyperparameters. Second, we propose a Pixel-level Semantic sampling Alignment (PSA) strategy that combines class-balanced pixel sampling with cross-modality semantic alignment loss, to mitigate alignment failures caused by severe class imbalance and improve minority-class recognition. Experiments on EarthMiss, WHU-OPT-SAR, and ISPRS Potsdam demonstrate that STARS consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods under missing-modality settings. In particular, STARS achieves 33.04 m I o U (＋9.60 vs. Baseline-SAR) on EarthMiss (SAR-only test), and reaches 34.07 m I o U (＋5.95 vs. Baseline-SAR) on WHU-OPT-SAR under the same missing-modality evaluation. Additional analyses further verify that STARS establishes reliable cross-modality semantic correspondence while decoupling shared semantics from modality-specific cues, enabling accurate and stable remote sensing semantic segmentation with incomplete multimodal data. The code is released in https://github.com/CVEO/STARS .
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Intensified snowmelt on Karakoram glaciers Revealed by Sentinel-1 Backscatter-Derived wet snow dynamics
abstract: Glacier surface melting critically drives glacier mass balance in the Karakoram, yet how wet snow evolves seasonally, altitudinally, and across glacier types remains poorly constrained, as optical observations are often limited by persistent cloud cover and complex topography. We developed a Sentinel-1 Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) time-series approach, optimized for complex high-mountain terrain to identify wet snow dynamics across Karakoram glaciers from 2017 to 2023. The results reveal a clear seasonal cycle, with wet snow generally peaking in July and occurring predominantly around 5,500 m a.s.l. The spatial evolution of wet snow shows a pronounced southwest–northeast melt gradient, closely linked to the seasonal migration of the 0 °C isotherm (R 2 > 0.95). Furthermore, glacier morphology significantly modulates these patterns: avalanche-fed Turkestan-type glaciers show earlier wet snow peaks and enhanced wet snow concentration in their middle-to-lower reaches, suggesting an important role of gravitational mass redistribution in altering local melt timing and surface hydrology. In addition, the upward migration of both wet snow boundaries over the study period indicates intensified surface melting. This trend provides a new surface-process perspective for understanding the recently reported transition or possible end of the Karakoram Anomaly. Our findings demonstrate the value of regionally adapted Sentinel-1 SAR observations for constraining heterogeneous glacier melt processes and high-mountain water-resource changes under a warming climate.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Machine-learning framework for cross-scale estimation of desert vegetation aboveground biomass and driver analysis in the Junggar Basin using UAV classification and satellite data fusion
abstract: Long-term monitoring of aboveground biomass (AGB) is essential for assessing ecosystem productivity and carbon storage. However, sparse vegetation and complex bare-soil backgrounds in desert regions introduce significant uncertainties in AGB inversion and driver analysis. In this study, field plots, UAVs, and satellite data were integrated to develop high-accuracy AGB inversion models for desert ecosystems using vegetation classification, data fusion, and multi-model comparison. Theil–Sen slope estimation, Mann–Kendall tests, and SHAP analysis were applied to characterize AGB dynamics and identify the driving mechanisms. The results show that object-based classification combined with deep learning (SegFormer) achieved the highest accuracy (OA = 94%). Vegetation-class-based variables improved UAV-scale AGB estimation. At the satellite-scale, spectral features generated by Landsat–MODIS fusion, combined with environmental variables, yielded the best performance with the Boruta–XGBoost model (R 2 = 0.84 RMSE = 733.32 kg ha⁻ 1 , CCC = 0.91). From 2000 to 2024, AGB exhibited an increasing trend, with 57.6% of the area increasing mainly in low-elevation temperate desert regions, while 37.9% decreased primarily in high-elevation temperate desert steppe regions. Temperature and precipitation were the dominant drivers of AGB variation, with notable interaction effects involving temperature-precipitation and potential evapotranspiration-precipitation. When precipitation exceeded 82 mm, the effects of temperature and potential evapotranspiration on AGB were enhanced and became positive influences. This study provides methodological support for AGB modeling and informs desertification management in arid regions.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: A flexible framework for wheat yield estimation from ground-based RGB imagery: evaluating explicit and implicit feature representations
abstract: Wheat is a major global staple, and accurate yield estimation is critical for agricultural management and food security. While satellite and UAV-based approaches are widely used, they are costly and operationally complex, making ground-based RGB imagery an attractive low-cost alternative. However, existing image-based methods are often limited by the restricted representational power of handcrafted features or the limited interpretability of end-to-end deep learning models. This study therefore develops a ground-based RGB framework to systematically evaluate the roles of explicit handcrafted features and deep implicit features in wheat yield estimation. Explicit features describe spike morphology and canopy color using spatial geometry, wavelet-based texture, and visible vegetation indices, while implicit features are extracted from a VGG-based segmentation encoder. Four regression models (RF, SVM, KNN, and XGBoost) were tested. The results show that both feature types are informative, but implicit features provide superior predictive performance. In particular, XGBoost with implicit features achieved the highest accuracy (R 2 = 0.85, RMSE = 1015.77 kg·ha⁻ 1 , rRMSE = 12.9%), outperforming models based only on explicit features and matching the performance of combined feature sets. Overall, the proposed approach clarifies the relative roles of different feature representations and provides a flexible and practical solution for low-cost, scalable crop yield assessment based on ground-based RGB imagery.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Phenology-driven hierarchical framework for grass species classification in coastal wetlands based on Sentinel-1/2 imagery: A case study of the Jiangsu Coast, Eastern China
abstract: Coastal wetlands are among the most vulnerable and valuable ecosystems, yet they are undergoing persistent changes in land surface conditions and vegetation composition driven by climate change and intensive human activities. Accurate mapping of grass species distribution is essential for the control of invasive plants, biodiversity conservation, and vegetation carbon accounting, yet the task remains challenging due to tidal inundation, frequent cloud cover, and the high spectral similarity among coastal grass species. This study developed a hierarchical classification framework to mitigate these limitations. The intertidal zone was first delineated from multi-temporal Sentinel-2 observations by exploiting temporal differences in water coverage, which compensated for the omission of grass species affected by tidal fluctuations that conventional classification methods have overlooked. Subsequently, two phenology-based vegetation features derived from monthly NDVI were constructed to improve the discrimination of spectrally similar species in the supratidal zone and were incorporated into a random forest classifier. The proposed framework achieved an overall accuracy (OA) of 0.94, notably higher than the OA of 0.85 from the traditional single-level classification, and effectively reduced misclassifications among species with overlapping spectral signatures. The hierarchical framework increased the total detected grassland area by approximately 13657.91 ha, with Spartina alterniflora contributing the majority of the improvement due to enhanced detection in the intertidal zone. In 2023, Jiangsu coastal zones supported 177,464.8 ha of grassland, with Spartina alterniflora occupying 52490.8 ha and showing substantial dominance along the Yancheng coasts. The successful detection of large areas of S. alterniflora that were omitted by a single-level model confirmed the importance of addressing tidal interference and demonstrated the benefits of incorporating phenological differences among grass species into the classification process. These findings demonstrate that the hierarchical strategy provides a more reliable solution to large-scale grass species mapping in dynamic coastal environments and offers practical support for invasive species management and ecosystem protection.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: NASA’s EMIT hyperspectral observations of phytoplankton ecology in estuarine waters
abstract: NASA’s EMIT hyperspectral spectrometer provides high spectral (∼7.4 nm) and spatial (60 m) resolution, capabilities that have not been routinely applied to water quality monitoring in shallow aquatic systems, where the bio-optical properties are highly complex. In this study, we developed Hyper-MoE-VAE, a deep-learning inversion framework integrating a mixture-of-experts architecture with variational autoencoders for globally applicable hyperspectral water-quality retrievals. The model accommodates diverse water types and addresses one-to-many inversions to retrieve chlorophyll- a (Chl a ) and phytoplankton absorption coefficient ( a phy ) from hyperspectral remote sensing reflectance ( R rs ). Hyper-MoE-VAE was trained on a global bio-optical dataset and applied to EMIT imagery over Lake Pontchartrain. Same-day field matchups acquired on 14 April 2025 provide the first validation of EMIT-derived Chl a (MAPE = 7.66 %; MAE = 1.13 in log 10 space, unitless) and a phy across all EMIT bands, with representative performance (NRMSE = 0.09–0.11 m −1 ; ε = 29–36 %), revealing a muted Chl a response under highly turbid freshwater conditions and a clear shift toward chlorophyte dominance following fresh inputs. In addition, PACE-OCI, also hyperspectral with lower spatial resolution, was compared with EMIT for Chl a retrievals. Both sensors show comparable spatial patterns despite differences in spectral and spatial resolution, supporting the Hyper-MoE-VAE’s cross-mission applicability. These findings demonstrate EMIT’s strong potential for characterizing phytoplankton dynamics, both in abundance and community composition, and for monitoring harmful algal blooms (HABs) in aquatic systems.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Quantifying the influence of DEM elevation errors on regional gravity forward modeling through DEM correction and fusion
abstract: High-precision characterization of the Earth’s gravity field is essential for geological structure analysis, volcanic activity monitoring, and resource exploration. As direct measurement of a high-resolution global gravity field remains impractical, forward modeling based on Digital Elevation Models (DEMs) is a key method for recovering its high-frequency components and is essential for regional high-resolution gravity field modeling. However, the accuracy of this method is severely limited by substantial errors in existing global DEMs, particularly those induced by vegetation cover. Currently, a systematic research quantifying the full pathway from DEM error correction to its impact on gravity field accuracy is lacking. To address this gap, this study proposes an integrated framework for correcting DEM errors and evaluating their propagation in gravity field modeling. Specifically, we develop a hybrid Random Forest-Inverse Distance Weighting (RF-IDW) method to fuse multi-source remote sensing data and generate a regionally optimized, high-precision DEM. The proposed framework is evaluated in the Wudalianchi volcanic region using in-situ gravity observations. Comparative forward modeling based on the original TanDEM-X DEM and the optimized DEM demonstrates a 42.35% improvement in elevation accuracy, resulting in a 17.89% increase in the accuracy of the modeled terrain gravity field. Furthermore, DEM elevation errors exhibit a moderately strong correlation with gravity anomaly error (R = 0.648), accounting for approximately 42.0% of their variance. These findings provide both a quantitative assessment of elevation errors in gravity field modeling and a transferable methodological framework for enhancing the accuracy of DEM-based gravity field solutions in diverse topographic and vegetation environments.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Spatially explicit predictions of land cover change using the Density-Functional Fluctuation Theory (DFFT) approach
abstract: Many existing models for predicting land cover change (LCC) rely on extensive spatial drivers and complex calibration. This study introduces Density-Functional Fluctuation Theory (DFFT) as an alternative, low-data and computationally efficient approach for spatially explicit LCC prediction. DFFT operates on binary landscapes consisting of focal and background cells and represents a site as a grid of blocks, each described by the proportion of focal cells it contains. From a single observed land-cover snapshot, the method infers a block-level density functional that encodes the statistical structure of local spatial configurations. Future density-grid patterns are generated using a stochastic Monte Carlo procedure that updates block densities toward configurations consistent with this functional and subject to a prescribed future global density. Predictions for multi-categorical LCC are obtained using a sequential binary procedure applied to individual land-cover categories. The approach does not rely on explicit transition rules, suitability surfaces, or spatial covariates. The method was tested on four National Land Cover Database (NLCD) sites between 2001 and 2019, covering urban expansion, two types of agricultural change, and wetland dynamics. Across multiple block sizes, predicted density grids show strong agreement with observed data, with mean absolute errors ranging from 0.012 to 0.101. Compared with commonly used approaches such as CA-Markov, DFFT is highly parsimonious and scalable, making it particularly suitable for large domains, data-scarce settings, and scenario-based forecasting.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Global patterns and driving mechanisms of vegetation sensitivity to compound atmospheric drought and heat events over 1982–2020
abstract: The increasing occurrence of compound atmospheric drought and heat events (CDHEs) has become a major risk to terrestrial ecosystems with global climate change. However, the global pattern of vegetation sensitivity to CDHEs (Scdh) and the key factors driving this sensitivity remain obscured. Accordingly, this study developed a comprehensive sensitivity index to quantify spatiotemporal changes in global vegetation Scdh, leveraging multi-source global observational datasets over 1982–2020. Results reveal that vegetation in the mid-to-high latitudes of the Northern Hemisphere typically exhibits low Scdh. Sensitivity also varies across vegetation types: forests show the lowest sensitivity, while crops are the most sensitive. Over the last four decades, the global average Scdh of vegetation greenness has remarkably increased (P < 0.001), with 63.6 % of ecosystems experiencing heightened sensitivity. Temperature emerges as the primary environmental factor affecting Scdh. The influence of temperature on Scdh shifts from positive to negative at a critical threshold of 12.9 °C, and it acts as the dominant factor in 34.5 % of terrestrial ecosystems. This study offers a new approach for quantifying vegetation Scdh, clarifies the spatiotemporal dynamics of Scdh and its key drivers and enhances our understanding of how ecosystems respond to CDHEs.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: The role of atmospheric correction errors in the underestimation of satellite-derived chlorophyll-a concentration in the Southern Ocean
abstract: Previous studies have consistently reported underestimation of satellite-derived chlorophyll- a concentration (CHL) in the Southern Ocean (SO). While this bias is often attributed to the region’s unique bio-optical properties, the potential contribution of atmospheric correction errors has been comparatively underexplored. This study evaluated the performance of three mainstream CHL retrieval algorithms (OC2, OC3, OCI) in high-latitude waters of the SO, mainly poleward of 63°S, using three types of remote-sensing reflectance ( R rs ) data: in-situ R rs , NASA-distributed standard VIIRS R rs , and VIIRS R rs obtained from a recently developed Cross-Satellite Atmospheric Correction (CSAC) algorithm. Our results show that when in-situ R rs were used as inputs, the mean absolute percent difference (MAPD) values between measured and estimated CHL by OC2, OC3, and OCI were 24.4%, 23.0%, and 30.2%, respectively. Using NASA-distributed VIIRS R rs increased the MAPD values to 41.7%, 50.4%, and 55.4%, respectively. In contrast, when CSAC-derived R rs were used, the MAPD values reduced to 25.4%, 22.5%, and 21.4%, respectively. This is because CSAC-derived R rs showed much stronger agreement with in-situ R rs than NASA-distributed R rs , with MAPD values reduced by approximately 50% across the visible bands. These results suggest that imperfect atmospheric correction plays a big role in the systematic underestimation of CHL in the SO from ocean color remote sensing. Additionally, CSAC was able to recover CHL retrievals under challenging observation conditions, such as moderate sunglint and straylight, which were previously masked in the standard VIIRS product, thereby substantially improving data coverage. Therefore, we anticipate that incorporating CSAC into the production of ocean color products will yield more accurate, better spatially covered products in this critical region.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: OpenPineDet: An open-set detection framework for the detection of dead pine wood in forests
abstract: Early and accurate detection of dead pine wood (DPW) is essential to mitigate the spread of pine wilt disease (PWD), a destructive affliction of pine forests. Deep learning-based object detection methods have been widely employed for DPW detection. However, these approaches typically assume that both the training and test datasets contain only instances from a single, known class (i.e., DPW). This closed-set assumption often results in unknown targets in the test data being misclassified as DPW. To address this limitation, we collected high-resolution drone imagery of pine forests, resulting in a dataset of 7,733 images (the GSD ranged from 10.4 to 15.5 cm/pixel for flight altitudes between 800 and 1200 m) comprising 29,575 samples of DPW and 7,334 samples of unknown categories. We then introduced an open-set object detection framework, OpenPineDet (OPDet), designed to accurately identify DPW while recognizing other similar objects (e.g., bare soil and houses) as unknown categories. OPDet integrates two novel modules: (1) a Bottleneck Channel Attention Network (BNCA) that leverages the Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) mechanism to enhance the model’s focus on DPW targets; and (2) a Dual Contrastive Learning (DCL) module, which combines Instance-Level Contrastive Learning (ICL) with Focal Loss (FL) to improve detection accuracy of hard-to-classify DPW instances. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that OPDet outperforms existing methods, achieving an Average Precision (AP K ) of 92.67 % and a Recall (R K ) of 97.24 %, while reducing Wilderness Impact (WI) and Absolute Open-Set Error (AOSE) to 1.80 and 242, respectively. Additionally, the proposed model demonstrates stable performance across different scenarios (such as simple scenes with only pine trees and complex scenes with other unknown categories), and exhibits better regional generalization capabilities. These results indicate that OPDet effectively reduces the misclassification of unknown targets as DPW, highlighting its effectiveness for open-set detection methodologies in forest management applications.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Physically consistent multitemporal dual-domain learning for dual-polarization SAR despeckling
abstract: Speckle contamination strongly affects the interpretability and practical application of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery. For real dual-polarization SAR data, despeckling is particularly difficult because clean supervision is unavailable and temporal variations between acquisitions complicate the characterization of speckle behavior. Existing unsupervised deep models have shown promise, but many of them still underuse the complementary information contained in neighboring temporal observations and insufficiently exploit the physical cues associated with polarimetric scattering, which may result in structural degradation and distortion of scattering characteristics. To address these limitations, we develop CD 2 P-Net, a collaborative dual-domain progressive network for real dual-polarization SAR despeckling. The method is established within a physically guided multitemporal unsupervised learning framework, where spatial, spectral, and temporal relationships are progressively modeled to make better use of temporal coherence and speckle variability across adjacent acquisitions. In addition, covariance-derived statistics and polarimetric decomposition descriptors are introduced to improve the physical reliability of the learned features. Experiments on real Sentinel-1 dual-polarization time-series data show that the proposed method achieves superior despeckling performance compared with representative competing approaches, while better preserving spatial structures, polarimetric characteristics, and semantic consistency.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Advancing green tide monitoring: a spatiotemporal analysis in the Southern Yellow Sea using a novel deep learning and remote sensing fusion approach
abstract: Green tides caused by the macroalga Ulva prolifera are recurrent marine disasters in the Southern Yellow Sea (SYS), China. Accurate monitoring and spatiotemporal characterization are essential for effective mitigation. However, conventional remote sensing methods struggle to detect fine filamentous structures, and prevailing deep learning models suffer from spatial detail loss and scene-dependent variability that undermines multi-temporal consistency. To address these challenges, we propose UPS-Net-LDU, an improved semantic segmentation model that integrates a Hybrid Attention Gate (HAG) and an Edge-Enhanced Strip (EES) module into the U-Net architecture. Using 170 GF-1 WFV images from 2018 to 2025, we construct a multi-year distribution dataset covering the high-incidence period (May–August) of U. prolifera in the SYS. Quantitative validation shows that UPS-Net-LDU achieves an IoU of 73.44%, Precision of 82.93%, Recall of 86.52%, and an F1-score of 84.68%, outperforming several mainstream benchmarks. Ablation experiments confirm the individual contributions of the HAG and EES modules. Spatiotemporal evolution analysis reveals a persistent spatial pattern: source area in the Subei Shoal → northeastward transport corridor → convergence zone in the southeastern Shandong Peninsula, with notable interannual variability including an alternating pattern of high- and low-intensity years between consecutive years. Integrated analysis with sea surface temperature (SST) data indicates that SST warming within 15–24 °C during May–June facilitates algal expansion, whereas persistently high temperatures (>24 °C) during July–August suppress growth and promote decay, clarifying a dual-phase regulatory mechanism. This study offers a robust methodological tool for precise monitoring and delivers critical insights into the dual-phase thermal regulation of green tides, supporting early warning and management in the region.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Multi-scale time-series framework for piping-induced levee failure using a piping potential index
abstract: River levee failures can occur from not only overtopping but also piping, a progressive internal erosion mechanism driven by sustained hydraulic gradients and accumulated moisture. This study proposes a time-series framework integrating river level, groundwater level, rainfall, and Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) root-zone soil moisture to investigate six piping-induced levee failures in South Korea since 2020. The Piping Potential Index (PPI) is defined as the sum of the standardized indicators that represent the driving head difference (D), accumulated rainfall (R), time-averaged soil moisture (SM), and incremental groundwater rise (GW). Hydro-environmental data were reconstructed at hourly resolution over a −14 to +1 day event window, and 27 accumulation-window combinations were evaluated using lead time, duration, and prominence metrics. Short-term rainfall and soil moisture windows (24 h) produced stronger and earlier anomaly peaks, whereas longer rainfall windows (72 h) prolonged the persistence of critical conditions. A configuration integrating short-term rainfall and soil moisture with medium-term groundwater accumulation demonstrated a balanced trade-off between early warning performance and signal strength, highlighting the multi-scale nature of piping-related levee instability.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Heterogeneous vegetation resilience trajectories beneath greening during open-pit mine reclamation
abstract: Satellite-observed vegetation greening is regarded as direct evidence of reclamation in open-pit mines. However, improvements in vegetation greenness do not necessarily indicate ecosystem resilience recovery. Identifying hidden areas of fragile resilience beneath apparent greening remains a critical challenge. In mining areas, extracting vegetation disturbance signals required for resilience assessment is difficult, because varying reclamation cycles and high spatial heterogeneity often lead to spectral mixing in existing decomposition methods. Therefore, we proposed VegDecouple, a decoupling method that adaptively separates background vegetation dynamics from short-term disturbances in mining areas. Using Landsat NDVI data (1990–2025) from a typical open-pit coal mine on the Loess Plateau, we characterized the heterogeneous trajectories of the variance-based resilience proxy beneath greening, identified three reclamation patterns, and quantified the effects of key drivers. The results showed that (1) VegDecouple effectively separated disturbance and steady-state components from non-stationary vegetation signals in mining areas. Compared with existing methods, it delivered the best spectral decoupling performance, achieving the highest energy capture and the lowest leakage. (2) Vegetation greenness and the resilience proxy exhibited pronounced temporal asynchrony and spatial mismatch. Three reclamation modes were identified within greening areas, revealing distinct inferred ecological recovery pathways. (3) Background vegetation state, reclamation age, and mean growing-season temperature showed the largest cumulative SHAP contributions, exceeding 75 % across the three reclamation modes. Moreover, SHAP dependence plots revealed nonlinear associations between key drivers and the resilience proxy. Beyond the case study, VegDecouple performed robustly across mining areas under contrasting climatic conditions. These findings provide a transferable framework for identifying potential degradation risks and supporting differentiated management in reclaimed mining landscapes.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Enabling seamless spatiotemporal flood monitoring via bridging observational gaps with a case study on the 2024 Bangladesh flood
abstract: Accurate and timely flood monitoring is critical for effective disaster management. Remote sensing observations offer large scale monitoring; however, they frequently suffer from observational gaps caused by cloud cover, limited swaths, and extended revisit cycles, severely hindering continuous tracking. To overcome these physical barriers, this study proposes an enhanced Knowledge-Driven Flood Intelligent Monitoring framework (KDFIMv2). Rather than relying on isolated imagery, KDFIMv2 proposes a synergistic architecture that integrates optical and SAR observations to maximize single day inundation extraction, employs topographic routing constraints for spatiotemporal gap filling, and incorporates dynamic water surface elevation calculations for three-dimensional parameter retrieval. The framework was evaluated using the 2024 Bangladesh flood. Quantitatively, KDFIMv2 achieves high depth estimation precision with prediction errors predominantly within 0.1 m. Crucially, benchmarking experiments assessing the spatial distributions of flood inundation demonstrate that KDFIMv2 maintains high classification performance across rising, peak, and recession stages, achieving a mean Overall Accuracy and F1 metric exceeding 0.9. While baseline methods exhibit severe stability fluctuations under observational gaps, spatiotemporal analysis reveals that KDFIMv2 achieves superior temporal consistency, with the proportion of stable pixels exceeding 70 %. The results highlight the potential of KDFIMv2 for near-real-time flood monitoring and disaster response, offering a scalable and interpretable solution for flood risk assessment and management.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: A global 500 m dataset of tree crown morphology to advance vegetation modeling and management
abstract: Tree crown architecture varies widely across the globe and strongly influences ecosystem functioning, biodiversity, the carbon cycle, and land-atmosphere interactions. However, its global variability and spatial patterns remain poorly quantified due to sparse field and LiDAR measurements, limiting large-scale ecological and modelling applications. Here, we present a globally consistent 500 m tree crown structure dataset, including crown depth (CD), crown width (CW), and aspect ratio (AR, defined as CD/CW) across eight plant functional types (PFTs). The dataset was generated using an allometric upscaling framework that links more than 340,000 field observations with satellite-derived canopy height and bioclimatic predictors. Moving beyond classic power-law allometry, this approach captures transferable crown structure–height relationships via Random Forest models, enabling wall-to-wall global mapping. It outperforms traditional allometric equations, increasing R2 from 0.26 to 0.84 and reducing RMSE from 2.43 m to 1.14 m for temperate PFTs. The resulting map reveals distinct PFT-specific patterns, with large crowns in tropical rainforests, deep narrow crowns in boreal PFTs (mean AR = 1.8±0.7), and wide shallow crowns in temperate regions (mean AR = 0.95±0.4). We also found that AR remains relatively invariant with height, suggesting its potential as a robust structural parameter for modeling. This dataset provides a novel gridded benchmark for ecological studies, remote-sensing retrieval applications, and Earth system models to advance vegetation dynamics and the carbon cycle.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: GROMS: GPS-free real-time UAV orthophoto mapping via terrain constraint monocular SLAM
abstract: To improve the coverage of individual Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) images and enable comprehensive environmental perception, it is essential to generate wide-field, large-scale, and metrically accurate orthophotos. However, traditional methods depend heavily on the Global Positioning System (GPS), exhibit high computational complexity, and are susceptible to drift and distortion in GPS-free environments. To overcome these challenges, we propose GROMS, a GPS-free, map-prior-assisted (DEM and satellite imagery) real-time UAV orthophoto mapping system. GROMS utilizes georeferenced satellite imagery and digital elevation model (DEM) solely as map priors to derive virtual control points (VCPs) and constrain monocular SLAM, without relying on any GNSS or IMU measurements. Specifically, we design an efficient keyframe selection and dynamic block matching module to enable robust alignment between UAV and satellite images. We further introduce a terrain-constrained monocular SLAM framework incorporating VCPs, enabling drift-free and high-precision pose estimation in the absence of GPS/IMU. Finally, a hybrid ortho-rectification and incremental multi-band blending strategy is proposed for seamless, real-time orthophoto generation. Extensive experiments in both typical and challenging scenarios validate the robustness, accuracy, efficiency, and visual fidelity of GROMS. The system achieves visual quality comparable to commercial software, with efficiency improvements of up to 7.6× . Under GPS-free conditions, GROMS attains mean absolute errors of 1.11 m and 0.64 m in the x- and y-directions, respectively, while sustaining stable end-to-end throughput with bounded latency (p99 < 2.8 s) during continuous online orthophoto generation. Demonstration videos of GROMS and the associated datasets are available at https://github.com/YFS90/Real-time-orthophoto .
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: MSRS-SLAM: A real-time multi-UAV dense mapping system for efficient low-altitude remote sensing
abstract: UAV remote sensing demands efficient, large-scale mapping for critical applications such as emergency response and resource surveying. However, traditional single-agent SLAM is inherently constrained by limited flight endurance, rendering the transition to multi-UAV collaborative frameworks imperative. We propose MSRS-SLAM, a novel real-time dense reconstruction framework for UAV swarms. The pipeline utilizes visual odometry for pose estimation, followed by deep multi-view depth estimation to generate local dense maps. To resolve multi-agent consistency challenges, we introduce a robust two-stage map fusion strategy initialized via GPS or visual features. The first stage achieves initial alignment through 3D-3D feature matching by leveraging multi-frame co-visibility, RANSAC, and the Umeyama algorithm. The second stage employs dense point cloud registration for precise relative pose estimation. Global consistency is ensured by eliminating accumulated errors through intra-agent and inter-agent loop closure detection coupled with global Pose Graph Optimization. Furthermore, an improved SAM3 model based on text prompts is integrated into the pipeline, enabling multi-UAV cooperative semantic dense reconstruction. By utilizing image datasets collected from diverse environments, the proposed method generates high-quality dense point clouds online through multi-UAV collaboration. The effectiveness of this approach is rigorously evaluated through comprehensive comparisons with current mainstream three-dimensional reconstruction algorithms. Experimental results demonstrate that MSRS-SLAM significantly enhances processing efficiency in large-scale scenarios by leveraging the parallel operation of multiple UAVs. Furthermore, through collaborative map fusion, the system achieves reconstruction accuracy comparable to that of offline algorithms, thereby attaining an optimal balance between computational efficiency and reconstruction precision.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: MS-AFNet: A multi-scale adaptive fusion network with high-resolution feature enhancement for tiny object detection in UAV imagery
abstract: Detecting tiny objects in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery remains a formidable challenge due to the diminutive pixel footprint of targets, severe background clutter, and the progressive degradation of spatial fidelity during multi-stage downsampling. This paper proposes MS-AFNet, an advanced deep learning architecture specifically optimized for robust tiny object detection in complex UAV scenarios. To counteract information loss in deep layers, we introduce a Multi-Scale High-Resolution Feature Enhancement (MS_HRFE) module at the P2 level, which effectively captures fine-grained morphological details through parallel multi-scale context branches and a dual-attention mechanism. Furthermore, an Adaptive Spatial Feature Fusion (ASC_FSF) mechanism is integrated to dynamically recalibrate spatial weights during cross-scale feature interactions, thereby suppressing background noise and enhancing adaptability to significant scale variations. Additionally, the RTAS_C3k2 module is designed to construct a parameter-efficient backbone, leveraging spatially sensitive guidance and partial texture enhancement to preserve localization accuracy. Experimental evaluations on the VisDrone2019-DET dataset demonstrate that MS-AFNet significantly outperforms state-of-the-art models. Specifically, evaluated on the rigorous test-dev set, MS-AFNet achieves an mAP 50 of 30.0%, exhibiting an absolute improvement of 7.7% over the YOLO11n baseline. Notably, the proposed model maintains a compact architecture with only 2.4M parameters, achieving an optimal trade-off between detection precision and computational efficiency in resource-constrained environments. This research provides a robust, high-precision detection solution for intelligent urban traffic management and large-scale UAV surveillance.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: ASA-DETR: Adaptive sparse attention enhanced RT-DETR for remote sensing landslide detection with multi-scale frequency-aware feature learning
abstract: Accurate landslide detection from remote sensing imagery is essential for geological hazard monitoring. However, existing methods suffer from insufficient feature extraction for complex geological textures, limited multi-scale fusion effectiveness, and poor small-target detection performance. This paper proposes ASA-DETR, a novel RT-DETR-based landslide detection algorithm that addresses these challenges through an improved lightweight backbone, a joint spatial-frequency domain feature learning module, and an adaptive multi-scale attention fusion mechanism. We also construct the RSLD-2K dataset containing 2,299 images with 6,545 landslide annotations from Google Earth, Planet Labs, and Sentinel-2. Experiments on RSLD-2K demonstrate that ASA-DETR achieves 73.2 % mAP@0.5 and 52.5 % mAP@0.5:0.95, improving 3.7 and 2.2 percentage points over baseline RT-DETR, respectively, while reducing parameters by 7.6 %. Cross-domain experiments on the DOTAv2 dataset yield 55.1 % mAP@0.5, suggesting a certain degree of transferability to broader remote sensing detection scenarios.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: An adaptive hybrid algorithm for retrieving particulate organic carbon in complex coastal waters
abstract: The retrieval of particulate organic carbon (POC) from optical properties in coastal waters remains a significant challenge because of profound spatiotemporal heterogeneity in water composition. Here, we propose an adaptive hybrid algorithm for POC retrieval (AHA-POC). This algorithm integrates optical water cluster classification with cluster specific model optimization to deliver improved POC estimates in optically complex environments, as demonstrated for the coastal waters of Guangdong and eastern Hainan Island. The algorithm first defines bio-optical water clusters using K-means clustering based on inherent optical properties (IOPs) and derived composite features. This classification separated samples into optically distinct clusters characterized by systematic differences in particle composition, absorption and scattering properties, and bio-optical relationships, which reduce the influence of variability in aquatic particulate matter composition on subsequent POC retrieval algorithms. After cluster definition, cluster specific sensitive features and retrieval models were selected to account for variable POC–IOPs relationships across optical regimes. To avoid station level data leakage, model performance was evaluated using leave-one-station-out cross-validation (LOSO-CV), in which all samples from the same station were held out together during validation. The AHA-POC achieved stable retrieval performance (R 2 = 0.79, RMSE = 0.071 mg /L, MAPE = 32.38 %, Bias = -0.78 %), showing improved accuracy relative to both univariate retrieval models and threshold-based water classification schemes in optically complex water environments. The algorithm was further applied to high resolution in situ IOPs profiles to reconstruct POC sections at 1 m vertical resolution, revealing fine scale vertical heterogeneity associated with riverine plume influence and near bottom particle resuspension. These results demonstrate the potential of cluster specific optical modeling for improving regional POC estimation in optically complex coastal waters and for supporting high resolution assessments of coastal carbon variability.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: A hierarchical framework employing voting mechanism for large-scale ALB and MBES point cloud registration
abstract: Registration is essential for fusing airborne LiDAR bathymetry (ALB) and multibeam echo sounder (MBES) data. However, existing studies are limited, often overlooking the unique characteristics and heterogeneity of bathymetric point clouds, which complicates the establishment of accurate correspondences. This study thoroughly analyzes the key challenges in ALB and MBES point cloud registration and proposes a hierarchical framework based on a voting mechanism. The framework transforms coarse registration into a hierarchical matching process, progressing from global to local compatibility graphs. It employs weak and strong voting mechanisms to progressively refine inlier selection from relaxed to strict criteria. An ICP algorithm incorporating geometric consistency is then applied to achieve fine registration. The strong voting mechanism enhances the weak voting mechanism by integrating local information. These hierarchical and voting strategies effectively reduce graph sensitivity, balancing accuracy and efficiency. Additionally, the study adapts initial correspondence extraction based on terrain complexity and introduces adaptive inlier selection through Gaussian fitting of fusion scores, calculated using the coefficient of variation. This study validates the proposed method using two field datasets from the South China Sea, providing a comprehensive analysis of the key steps in the algorithm. The proposed method outperforms Comparison Methods 1 and 2, reducing overall error (OE) by 221.2% and 206.4% on Data I, and 223.1% and 202.6% on Data II. Furthermore, experiments demonstrate the method’s robustness in complex noisy environments.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: AFDINet: Adaptive frequency disentanglement and interaction in hybrid Mamba–CNN for optical-SAR land cover classification
abstract: The synergistic integration of optical and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery enables robust Earth observation by overcoming the limitations of single-sensor modalities, such as atmospheric occlusion and spectral deficiency. However, prevailing fusion paradigms typically treat multi-modal integration as a homogeneous spatial operation, neglecting the distinct physical properties inherent in different frequency domains. This oversight often results in the loss of high-frequency (HF) details, leading to fragmented boundaries in fine-grained land cover classification (LCC). To bridge this gap, this study introduces the Adaptive Frequency Disentanglement and Interaction Network (AFDINet), a hybrid architecture fusing CNN and Mamba. We devise a Learnable Frequency Disentanglement (LFD) module that reformulates wavelet decomposition as a data-driven process, adaptively separating structural consensus from modality-specific textures. Subsequently, a High–Low Frequency Fusion (HLF 3 ) module implements a role-aware interaction strategy, calibrating low-frequency (LF) geometry while enhancing HF details. Extensive empirical evaluations on the Xi’an, YYX-OPT-SAR, and WHU-OPT-SAR datasets demonstrate that AFDINet achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance in terms of OA, mIoU, and Kappa, while exhibiting exceptional resilience to cloud interference.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Bridging the visual-computational gap: transforming UAV reality meshes into volumetric geological models via explicit-implicit integration
abstract: Targeting complex geological environments characterized by high-steep cliffs, such as Danxia landforms, traditional geological modeling often relies on sparse subsurface detection data and low-precision Digital Elevation Models (DEM), making it difficult to accurately depict the complete 3D morphology of both the surface and the subsurface. To overcome this limitation, this paper introduces large-area, high-precision UAV Oblique Photogrammetry (OSGB) remote sensing data and proposes an OSGB-enhanced explicit–implicit integrated modeling framework. This method aims to bridge the “Visual-Computational” gap, where raw OSGB data possesses excellent visual fidelity but essentially consists of unstructured, non-manifold surface meshes, posing severe topological challenges for direct Boolean operations and volumetric calculations. Rather than merely applying existing algorithms, the methodological innovation lies in formulating a coupled architecture where explicit high-precision surface meshes mathematically constrain the implicit volumetric fields, bridging the distinct mathematical spaces of computer graphics and geostatistics. The approach first converts the OSGB reality model into high-quality explicit geometric constraints through topology repair and mesh optimization, combining Hermite Radial Basis Functions (HRBF) to establish a high-precision peak model. Subsequently, the Skinning Method is adopted to represent rivers and Quaternary thin layers, and a Dual Implicit Function managed by a binary tree is introduced to accurately resolve complex fault networks. Finally, within a unified tetrahedral grid space, a Boolean cutting process strictly following the geological evolutionary sequence is established. Application to the core area of Mount Danxia demonstrates that this framework successfully transforms large-area photogrammetric meshes into 3D geological models, realizing a transition from traditional DEM-constrained modeling to the integration of OSGB-derived, geometrically detailed surface constraints with deep geological attributes. Cross-section analysis indicates a high degree of consistency between the model and stratigraphic data. This study provides a universal technical paradigm for high-precision refined modeling in complex orogenic belts and special geomorphic areas.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: An improved slime mould algorithm applied to hyperspectral feature selection in soil fertility indicators
abstract: High-precision soil quality monitoring is vital for precision agriculture. Recently, swarm intelligence (SI) algorithms have become essential for identifying hyperspectral features. Aiming at the challenges of high dimensionality in soil fertility indicator retrieval, this paper integrates ZY1-02E satellite and HyMap airborne data to conduct feature selection and fertility estimation using an improved slime mould algorithm (ISMA). ISMA integrates three synergistic stages: (1) spectrally-informed initialization and pre-screening for redundancy reduction, (2) a multi-level location update strategy for balancing exploration and exploitation, and (3) a complementary stagnation control strategy for late stage search refinement. A customized fitness function is designed to optimize the estimation of soil fertility indicators. The effectiveness of the proposed ISMA was first validated on ZY1-02E satellite imagery. Experimental results demonstrated that the ISMA-XGBoost model yielded the best optimization capability, achieving the test R 2 of 0.752 for soil organic matter (SOM) on ZY1-02E data, and its multi-indicator applicability was confirmed with R 2 values of 0.675 (total phosphorus), 0.670 (total potassium), and 0.678 (total nitrogen). The model’s reliability was validated on independent HyMap data (R 2 = 0.757), a significant improvement over conventional algorithm (R 2 = 0.730). These findings provide critical technical support for regional precision agriculture.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Global assessment of climate-driven lag and cumulative effects on vegetation using Earth Observation data and multivariable machine learning models
abstract: Vegetation rarely responds instantaneously to meteorological variations; instead, its adjustment often reflects delayed and accumulated climatic influences. However, these temporal effects have not been comprehensively analyzed at the global scale, particularly with higher-resolution Earth Observation (EO) data and across multiple climate drivers. By leveraging EO datasets and modeling approaches, this study characterizes global trends in vegetation and climate, evaluates time effects, and develops climate–vegetation regression and prediction models. Our results revealed normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) increase alongside shifts in key climatic variables during the study period. A large proportion of vegetated regions showed temporal responses, with heterogeneity in major climate zones. Incorporating time-effect variables into eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model influenced model performance across regions, while temperature (Tmp) and surface solar radiation downwards (SSRD), together with their corresponding temporal-effect predictors, were identified as the key influential climatic contributors. Among predictive approaches, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) showed the highest skill in capturing nonlinear vegetation–climate interactions. These findings underscore that temporal effects are fundamental to global vegetation dynamics and point to the need for EO-based, multivariable modeling frameworks to elucidate ecosystem response under ongoing climate change.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: A framework for assessing rainfall extremes induced aboveground biomass loss from multisource remote sensing data
abstract: Increasingly frequent and intense rainfall extremes can trigger flooding, landslides, and severe soil erosion, leading to substantial losses of vegetation aboveground biomass (AGB). However, event-scale assessments of rainfall extremes induced AGB loss remain largely unexplored. Here, we propose a framework to estimate event-scale AGB loss induced by extreme rainfall events. The framework integrates high-resolution change detection techniques to identify vegetation loss sites with an Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost)-based downscaling approach to derive sub-meter AGB from coarse-resolution AGB products. We evaluated the framework across three extreme rainfall events in China: Beijing (2023), Luochuan (2021), and Zixing (2024). The framework achieved high accuracy across all case studies, with F1 scores of 0.94, 0.92, and 0.94 for three events in identifying loss sites, as well as an R 2 value of 0.88 and RMSE of 4.44 Mg/ha for downscaled high-resolution AGB estimates. We further apply a Random Forest-based residual modeling to investigate model errors, indicating that terrain-related factors play a dominant role in shaping the variability of AGB estimation errors. The average AGB loss densities within identified sites are 75.21 Mg/ha, 67.08 Mg/ha, and 90.94 Mg/ha for three events, respectively. These findings highlight the framework’s potential in assessing event-scale AGB loss, providing a practical tool for ecological monitoring and disaster response under intensifying climate variability.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: SignSpotter: scene text-informed cross-modal semantic consistency verification for street view images and POI data
abstract: Ensuring semantic consistency between street view images and Points of Interest (POI) is critical for reliable geographic entity validation in complex urban scenes. To address challenges such as visual occlusion, scale variation, and ambiguous scene text, this paper proposes SignSpotter, a novel multi-scale vision-language framework for entity-level consistency verification. First, a scene text-informed visual pre-training strategy is introduced to sensitize the Vision Transformer to fine-grained textual regions. Second, a resolution-adaptive asymmetric dual-tower architecture is employed to jointly model multi-scale visual features and POI textual embeddings, effectively mitigating scale disparities. Furthermore, a cross-modal semantic reasoning module establishes precise visual-textual associations via bidirectional attention for explicit consistency inference. Experiments on a large-scale dataset demonstrate that SignSpotter achieves an F1-score of 90.96% on the source city dataset. Cross-city and cross-platform transfer tests further yield stable F1-scores exceeding 86%. These results, together with occlusion analyses, confirm the robustness of SignSpotter and highlight its potential for automated large-scale geographic data quality control.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Spatiotemporal prediction of grass curing in Victoria, Australia using Multi-Source remote sensing and deep learning models
abstract: Degree of Curing (DoC) is an important ecological indicator for assessing grassland dryness and vegetation flammability, and accurate monitoring and prediction are critical for wildfire risk assessment in fire-prone regions. Focusing on Victoria, Australia, this study developed and compared several deep learning models for monthly spatiotemporal DoC prediction using multi-source remote sensing datasets derived from MODIS and ERA5-Land. Among the tested models, the Temporally Enhanced Convolutional Long Short-Term Memory model (TE-ConvLSTM) achieved the best overall performance, with an RMSE of 9.18 and an R 2 of 0.834. By integrating explicit temporal encoding and multi-scale spatial feature extraction, the model effectively captured seasonal DoC dynamics, more accurately reproduced elevated curing conditions and seasonal peaks during the fire-prone period and better represented spatial gradients and regional heterogeneity across the study area. The results demonstrate that the proposed temporally enhanced convolutional framework provides an effective approach for modeling spatiotemporal DoC dynamics and establishes a promising foundation for future investigations of predictive grass curing modelling for regional wildfire risk assessment and monitoring.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Infinite details: A cartography-informed parametric method for constructing realistic 3D natural scenes
abstract: Realistic 3D scenes enhance spatial comprehension and support decision-making by creating intuitive and immersive representations of the physical world. However, achieving realism in natural scenes is challenging because of the complexity of microscale details influenced by natural disturbance events such as weathering, aging, and decay. This study introduces a cartography-informed parametric method for constructing 3D natural scenes with fine-scale details, including three components: a semantic tree, a spatial layout, and a model placement. The method simultaneously considers global entities and local details, where the generation of the latter is spatially constrained by the context of the former. Experiments are conducted across five natural scenes, and two types of user studies are carried out to evaluate visual perception. The results demonstrate the adaptability and effectiveness of the proposed method in scenes comprising various types of entities and details. Compared with scenes without details, scenes containing details exhibit superior visual realism, as evidenced by an average user rating scores of 3.51 versus 2.78 and a user selection count of 5.12 versus 0.88. This work provides a new methodological perspective on natural scene modeling and expands upon potential interdisciplinary applications that span dynamics and aesthetics.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Editorial Board
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Reconstructing history: 3D high-resolution GPR analysis based on SAR discoveries in the ancient Siniyah Island of Umm Al-Quwain, United Arab Emirates
abstract: The Siniyah Island in Umm Al-Quwain is one of the pearls of the United Arab Emirates. Archaeologists have discovered vivid evidence that brought to light a vibrant multicultural past occupation. Among the substantial findings were tools of prehistoric settlements, a Christian monastery and a wide marine trading network between the Arabian Gulf and other far regions. These revelations deliver a valuable depiction of the socio-economic, cultural, and religious dynamics of the Siniyah Island prior to the Islamic era. Here, we present for the first time on the island, A high-resolution Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) survey was carried out in three priority areas delineated through an integrated Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) analysis and machine-learning–based spatial screening. SAR tomography provided intermediate-scale subsurface assessment, reducing spatial uncertainty prior to field investigation. The subsequent GPR surveys enabled detailed imaging and three-dimensional reconstruction of buried structures, allowing validation and refined characterization of candidate archaeological features. Despite the anticipated theoretical hostile conditions to investigate electromagnetic waves, GPR results perfectly align with the geometry of the unearthed ancient structures. In addition to the known archaeological sites, GPR data, analyzed through B-scans, C-scans, and three-dimensional models, reveal a high concentration of sharp anomalies resembling archaeological features, suggesting that the island was once home to a high-density ancient population.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Spatial and temporal patterns of early leaf discoloration in Switzerland’s European beech forests
abstract: The onset of leaf discoloration in deciduous trees is primarily triggered by seasonal declines in temperature and photoperiod. However, severe drought conditions can induce early leaf discoloration and shedding. Early discolored trees may be more susceptible to crown dieback and mortality following a drought. These persistent legacy effects of drought underlie efforts to understand the environmental drivers of early discoloration but also complicate ongoing discoloration monitoring. Here, field observations of early leaf discoloration in Switzerland’s European beech (Fagus sylvatica L.) forests and annually normalized Sentinel-2 vegetation index time series were used to model and isolate the signal of discoloration in both drought and post-drought years. To demonstrate model efficacy and examine empirical inter- and intra-annual trends in early leaf discoloration, the trained model was applied to predict monthly April to August early leaf discoloration across Switzerland at a 10 m resolution from 2017 to 2023. Results reveal a striking nine-times increase in early leaf discoloration during the drought-affected month of August 2018 as compared to non-drought affected August 2020 and a nearly three-times increase in August 2023 discoloration over August 2020. In 2018 and 2023, discoloration hotspots formed as early as June in Switzerland’s most severely affected northwestern regions and spread rapidly in the following weeks. Efforts here establish a robust framework for disentangling seasonal drought related discoloration from legacy effects of drought and forest management forming a baseline for further investigations of biotic and abiotic early leaf discoloration drivers.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: High-resolution (30-m) multi-decadal reconstruction of coastal water quality via Landsat-Sentinel fusion and ensemble machine learning (1985–2024)
abstract: Coastal water quality monitoring is pivotal for marine ecosystem management. However, current monitoring capabilities are constrained by a trade-off between the high accuracy of sparse in-situ sampling and the broad coverage but coarse resolution of traditional ocean color satellites. To bridge this gap, this study establishes a cloud-native framework coupling multi-source satellite fusion with machine learning to reconstruct a high-resolution (30 m) water quality dataset for the coastal waters of Guangdong, China, spanning a 40-year period. Leveraging the Google Earth Engine (GEE) platform, we harmonized Landsat-5/7/8 and Sentinel-2 MSI, processing over 22,172 valid scenes via a hierarchical regression strategy to overcome cross-sensor spectral inconsistencies. A Random Forest ensemble model was developed to retrieve Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD, R 2 = 0.76), Total Nitrogen (TN, R 2 = 0.86), and Total Phosphorus (TP, R 2 = 0.88). The time series unveils a significant upward trajectory in COD concentrations (+4.08 × 10 −3 mg/L/yr) with a regime shift around 2013. Spatially, COD plumes exhibited a “Westward Expansion” pattern during the wet season, contrasting with winter maxima for TN and TP. This parameter‑specific divergence demonstrates that organic and nutrient pollutants are governed by different source and transport mechanisms – a finding that single‑parameter studies would miss. We further explored the associations between water quality variations and environmental drivers, revealing a “Human-Climate Coupled” control pattern. Beyond this qualitative mechanism, we identify a dual‑process pathway and quantify a 6‑month lag between ENSO events and peak COD anomalies, moving the discussion from simple correlation to potentially predictive understanding. This study provides the first multi-decadal, high-resolution benchmark for the Greater Bay Area and demonstrates the value of cloud-based multi-sensor fusion for precision coastal management.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Machine learning correction of C2-Net for chlorophyll-a retrieval in optically complex small reservoirs
abstract: Accurate recovery of chlorophyll-a concentration in small inland reservoirs remains challenging due to optical complexity, land-water adjacency effects, and scaling mismatches in atmospheric correction algorithms. This study evaluates the performance of the C2-Net atmospheric processors (C2RCC, C2X, and C2XC) applied to Sentinel-2 images of 32 small reservoirs in Extremadura, Spain, using 94 satellite scenes and in situ chlorophyll-a measurements. While C2RCC showed moderate correlation with field data, it exhibited systematic underestimation, whereas C2X and C2XC produced extreme overestimations despite preserving strong monotonic relationships. To address these limitations, a machine learning-based correction framework was developed, combining rescaled processor outputs, interaction terms, and aggregate statistics. The proposed approach significantly improved recovery accuracy, reducing the RMSE by up to 35\% compared to the best baseline processor. Regularized regression models provided a solid balance between accuracy, stability, and interpretability, while more complex models achieved superior peak performance. Validation results confirmed good spatial transferability across reservoirs and trophic conditions, with greater uncertainty in hypertrophic scenarios. The proposed framework offers an operational and transferable solution for improving satellite monitoring of chlorophyll a in small, optically complex inland water bodies.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Hybrid physics–AI aerosol property retrieval algorithm for AMI/GK-2A with a deep learning radiative transfer emulator
abstract: Computational advances have enabled the evolution and refinement of satellite aerosol retrieval algorithms to mitigate issues in previous versions and improve their results. This study addressed a fundamental limitation in operational satellite remote sensing which is the trade-off between computational efficiency and retrieval accuracy in conventional look-up table (LUT)-based algorithms. The hybrid-Yonsei Aerosol Retrieval (hybrid-YAER) algorithm for the Advanced Meteorological Imager (AMI) incorporates a flexible aerosol model input, which became available by using a deep learning (DL) radiative transfer model (RTM) that replaces the interpolation-based inversion with LUTs. The DLRTM, trained with 100,000 Vector LInearized Discrete Ordinate Radiative Transfer (VLIDORT) code simulations using a Set Transformer architecture, accurately reproduces top-of-atmosphere reflectance (the root-mean-square error is about 0.002 for Mie calculations) at computation times about 0.1% of those of a conventional RTM. Additionally, a dust call-back procedure and an extended surface reflectance database based on multi-year minimum reflectance are introduced in the hybrid-YAER algorithm. Validation against AERONET and comparison with Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) Dark Target (DT) and Deep Blue (DB) AOD products demonstrate that the new algorithm mitigates underestimation of low values of aerosol optical depth (AOD) and discontinuities of AOD values between adjacent land and ocean, while improving overall correlation (R increased from 0.757 to 0.767 for land pixels and from 0.856 to 0.881 for ocean pixels) and reducing bias. Over ocean, bias patterns become more linear, and the retrieval stability is improved (R² increased from 0.88 to 0.94) compared to the original version. Uncertainty analysis shows that retrieval uncertainty scales linearly with AOD, confirming the robustness of the hybrid algorithm. The concept of advancement in aerosol retrieval via hybrid algorithm can be applied to any other aerosol remote sensing algorithms.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: An AI system for residential building damage estimation using multimodal remote sensing data fusion
abstract: The increasing intensity of tropical storms has created an urgent need for rapid, reliable damage assessment. Although recent AI-based approaches have improved upon manual inspection, many rely on proprietary satellite imagery or ad hoc UAV datasets, limiting scalability, repeatability, and operational deployment. In this study, we develop a multimodal AI framework for post-disaster damage assessment using only publicly available remote sensing and geospatial data, including NOAA aerial imagery, Microsoft building footprints, and FEMA damage labels. A key methodological contribution is the use of spatially disjoint training and validation regions in the Hurricane Michael dataset to prevent geographic data leakage and to more realistically evaluate generalization to unseen locations, an issue that is frequently overlooked in geospatial AI studies. Using this rigorous validation strategy, we conduct a comparative evaluation of leading deep learning architectures, including Convolutional Neural Networks (ResNet and VGG) and the Vision Transformer (ViT). Model performance in classifying buildings as affected or destroyed is assessed using disaster-relevant evaluation metrics. Results demonstrate that the Vision Transformer consistently outperforms CNN-based models, likely due to its global self-attention mechanism, which more effectively captures spatial context in dense urban environments. Overall, this work demonstrates the feasibility of a scalable, public-data-based framework for rapid damage assessment, while identifying severe class imbalance as a key operational challenge, motivating the use of specialized loss weighting and data augmentation strategies in future deployments.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: From pixels to Algae: Assessing cyanobacterial bloom severity in Northeastern lakes through Multi-Class phytoplankton density retrieval
abstract: Frequent algal blooms have intensified ecological risks in lakes and reservoirs worldwide, posing serious threats to regional water quality and drinking water security. As a key indicator of lake ecosystem health, phytoplankton density has long been central to limnological and environmental research. However, most existing studies provide only broad descriptions of bloom dynamics and rarely differentiate the specific contributions of individual algal phyla to bloom development. This limitation hinders a deeper understanding of phylum-specific density variations and their environmental response mechanisms. In this study, satellite observations were used to examine the spatiotemporal dynamics and driving mechanisms of major algal phyla in lakes larger than 20 km 2 across Northeast China. Bloom types dominated by Cyanophyta, Chlorophyta, and Bacillariophyta were identified, and a cyanobacterial bloom classification system was established based on phylum-specific density thresholds.
