Results showed that Cyanophyta overwhelmingly dominated phytoplankton communities, with an average density of 1.54 × 10 7 Cells/L —15.6 and 17.0 times higher than those of Chlorophyta (9.84 × 10 5 Cells/L ) and Bacillariophyta (9.06 × 10 5 Cells/L ), respectively. Between 2016 and 2023, 42.37 % of the lakes exhibited a significant increasing trend in Cyanophyta density ( p < 0.05), indicating that algal bloom events in Northeast China’s lakes and reservoirs are primarily driven by Cyanobacteria. On average, the areal proportions of lakes experiencing no bloom (Level I), mild (Level II), moderate (Level III), and severe blooms (Level IV) were 73.74 %, 16.76 %, 8.11 %, and 1.38 %, respectively. Over the past decade, the area affected by severe Cyanophyta blooms expanded from 1.51 % to 2.54 %, suggesting that bloom proliferation has become increasingly common and that associated ecological risks are intensifying. This study underscores the importance of phylum-level phytoplankton density monitoring in inland lakes and provides a novel perspective for identifying bloom types and assessing their ecological implications.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: GSR-Track: A Geo-Semantic Regularized Sparse tracker for satellite videos
abstract: Satellite video object tracking (SVOT) faces general challenges such as tiny target sizes, dense distractors, and complex environmental occlusions. While Vision Transformers (ViTs) have recently driven significant progress in visual tracking, directly applying standard ViT architectures to satellite videos exposes three mechanism-level limitations: (1) sub-patch feature dilution, where the structural details of tiny targets are overwhelmed by background information within a single token; (2) attention noise propagation, where global attention mechanisms struggle to distinguish the target from visually similar distractors in dense traffic; and (3) lack of spatial constraints, leading to tracking failure during prolonged visual occlusions like cloud cover. To systematically address these architectural limitations, we propose the Geo-Semantic Regularized Sparse Tracker (GSR-Track). First, a Frequency-Aware Feature Refinement (FFR) module is introduced to explicitly recover high-frequency structural details before tokenization. Second, we design an Interference-Suppression Sparse Attention (ISSA) mechanism that utilizes dynamic soft-thresholding to adaptively prune attention connections to background noise. Third, a Category-Specific Semantic Guidance (CSG) module incorporates geographic information system (GIS) priors to constrain target trajectories within feasible physical regions. Extensive experiments on SatSOT, SV248S, and VISO benchmarks demonstrate that GSR-Track significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving 75.5% and 77.7% Precision on SatSOT and SV248S, respectively.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Robust hyperspectral anomaly detection via low-rank discriminative dictionary and global-local saliency weight
abstract: Robust hyperspectral anomaly detection (HAD) without prior information is an important task in hyperspectral data analysis. Recently, collaborative representation-based (CR) methods have gained increasing attention. However, existing methods are limited in detection performance due to single constraints, insufficiently robust dictionaries, and inadequate feature utilization. To address these issues, this paper proposes a robust HAD framework featuring low-rank discriminative dictionary learning and global-local anomaly saliency weight. Specifically, a low-rank discriminative dictionary learning framework is established to construct a robust background representation by selecting training samples with strong coverage through an optimized ordering and stepping strategy. To further preserve the local geometric structure among dictionary atoms, a graph regularization is integrated into the CR model. Furthermore, we exploit both global and local spatial-spectral information to construct a saliency weight, which effectively suppresses background interference and highlights anomalous targets. Furthermore, a new hyperspectral dataset, Hohai Camouflage, is introduced to provide a more comprehensive evaluation under complex camouflage scenarios. Experimental results on this dataset and three publicly datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms other classical and advanced algorithms, exhibiting its robustness and adaptability. The code and new dataset will be published at: https://github.com/skipper12138/AGCR-LRD
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Identifying multi-scale human flow clusters via spatiotemporal network flow L function
abstract: Understanding spatiotemporal clustering patterns of human flows is critical for interpreting mobility dynamics and addressing urban issues. Ripley’s K-function, distinguished by its non-parametric and multi-scale properties, provides an effective method for flow clustering. Human flows, however, are inherently constrained by road networks and evolve along linear structures over time, making network-based spatiotemporal analysis indispensable. Existing network K-functions for flow clustering ignore linear geometry, neglect temporal dynamics, and suffer from edge effects and cross-network incomparability. This study introduces the linear reference system to explicitly represent human flows on linear road networks, and proposes the Spatiotemporal Network flow K-function (STNflowK) and its variation (STNflowL function) for multi-scale human flow clustering. Spatiotemporal expansion factors are innovatively proposed to correct edge effects and to ensure that the expectation of STNflowK is independent of network geometry and flow locations. We theoretically and empirically verify that E [ S T N f l o w K ] = s 2 t 2 and E [ S T N f l o w L ] = 0 for any spatiotemporal scales, thereby enabling reliable pattern detection within individual networks and statistically consistent comparison across different networks. Simulations across various scenarios validate that the STNflowL function outperforms baseline models in spatiotemporal network flow clustering. Applications to real-world human flows further reveal its superiority in spatiotemporal scale estimation, multi-scale flow cluster extraction, and mobility dynamics understanding.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Satellite-derived population-weighted NO2 exposure and inequality across African subnational regions for SDGs 3 and 11
abstract: Air-pollution exposure is a growing public-health and urban-governance concern in Africa, but comparable subnational evidence remains limited. This study constructs an Africa-wide Administrative Level 1 (ADM1) panel for 2019–2023 using Sentinel-5P TROPOMI tropospheric nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ), LandScan population, settlement, meteorological, and topographic data. We estimate area-mean NO 2 and population-weighted NO 2 exposure, quantify within-country inequality, assess population-pollution alignment, and examine interpretable natural and human-related associations. Population-weighted NO 2 exposure is spatially persistent and highly uneven, with elevated burdens concentrated in North African coastal and Nile-corridor regions, Southern African urban-industrial zones, and selected metropolitan or industrial ADM1 units elsewhere. Continental mean exposure declined slightly in 2020 and rebounded above the 2019 level from 2021 onward, consistent with a short-lived disruption of traffic and industrial activity during the COVID-19 period. National averages concealed strong internal concentration, with a limited number of ADM1 units carrying disproportionate national burden. Random held-out validation indicated strong predictive structure, while country-blocked validation exposed limited out-of-country transferability. Interpretable machine-learning attribution using XGBoost and SHAP showed that nighttime lights and built-environment indicators were strongly associated with exposure, while wind, temperature, precipitation, elevation, and slope further shaped the observed patterns. Sensitivity analyses showed that ADM1-level exposure rankings were robust to NO 2 -to-population-grid alignment choices and that GHSL built-environment covariates were stable between 2020 and 2025; independent near-surface NO 2 evidence in Accra further showed moderate spatial agreement and consistent Harmattan enhancement with satellite-derived NO 2 . The framework provides an Earth-observation-based baseline for identifying priority subnational regions, tracking exposure inequality, and supporting SDG 3- and SDG 11-relevant air-quality governance in data-scarce African settings.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: UVSENet: A Semantic-Embedded dual branch fusion network for urban villages mapping
abstract: Urban villages (UVs) represent a typical yet highly complex spatial outcome of rapid urbanization. Accurate identification of UVs from remote sensing imagery is of great significance for understanding urban–rural mechanisms and supporting scientific urban governance and sustainable development. However, traditional optical remote sensing imagery is inherently limited by insufficient single modality representation capability, while multimodal data fusion is often constrained by data heterogeneity and cross modal semantic inconsistency. To address these challenges, this study proposes a cross modal semantic guided dual branch network for UVs identification (UVSENet). The proposed model deeply integrates Satellite Embedding data with Sentinel-2 optical imagery, enabling semantic level information compensation and structural level joint perception. Specifically, the semantic branch encodes high-level prior knowledge to guide the optical branch in achieving semantic alignment and feature enhancement during spatial structure extraction. This design further facilitates cross regional knowledge generalization, thereby improving the recognition of complex spatial patterns characteristic of UVs. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model consistently outperforms conventional single data source methods and shallow feature fusion approaches in terms of IoU, F1 score, and overall accuracy. The model achieves an IoU of 71.44 % and an F1 score of 83.35 % for UV identification, outperforming existing methods and demonstrating highly competitive performance. These findings validate the effectiveness of incorporating satellite semantic embedding data into remote sensing semantic segmentation and highlight its potential for large scale UV mapping. Moreover, this work provides a novel technical pathway for multimodal semantic alignment and knowledge driven urban analysis.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Automatic design of efficient SAR ship detection networks for large-scale scenes via neural architecture search
abstract: Large-scene ship detection based on Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery plays a critical role in wide-area maritime surveillance and navigation safety. However, conventional intelligent SAR detection methods heavily rely on expert prior knowledge for network architecture design, which limits their adaptability to the diverse ship target morphologies present in large-scale and complex marine environments. To this end, we propose an efficient SAR ship detection network automatic design method based on Neural Architecture Search (NAS). First, constructed a high-capacity SuperNet based on weight sharing, in which multiple convolutional kernels are merged into a unified superkernel to accelerate the architecture search process. Second, employed the Gumbel–Softmax distribution to dynamically adjust the weights of different paths, integrate multipath convolutional outputs, enhance the model’s generalization capability. Finally, unified the architecture search spaces of the Backbone and Neck into a joint optimization framework to more effectively fuse and strengthen hierarchical feature representations. On the SSDD and HRSID datasets, the proposed method achieves search times of 1.981 h and 11.449 h, respectively, with mAP50 detection accuracies of 98.2% and 92.3%, respectively. Demonstrate that our approach can efficiently perform model search for different datasets while achieving high detection accuracy.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: PG-GVB: A prior constrained backscatter framework for P-band PolInSAR forest height inversion
abstract: Facilitated by the BIOMASS mission, P-band polarimetric SAR interferometry (PolInSAR) provides a key capability for large-scale forest height mapping and biomass estimation. Within this context, the random volume over ground (RVoG) model stands out for its physical consistency and broad applicability. However, at P-band, deviations of canopy backscattering from the exponential extinction assumption in RVoG lead to biased height estimates. While gaussian vertical backscatter (GVB) offers greater flexibility, its surplus parameters and unconstrained convergence raise robustness concerns, resulting in estimation biases that limit its widespread application. To address these challenges, a convolutional neural network (CNN) is used to link structure parameters to SAR observations, thereby imposing prior constraints. A parameter-guided GVB (PG-GVB) variant is developed within a three-stage framework, achieving improved performance while explicitly analyzing how different parameters influence robustness. Validation on BioSAR-2008 and AfriSAR-2016 shows that the best-constrained configuration reduces forest height errors by 20.5% (4.83 m to 3.84 m) and 26.5% (7.49 m to 5.50 m) relative to the exponential model at Krycklan and Lopé, respectively. These results reveal transferable optimization strategies, with shapley additive explanations (SHAP) analysis further quantifying feature contributions.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Spaceborne imaging spectroscopy advances modeling of grazer resource selection
abstract: Linking animal movement to underlying forage resources across large landscapes remains challenging because spatially explicit measurements of forage quantity and quality are difficult to obtain at broad spatial extents. Researchers have often relied on localized field studies, limiting the ability to generalize movement-resource relationships at landscape scales. Imaging spectroscopy offers a promising solution, yet its application in modeling animal resource selection has been constrained by the limited availability of fine spatial resolution data. We integrated airborne and spaceborne imaging spectroscopy with Global Positioning System telemetry from 28 free-ranging cattle monitored from April to July 2025 at the Tallgrass Prairie Preserve (TGPP), Oklahoma, USA, to evaluate how forage quantity (aboveground dry biomass) and quality (nitrogen concentration) shape movement in a grassland managed with prescribed fire and grazing. We assessed the capacity of imaging spectroscopy to predict forage characteristics using two datasets acquired during the peak growing season in June 2025, including a 1 m airborne dataset collected with an AISA Fenix imaging spectrometer and a fused 3 m product combining DLR Earth Sensing Imaging Spectrometer (DESIS) and PlanetScope imagery. Specifically, we estimated forage characteristics using partial least squares regression models calibrated and validated with field measurements of aboveground dry biomass and nitrogen concentration collected from 900 quadrats across 100 plots. Airborne data achieved the highest predictive performance for both aboveground dry biomass (R 2 = 0.32, RMSE = 53 g/m 2 , NRMSE = 19%) and nitrogen concentration (R 2 = 0.35, RMSE = 0.28%, NRMSE = 20%), while the fused DESIS-PlanetScope product achieved comparable biomass estimation (R 2 = 0.35, RMSE = 52 g/m 2 , NRMSE = 18%) but weaker nitrogen retrieval (R 2 = 0.19, RMSE = 0.29%, NRMSE = 22%), likely due to the absence of shortwave infrared bands in DESIS. We then incorporated these variables into an integrated step selection function to test whether imaging spectroscopy enables inference of grazer resource selection and how selection varies with fire history. Cattle consistently avoided areas with high aboveground dry biomass but selected nitrogen-rich vegetation, indicating a preference for high-quality regrowth. Selection varied with time since fire; recently burned patches showed higher relative selection strength, whereas older burns were increasingly avoided. Spatial patterns of resource selection were highly consistent between airborne and fused spaceborne datasets (concordance = 0.81 for both), indicating that data fusion is a scalable solution for transitioning from localized airborne surveys to global monitoring using spaceborne assets. These findings demonstrate that spaceborne imaging spectroscopy can facilitate routine, landscape-scale monitoring of herbivore-vegetation interactions, with broad implications for rangeland management, conservation planning, and the utilization of next-generation imaging spectroscopy missions.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Limitations of interpreting orbiting satellite-based fire detection for crop residue burning: Has rice straw burning in northwest India decreased in recent years?
abstract: In the northwest region of India, large-scale rice straw burning (RSB) takes place after the harvest every year. For policymaking purposes, the year-to-year variation of RSB fires has been studied extensively using the ‘fire detection counts’ (FDC) derived from orbiting satellite-borne sensors such as the Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) and the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS). However, because RSB fires are typically extinguished within an hour, orbiting satellites represent only a small fraction of the daily total active fires. Many fires can also go undetected due to cloud cover, further compromising the reliability of the FDC. In this study, we demonstrate the limitations of interpreting the FDC for the post-harvest burning of rice straw, the most extensively burned crop residue in the region. We investigated the effects of cloud cover, estimated the number of fires obscured by clouds using Gaussian fitting, and explored potential fires occurring outside the satellite’s observation times. This analysis was based on FDC data from MODIS and VIIRS, aerosol data from MODIS, and smoke data from the Indian INSAT-3D geostationary satellite. Our findings indicate that while the relatively low FDC in the year 2019 can be explained by cloud shielding, the rapid decrease in the FDC after 2022 cannot be attributed solely to cloud effects or mitigation policies. In particular, in 2024, the higher number of INSAT-3D smoke pixels at hours outside the orbiting satellite overpass (13:30 local time) suggests that burning occurs more frequently outside the orbit passage. These findings are expected to help researchers and policymakers better interpret the year-to-year variation in the orbiting satellite-based observed FDC when monitoring the effectiveness of RSB mitigation policies.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Large-Scale monitoring of dry snow in High Mountain Asia (2015–2024) from Sentinel-1 SAR observations
abstract: Dry-snow zones, the highest and coldest parts of a glacier where summer melt is absent, remain poorly constrained in High Mountain Asia (HMA) due to limited high-altitude observations. Here we present the first decadal, region-wide assessment of dry-snow distribution across HMA from 2015 to 2024 based on Sentinel-1 SAR observations. A physically guided approach combining SAR backscatter thresholds with an elevation constraint is used to delineate dry-snow zones. Dry snow is mainly confined to high-altitude western and southern regions, while largely absent elsewhere across HMA. Its extent shows strong interannual sensitivity to summer air temperature, weak correlation to precipitation, and positive associations with glacier mass balance across subregions. The consistency between SAR-derived dry-snow patterns and independent climatic and mass-balance signals indicates that this simple, physically based approach provides reliable large-scale estimates of accumulation-state conditions in data-sparse, high-elevation environments. Dry-snow extent therefore emerges as a sensitive and previously underexplored indicator of glacier–climate interactions, providing new observational constraints for future glacier-change projections.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Navigating Hierarchies in Hyperbolic Space: A Knowledge-Driven Graph Network for Semantic Segmentation of Remote Sensing Imagery
abstract: Semantic segmentation of multi-scale remote sensing objects faces two key challenges: representing complex relationships and effectively integrating geographic knowledge. These relationships generate hierarchical patterns embedded with eigen properties, forming a nested system that exhibits exponential growth, a characteristic poorly captured by Euclidean-based deep learning models limited to polynomial expansion. Hyperbolic space offers a geometrically faithful alternative, but current hyperbolic neural networks rely on tangent space projections for computation, introducing significant approximation errors that degrade network performance. To address these challenges, we introduce a knowledge-driven framework founded on fully hyperbolic neural network operators. These operators are designed to be manifold-preserving, enabling all computations to be performed directly within hyperbolic space and thereby eliminating tangent space approximation errors. Building on this foundation, we propose a novel Fully Hyperbolic Graph Attention Network (FHGAT) that operates on a multi-relational heterogeneous graph representation of remote sensing objects. Our model effectively mines and integrates embedded knowledge from complex, multi-scale relationships in a bottom-up fashion. Extensive experiments validate its superiority; compared to a standard Euclidean baseline, our model increases object-level accuracy and Mean Intersection over Union (MIoU) by 7.2% and 7.6%, respectively. Notably, it also surpasses a state-of-the-art tangent-space approximation model by 5.4% in accuracy, confirming the benefits of its end-to-end hyperbolic design for resolving spectral confusion. This research marks a significant step in advancing remote sensing analysis from a data-driven to a more robust and interpretable knowledge-driven paradigm.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: An optimization AI model based on MoE for retrieving land surface temperature and emissivity
abstract: The main drawbacks of contemporary MODIS land surface temperature (LST) and emissivity (LSE) outputs stem from cloud pollution, imprecision in atmospheric moisture vapor rectification, preliminary miscalculations of variable surface emissivity, and heterogeneity at the sub-pixel level, leading to significant potential for advancements in the reliability of these outputs. This study proposes an iterative optimization strategy based on an Optimization Artificial Intelligence Model Based on Mixture of Experts (Opt-MoE) model. Initially, a logical analysis based on physical principles was conducted using the radiative transfer equation to verify that the model’s input and output parameters align with the principles and determination criteria of parameter inversion. Subsequently, the radiative transfer framework was applied to model and progressively refine the MODIS thermal infrared channels, confirming the practicality of enhancement and determining the most suitable band configuration. Then, brightness temperature, LST, and LSE product data were collected in five MODIS thermal infrared bands. An iterative fine-tuning strategy was constructed based on the Adam optimizer to gradually optimize the Opt-MoE and obtain a product dataset that more closely approximates the real LST and LSE. Lastly, the Opt-MoE underwent retraining and was implemented for retrieving MODIS information. Outcomes demonstrate that, during the experiment with modeled data, in contrast to the four-band arrangement, the mean absolute error (MAE) in LST retrieval employing five-band inputs dropped from 0.6346 K to 0.5238 K, the Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) rose from 0.9981 to 0.9993, and the precision of LSE retrieval likewise experienced substantial enhancement. Additionally, the discrepancy between the refined perturbed simulation data and the true simulation data was negligible. The optimization validation using observational data showed that, after iterative fine-tuning, the MAE of LST retrieval decreased from 1.7748 K to 0.7199 K, while the PCC increased from 0.9817 to 0.9973.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: A data- and knowledge-driven cropland parcel recognition method based on segment anything model (SAM)
abstract: In modern agricultural practices, information on cropland parcels serves as an indispensable foundation of agricultural production management. However, manual annotation of remote sensing image datasets is time-consuming and labor-intensive. Traditional models tend to focus on pixel-level segmentation while neglecting the fine-grained boundary features of cropland parcels. To address these challenges, this study first utilizes the Segment Anything Model (SAM) to generate cropland parcel label samples based on multi-source remote sensing imagery and the Third National Land Survey (TNLS) data. Morphological processing and texture feature screening are employed to enhance the quality of pseudo-labels. Subsequently, we propose a multi-task intelligent cropland parcel extraction model, Squeeze-and-Excitation Multiple Task Decoder Network (SE-MTDNet). This model adds a Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) channel to RGB channels to extract hierarchical features. The atrous spatial pyramid pooling (ASPP) module and channel attention are introduced to aggregate multi-scale contextual information. In the decoder, multi-task joint training is adopted to prevent over-reliance on the single results. Experimental results demonstrate that SE-MTDNet significantly improves both the accuracy and boundary clarity of cropland parcel recognition. In Xi County, SE-MTDNet achieved an overall classification accuracy of 94.25%, an Intersection over Union (IoU) of 88.67%, and an F1-score of 92.76%. Furthermore, the model also outperformed other comparison models in transfer validation conducted in Lishu County. Ablation experiments further confirm that key modules and the NDVI feature contribute significantly to improved cropland parcel segmentation accuracy. Our method provides valuable insights into high-precision and automated cropland parcel recognition.

title: Improved understanding of California coastal cliff morphodynamics using airborne lidar and vegetation filtering (2016–2023)
abstract: Coastal cliffs are widespread along California coastlines, yet their erosion remains difficult to quantify at statewide scales because of (1) limited high-resolution data, (2) intensive processing requirements, and (3) challenges in mapping ground elevations beneath vegetation. This study collected airborne lidar data across the California coast in 2023 and compared it with 2016 lidar to evaluate coastal cliff changes. We developed automated approaches to (1) delineate cliff geometry and cliff top retreat, and (2) quantify erosion volume changes and retreat rates at 5-m spacing alongshore. Using ground filtering algorithms, we reduced vegetation-obscured areas from 70–90% to <20%. The results show that mean cliffs are 38 m tall, 55 m wide, and slope at 37°, with height and width generally increasing northward. ∼34.5% of cliffs showed no measurable cliff face retreat change, while statewide retreat averaged 0.06 m/yr and reached a maximum of 10.2 m/yr. Both cliff top and face retreat rates were highest in Northern California. The maximum erosion rate exceeded 1150 m 3 /m/yr, while the statewide mean erosion and deposition rates were 2.6 m 3 /m/yr and 0.3 m 3 /m/yr, respectively. Although taller cliffs experienced higher erosion rates, a negative trend existed between cliff face retreat rate and cliff height for cliffs <100 m. This study provides a framework for statewide cliff change monitoring for improved understanding of coastal hazards across diverse coastal settings.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Global retrieval of stokes vector of water-leaving radiance via Unet-based framework
abstract: The polarization characteristics of water-leaving radiance ( L w ) exhibit marked sensitivity to the micro-optical properties of oceanic particles, making multi-angle polarimetric observations a crucial approach for solving nonlinear, ill-posed, and underdetermined radiative transfer (RT) equations in ocean color remote sensing. However, most existing statistically optimized search-based atmospheric correction (AC) models neglect the multi-angle Stokes vector contribution of L w in retrieving polarimetric aerosol properties. In this study, a polarization-based AC model for the multi-angle Stokes vector of L w was developed using Fully Connected U-net (FUCN-AC) and global RT simulations database. And, the global spatial distribution patterns of inversion errors for the L w Stokes vector, and the impact of instrument noise on the FUCN-AC with respect to observation geometry, were systematically investigated. The results showed that the global mean absolute percentage errors (MAPEs) for the L w Stokes parameters ( I , Q , and U ), remote sensing reflectance ( R rs ), aerosol optical thicknesses (AOTs), and degree of polarization (DOP) at 490 nm were 2.24 %, 5.86 %, 6.38 %, 2.2 %, 15.94 %, and 6.06 %, respectively. The maximum MAPE for each parameter in coastal waters were mainly concentrated along the coastlines of the Eurasian continent in the Northern Hemisphere and the coastal waters of Antarctica. Additionally, field-measured polarized radiances validated the FUCN-AC model with a MAPE of 39.84 % for DOP, which might be attributed to uncorrected instrumental polarization and aerosol model mismatches. Moreover, the FUCN-AC model demonstrated significantly larger MAPE for the Stokes parameter Q and AOT at 490 nm, exceeding those for Stokes parameter I by factors of approximately 4.12 and 4.95, respectively. Furthermore, instrument noise exerted the most pronounced impact on Stokes parameter I and R rs , with the MAPEs increasing by factors of 2.54 (3.80) and 2.61 (3.90) under 3 % (5 %) noise levels, respectively. Overall, the FUCN-AC achieves the nonlinear decoupling between atmospheric and ocean polarization signals, and provides technical support for the large-scale, high-frequency dynamic monitoring of the multi-angle Stokes vector of L w .

title: A double-temperature-difference framework for anthropogenic heat flux estimation accounting for surface energy balance perturbations
abstract: Anthropogenic heat flux (AHF) is an important driver of urban climate, but its estimation is still commonly based on the assumption that anthropogenic heat is mainly expressed as sensible heat. This assumption neglects the concurrent perturbations of other surface energy balance (SEB) components and may limit the applicability of AHF estimation under different seasonal conditions. In this study, a Double Temperature Difference (DTD) framework was developed to estimate AHF from land surface temperature and near-surface air temperature responses. The framework represents AHF as the integrated response of multiple SEB perturbation pathways, including sensible heat, latent heat, net radiation, and heat storage. The framework was applied to the central urban area of Beijing using four representative seasonal cases. The estimated AHF showed distinct seasonal variability. Mean AHF reached 102.92 W m −2 in summer and 93.36 W m −2 in winter, compared with 74.57 W m −2 in spring and 60.45 W m −2 in autumn. The results also showed clear intra-urban heterogeneity. Annual mean AHF was highest in LCZ1 (95.63 W m −2 ) and lowest in LCZ3 (71.11 W m −2 ). This indicates that compactness and building intensity are important controls, but deviations among LCZ types also suggest the influence of land-use function, activity intensity, source composition, and intra-class heterogeneity. Compared with the sensible heat separation method, the DTD framework produced broadly consistent spatial patterns, with seasonal correlations ranging from 0.87 to 0.92, while reducing dependence on the sensible-heat-only assumption, particularly under winter conditions when sensible heat flux was weak. These findings indicate that AHF estimation can benefit from considering multiple SEB perturbation pathways. The proposed DTD framework provides a physically constrained and EO-supported approach for city-scale AHF mapping and can support urban climate modeling and thermal-environment assessment.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Quantifying changes in annual lichen volume for woodland caribou in Newfoundland using Landsat time series
abstract: Terrestrial and arboreal lichen are the primary winter food source of the threatened boreal ecotype of woodland caribou (Rangifer tarandus caribou). Despite its essential role, lichen biomass, a key factor of caribou habitat suitability, remains poorly quantified in forested landscapes, limiting effective habitat management and recovery planning. Our objective was to estimate lichen volume across two Newfoundland (Canada) boreal caribou herd ranges (Gros Morne and Gaff Topsails) using vegetation-specific models that integrate 1984–2022 Landsat Best Available Pixel composites with annual vegetation classifications from the National Terrestrial Ecosystem Monitoring System. Field data from 66 plots informed zero-inflated gamma models for coniferous forests, wetlands, barren land and shrublands. Predictors included spectral reflectance, vegetation indices, and vegetation type interactions. Model predictions closely matched observed lichen volume (pooled R2 = 0.77, RMSE = 8.58 dm3 m−2). Spatial outputs revealed widespread low lichen volume, with the highest volume in coniferous forests. Temporal trends showed a general increase in lichen volume since the early 1990s, with faster recovery across Gros Morne—potentially aided by the protected national park—compared to the more disturbed Gaff Topsails, where historical disturbances could have slowed early recovery. Estimated lichen biomass showed that patches reaching ~3,000 kg·ha−1—a level typical of stands preferentially used by caribou in winter—were rare but widely distributed across the landscape. These vegetation-stratified, long-term estimates of lichen volume provide a key tool for assessing habitat suitability and guiding conservation strategies aimed at supporting woodland caribou recovery across Newfoundland.

title: Baseline framework for inferring POI floors to enhance 3D urban vertical analytics: A comparative study in Shanghai
abstract: Accurate floor-level information of Points of Interest (POIs) is essential for extending urban analytics from planar to three-dimensional geospatial environments. Many studies of earth observation adopt POIs and focus on planar functional representations as well as urban morphology. However, most open POI datasets lack vertical attributes, causing incomplete semantic representations. This study proposes a baseline framework for urban POI floor inference by integrating GraphSAGE and XGBoost approaches. Using the city-wide POI dataset of Shanghai city extracted from digital map providers, 573,023 valid POIs were identified within building footprints, of which 31.1 % contained recoverable floor information. A K-nearest-neighbor spatial graph was constructed to extract localized spatial-contextual embeddings with GraphSAGE, while XGBoost served as a stand-alone model as well as a downstream regressor/classifier using GraphSAGE embeddings. Accuracy, tolerance accuracy (±1 to ±3 floors) and quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) are used for evaluating performance. Results show that XGBoost models provide strong and stable baselines, and GraphSAGE embeddings bring complementary gains. On the test dataset, a GraphSAGE-embedding–XGBoost hybrid model achieves the best ±2 tolerance accuracy (about 0.73) and QWK (about 0.75). The results demonstrate the feasibility of inferring POI floor levels from partially labeled open data using lightweight features, which can support vertical semantic enrichment for 3D urban analytics and serve as an updateable semantic enrichment module for urban digital twins, when new POI and building data become available.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: WaterPLNet: A noise-robust weakly supervised network for water extraction from SAR imagery using point labels
abstract: Existing methods for water extraction from Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery rely on labor-intensive and costly pixel-level annotations, which demand expert knowledge of SAR backscatter characteristics, significantly hindering the large-scale application of water extraction models. Although Weakly Supervised Semantic Segmentation (WSSS) can mitigate this label-dependence limitation, the label sparsity inherent in existing methods limits the accuracy of water extraction, exacerbated by speckle noise and insufficient regional spatial semantic information. To address these challenges, a noise-robust weakly supervised Network for high-precision Water extraction (WaterPLNet) from SAR imagery is proposed that leverages only Point Labels. First, a Noise-Robust Network (NRNet) with an asymmetric dual-branch structure is proposed, which enhances feature robustness and mitigates noise-induced accuracy degradation by introducing Gaussian perturbations. Second, a Prior-Guided Region Expansion (PGRE) module is designed to identify potential water regions and mitigate false negatives arising from insufficient spatial semantic information. Finally, a Low-Backscatter Ambiguity Reduction (LBAR) module is proposed to leverage point labels and low-scattering priors, thereby reducing confusion between water and similar low-backscatter land covers. Experiments conducted on three datasets of SAR images collected from the Gaofen-3 and Sentinel-1 satellites covering typical spatial resolutions (1 m, 3 m and 10 m) demonstrate that WaterPLNet reduces reliance on labeled data while achieving state-of-the-art performance compared to other WSSS approaches using point labels. Specifically, WaterPLNet achieves an overall accuracy of over 93% across all datasets, with an mIoU that outperforms other methods by an average of 5.48%. The code is publicly available at: https://github.com/Kiwi-xd/WaterPLNet .
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: SAR2LiDAR: A deep learning-based cross-modal matching framework between SAR images and LiDAR point clouds
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) and light detection and ranging (LiDAR) are two fundamental active remote sensing technologies. Their synergistic use can significantly enhance the effectiveness of remote sensing applications. However, existing studies primarily focus on product-level integration, and direct mapping between SAR images and LiDAR remains a challenge due to cross-dimensional modality differences. In this paper, a deep learning-based SAR-to-LiDAR (SAR2LiDAR) matching framework is proposed, which enables direct matching between SAR images and LiDAR point clouds. The framework features a dataset generation method that creates accurate 2D-3D correspondences between SAR images and LiDAR point clouds. It explicitly models the geometric and scattering visibility relationships of SAR imaging, and employs an autoencoder-based deep learning model with specific global feature representation and cross-modal alignment capabilities. The proposed model is trained and evaluated using airborne LiDAR datasets from five urban regions: Barcelona, Hong Kong, Los Angeles, Tarragona, and Girona. Extensive qualitative and quantitative experiments demonstrate that the proposed SAR2LiDAR framework achieves accurate and robust matching performance across diverse urban scenarios, attaining an average recall@1 of 95.64%, which significantly outperforms the best competing methods by 13%. Moreover, an average recall@1 of 91.68% on out-of-distribution (OOD) test regions demonstrates the strong generalization capability of the proposed framework and its potential for large-scale remote sensing applications.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Federated learning in forest resource modelling and monitoring: Bridging data confidentiality and collaborative research
abstract: The availability of reliable ground-truth data is one of the main bottlenecks for improving high-resolution forest attribute maps from Earth observation data. This is underpinned by the European Union (EU) Forest Strategy for 2030 that underscores the need for harmonized, cross-border forest resource assessments that integrate both remote sensing and field-based National Forest Inventory (NFI) data. However, confidentiality constraints on NFI plot coordinates present a significant barrier to aligning these datasets, thereby limiting the development of unified forest monitoring systems that can fully leverage the potential of Earth Observation data. To overcome these data-sharing limitations we explored the effectiveness of a privacy-enhancing technique, known as Federated Learning (FL), that is a form of distributed computing aimed at preserving the privacy and confidentiality of data owned by different organizations. This methodology has been tested for the collaborative modelling and mapping of forest timber volume across four European countries: Norway, Sweden, Finland, and Italy. We employed a time-series convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture tailored to integrate 40 years of Landsat or 7 years of Sentinel imagery and terrain variables with harmonized NFI data from more than 85,000 sample plots. This model architecture was used for the FL approach and compared to traditional country-specific and centralized modelling strategies. FL models achieved predictive performances comparable to the traditional models, which proofs the effectiveness of the proposed approach. Centralized or global models showed slightly reduced performance compared to the national models, highlighting the value of fine-tuning with local ground-truth data. By aligning with the EU’s forest monitoring objectives, FL facilitates the generation of harmonized models and maps of forest features, like timber volume and biomass, that are critical to support evidence-based forest policy and management. The findings underscore the potential of FL to transform collaborative environmental monitoring, particularly in domains where data confidentiality and interoperability are critical.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Multi-Criteria evaluation and ranking of 28 precipitation products over China
abstract: Multi-source precipitation products exhibit strong regional differences across China’s complex monsoon climates and pronounced topographic gradients, making single-metric evaluations insufficient for product selection. This study evaluates 28 widely used precipitation products over China from four categories: gauge-based, satellite-derived, reanalysis, and multi-source merged products. Product performance is assessed at both grid and seven major climate-zone scales using conventional error statistics, consistency metrics, ETCCDI (Expert Team on Climate Change Detection and Indices) extreme precipitation indices, precipitation detection skill, and SAL (Structure–Amplitude–Location) diagnostics for the intensity, structure, and location of heavy-rainfall events. These indicators are further synthesized within an ensemble multi-criteria decision-making framework to derive national and regional rankings. The results show that most products capture daily precipitation variability reasonably well, but intense rainfall events remain associated with widespread amplitude underestimation and enlarged errors, while extremes also exhibit notable structural distortion and location bias. At the national scale, multi-source merged generally show greater overall robustness. Regional rankings further reveal strong spatial heterogeneity: arid zones and some humid regions tend to favor reanalysis-type products, whereas plateau regions show higher sensitivity to satellite products and greater ranking uncertainty. Overall, this study provides a transparent and application-oriented framework for integrated precipitation product evaluation and ranking over China. The resulting national and climate-zone-specific rankings offer practical guidance for precipitation product selection, candidate-pool construction for multi-source merging, and hydrometeorological risk analyses.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Stratified and adaptive regression for NDVI-based land surface temperature downscaling over agricultural fields
abstract: Improving the spatial resolution of thermal imagery is essential for agricultural field management, especially in developing countries where fields are fragmented and heterogeneous. The existing downscale land surface temperature (LST) products are a promising solution while awaiting for further advances in satellite-based thermal sensors. In this study, a linear regression-based approach was proposed to downscale LST from 1 km to 10 m spatial resolution. The proposed method is hereafter referred to as Stratified and Adaptive Regression for Land Surface Temperature Downscaling (STAR-LST). Taking advantage of the linearity between LST and NDVI under homogeneous conditions, multiple linear regression models were first derived for different regions in the (LST, NDVI) feature space at coarse resolution. These regions were defined by partitioning the triangular form of the (LST, NDVI) feature space into sub-triangles, sharing a common top vertex. Each model is then applied to the corresponding NDVI range, allowing thus to derive LST at finer resolution. LST estimates were validated against in-situ measurements collected over olive trees, Kernza, wheat, and barley. Good results were obtained with RMSE values ranging from 2.79 to 4.49 °C for STAR-LST. This presents an improvement of an average of 33 % compared to the two classical methods DisTrad and TsHARP (RMSE in the range 4.18–6.83 °C), which showed similar accuracy. In addition, STAR-LST enabled daily LST estimation whenever coarse-resolution data were available, using interpolated NDVI to generate a high spatio-temporal LST product suitable for managing agricultural fields, particularly the small size fields.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: LiDAR-based assessment of treetop dieback to detect asian longhorned beetle damage in poplar forests
abstract: Effective forest management depends on accurately monitoring changes in forest health. The Asian longhorned beetle (ALB) has caused extensive mortality in broadleaf trees worldwide. ALB typically manifests as a distinctive treetop-dieback phenotype that progresses downward in damaged trees. Although LiDAR is widely used for plant-stress detection, two challenges persist: (1) non-specific structural responses that hinder the identification of damage-specific phenotypes and (2) limited transferability of structural metrics across age- and size-heterogeneous stands. We address these challenges with a within-tree ratio-based framework that targets the treetop-dieback phenotype with internal normalization. Two poplar plots (young, old) were selected to represent age- and size-related heterogeneity. Based on field evidence (oviposition pits, frass holes, exit holes), each tree was labeled as healthy, lightly damaged, or severely damaged. For each tree, we vertically segmented the point cloud at 50% and 80% of total height and computed crown volume (V), point density (PD), and leaf area index (LAI) of each segment. We then derived upper-to-lower ratio metrics, using the lower crown as an internal normalizer, to capture top-down dieback while normalizing size- and age-related heterogeneity. We also defined a family of combination ratios that aggregate ratios at 50% and 80% heights. Using Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA), we evaluated separability of each metric under two strategies: (1) a 70/30 random split by trees and (2) a plot-transfer test (train: Stand young ; test: Stand old ). The results indicated that the proposed metrics, Summary Ratio of Volume (SRV = V u p p e r 50 % V l o w e r 50 % + V u p p e r 20 % V l o w e r 80 % ), achieved the highest overall accuracy (OA): 76.23% in random split, and 70.58% in plot-transfer, significantly outperforming other proposed metrics and existing LiDAR indices. By coupling phenotype-focused features with internal normalization, the approach enables precise detection of treetop dieback and improves transferability across age and size heterogeneity.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: A machine learning framework for predicting agricultural terrace suitability using positive and unlabelled datasets: an application for the Troodos Mountains, Cyprus
abstract: Terraces are a defining feature of Mediterranean mountain landscapes, enabling agriculture on steep slopes while providing multiple ecosystem services. Land suitability analysis (LSA) can guide authorities and land users to sustainably manage and expand these environments. It typically requires fully labelled datasets, but in many real-world applications only a fraction of positive examples is available, with the rest unlabelled. This study aims to present an integrated predictive modelling framework that combines GIS with data-driven Machine Learning (ML) techniques, capable of learning from Positive and Unlabelled (PU) datasets for LSA. The proposed framework was applied to develop a terrace suitability map for Cyprus’ Troodos Mountains. A 5-m DEM was processed to extract the mountain area, with elevation ≥ 500 m and slopes ≥ 15%, defining the study area. Crop plots registered under the Single Area Payment Scheme of the European Common Agricultural Policy were used to classify the study area into Terrace-Present (TP) and Terrace-Absent (TA) cells, with TP serving as labelled positive and TA as unlabelled samples. A two-step ML approach was applied, first identifying reliable negatives from TA cells, then using these with TP cells for suitability prediction. The developed PU-classifier was evaluated under the selected completely-at-random (SCAR) assumption, achieving a Recall of 84.6%, Precision of 81.5% and an F1 score of 83%. Feature importance analysis identified land cover, terrain slope and tree cover density as the most influential parameters for terrace suitability. Comparative analysis between 2017 and 2024 revealed abandonment of terraced agricultural land (29% decrease) as well as revitalisation (12% increase). The resulting suitability map and accompanying data layers are accessible through a Google Earth Engine application, aiming to support informed decision-making for sustainable landscape planning.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: A novel edge-based accuracy assessment framework for target detection from remotely sensed images
abstract: Accuracy assessment is critical for evaluating map quality and improving algorithms for target detection in remotely sensed images. Traditional methods for assessing a target-detection task were often performed by estimating the relative areas of correct and incorrect identifications (e.g., F1 score). However, this approach only considers the pixel-by-pixel agreement and ignores important aspects of positional errors and target object quality. To provide comprehensive diagnostic information, we propose a novel edge-based accuracy assessment framework. This framework firstly applied a newly proposed assessment tool, Dynamic Epsilon-band Accuracy Function (DEAF), which is a linear fitting function from a series of edge accuracies associated with expanded buffers on the object edges, and then extracted the level-off and the middle point from the DEAF curve respectively to derive edge-based accuracy metrics and to assess thematic and positional error components. We presented an experiment on synthetic maps to reveal that the new edge-based accuracy metrics better reflects under- and over-segmentation errors compared to traditional measurements (e.g., F1 score, over-/under-segmentation indices). Moreover, we applied the new framework for two practical target-detection tasks, agricultural fields and building rooftops. The results demonstrate the two innovative aspects of the edge-based framework, which are that it provides: 1) a more rigorous assessment of object quality, and 2) error attribution for both thematic and positional errors. The proposed framework therefore provides a new capability for assessing the accuracy of target detection maps, which is of vital importance for evaluating and improving state-of-the-art remote sensing products.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Simulating potential landward migration pattern of mangrove wetlands under the ‘two-way squeeze’ from sea level rise and human activities
abstract: Mangroves play critical roles in carbon sequestration, biodiversity conservation, and coastal protection. However, they face growing threats from a ‘two-way squeeze’ driven by sea level rise (SLR) under climate change and intensive human activities. To address this, we developed a multi-scenario assessment framework based on the Sea Level Affecting Marsh Model (SLAMM) that integrates high-resolution DEM, land-use dynamics, and regional hydrological parameters. This framework was employed to simulate mangrove migration and habitat loss under Representative Concentration Pathway (RCP) and Shared Socioeconomic Pathway (SSP)-based scenarios, enabling a quantitative evaluation of anthropogenic impacts (e.g., seawall barriers and land-use constraints) against baseline SLR projections. Results indicate that mangrove loss will range from 16 % to 23 % by 2050 and 15 % to 49 % by 2100. During this period, mangroves are projected to primarily migrate toward inland freshwater and saltwater wetlands, exhibiting minimal conversion to dry land. The stability of mangrove expansion is highly contingent upon sediment availability, with sediment-starved areas demonstrating pronounced vulnerability. Notably, anthropogenic structures, particularly seawalls, significantly hinder landward migration by blocking physical pathways and reducing sediment deposition (critical for vertical accretion). Consequently, our simulations reveal that 14.88 % of the projected mangrove loss is directly attributable to the spatial constraints imposed by these seawalls. To mitigate these impacts, targeted strategies to enhance mangrove resilience are further proposed: (1) reducing seawall-induced barriers via ecological modification to restore sediment supply; (2) controlling coastal development to maintain migration corridors; and (3) supporting sediment accumulation to sustain vertical adaptation, effectively addressing the dual stressors of SLR and human interference. These measures are imperative for maintaining mangrove ecological functions, supporting biodiversity, and sustaining coastal resilience under climate change.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Multi-source complementary feature self-integration network for geological lithology interpretation
abstract: Geological lithology interpretation in multi-source remote sensing imagery still faces challenges due to the spatial heterogeneity of multi-source features and the fragmented spatial distribution of geological elements. To address these issues, we propose the complementary feature self-integration network (CFSI-Net), a unified framework for multi-source feature fusion and lithology interpretation. To mitigate spatial heterogeneity in multi-source features, we developed the cross-domain feature extraction and fusion module (CDFEFM), a dual-branch structure that adaptively extracts and fuses complementary features across channels while reducing redundant lithology information. Furthermore, we introduced the frequency-spatial feature integration module (FSFIM) and a segmentation module (SegM) to alleviate the problem of boundary ambiguity in segmentation. FSFIM captures boundary structural details and spatial contextual dependencies from the frequency and spatial domains, whereas SegM further refines spatial dependencies across channels, enriching textural details and enhancing the discrimination of adjacent elements. Experimental results on the CUG-LithXZ dataset demonstrate that CFSI-Net consistently outperforms state-of-the-art models, achieving an OA of 80.13% and mIoU of 66.18% in Geo-GZ, and an OA of 72.49% and mIoU of 50.26% in Geo-LZ. These results confirm that the synergistic utilization of frequency and spatial information provides richer details for accurate geological lithology interpretation in complex terrains.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Mapping the extent, type and remnant areas of the coastal dunes of Australia and New Zealand by integrating multi-source data
abstract: Accurate large-scale mapping of coastal dune types is critical for coastal management but remains challenging due to the dunes’ high spatial heterogeneity and the spectral complexity in coastal environments. Therefore, this study aims to develop a coastal dune mapping approach and demonstrate its applicability across Australia and New Zealand. Firstly, we leveraged geological maps to delineate the spatial extent of coastal dune fields, effectively masking out non-dune areas. Secondly, we applied an object-based image analysis (OBIA), followed by a random forest classifier that integrated multi-source features to classify six coastal dune types within the delineated coastal dune fields, including active dunes, foredunes, sandy beaches, semi-stabilized dunes, stabilized dunes, and wetlands (dune slacks). Based on this approach, we generated a 10 m fine classification map of coastal dune types across Australia and New Zealand, covering a total area of 27,564 km 2 . Accuracy assessment yielded an overall classification accuracy of 90.68 %. Most categories achieved satisfactory performance, with stabilized dunes showing the highest accuracy (96.81 %). We also found that approximately 498 km 2 of coastal dune area has been converted to urban development land. However, this development pressure was mitigated by conservation efforts, as 15,781.80 km 2 (59.44 %) of the total coastal dune area was situated within protected areas. This study provides a replicable methodology for large-scale fine classification of coastal dune types. The resulting map offers scientific support for monitoring coastal dune systems state and evolution under human intervention.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Geomorphology-constrained bathymetric inversion of turbid tidal channels using centerline-network priors and machine learning
abstract: Bathymetric inversion in turbid tidal channels remains challenging because of degraded bottom-related optical signals and complex-branched channel networks. This study investigates whether geomorphic structure can act as a stable prior for bathymetric reconstruction when the spectral-depth relationship breaks down. We develop a geomorphology-constrained framework that integrates UAV multispectral imagery, suspended sediment concentration, RTK-derived channel depths, and adjacent flat DEM constraints. A branching centerline network is first extracted to characterize channel organization, from which geometric and network-structural predictors, including normalized width, width-to-depth ratio, downstream accumulation, tributary order, and distance to junctions, are derived and used to construct a random-forest depth prior. Then, these predictors are refined through constrained optimization with anisotropic smoothing along channel directions and boundary consistency with exposed terrain. The framework is tested in a turbid tidal-channel system along the southern Yellow Sea and further evaluated through a transfer experiment in the Yangtze Estuary. Among all predictors, the width-to-depth ratio provides the greatest improvement in inversion accuracy, reducing RMSE from 0.30 m to 0.18 m (38 %), highlighting the dominantly geomorphological control on channel cross-sectional geometry. Overall, The provided framework achieves RMSE values of 0.15 m (RTK-based) and 0.23 m (DEM-based), outperforming empirical spectral, conventional machine-learning, and deep-learning approaches, particularly in scour zones, narrow tributaries, and channel confluences. In the Yangtze Estuary, the model attains an RMSE of 3.46 m (R 2 = 0.70), suggesting preliminary transferability across more than three orders (from ∼ 10 m to 10 km) of magnitude in channel scale. The results show that the main bottleneck in turbid tidal-channel inversion is not only optical degradation, but also the lack of geomorphic organization in model design. By coupling data-driven learning with structural and boundary constraints, this study advances a transferable inversion paradigm for optically complex coastal environments.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Feasibility of space-borne remote sensing to detect features related to CO2 and N2O exchange of boreal agricultural fields
abstract: We explored the applicability of microwave satellite observations to characterize the carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) exchange processes in boreal agricultural fields for three regions in Finland. The sites under investigation included two grassland fields on mineral soil and one on peat soil. We evaluated whether the space-borne microwave radiometer data-derived information on freeze–thaw, snow accumulation and snow melt obtained at a landscape scale is useful in explaining carbon and nitrogen exchange processes at daily temporal and field scale spatial resolutions. Specifically, we focused on the annual balance and seasonal behaviour of CO 2 exchange, and the feasibility of microwave observations in explaining the observed nitrous oxide (N 2 O) emission rates from a peatland field. Additionally, the feasibility of space-borne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data to support observation time series of optical satellite data on a field block level was investigated for the growing season. The results indicate the potential of space-borne microwave observations to provide information useful in assessing CO 2 exchange and N 2 O bursts from boreal agricultural fields. The results show that seasonal changes due to climate and management, detectable on a landscape scale from space-borne microwave radiometry, significantly contribute to the annual balance of CO 2 exchange of boreal fields. The results also suggest that SAR data can potentially be used to fill cloud cover induced gaps in leaf area index (LAI) time series available from optical-range satellite imaging, improving the usefulness of satellite data in the monitoring of field management. Results show that landscape-scale freeze–thaw and snow cover information derived from space-borne SMOS and SSMI/S observations distinguishes seasonal periods with distinct CO 2 exchange characteristics, indicating the potential of coarse-resolution microwave radiometer data to constrain carbon exchange models of boreal agricultural fields outside the summertime growing season. Further, C-band Sentinel-1 SAR backscatter observations were found to correlate significantly with GPP dynamics and enable detection of harvesting events, suggesting that combined SAR and radiometer time series can support year-round agricultural monitoring.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Spatiotemporal fusion of radar backscatter for enhanced monitoring of surface melt dynamics over Antarctic ice shelves
abstract: Surface meltwater over the Antarctic Ice Sheet acts as a primary modulator of the polar energy budget, potentially triggering ice shelf collapse and exerting far-reaching impacts on the global climate system. Radar scatterometers enable daily melt detection but at coarse resolution, whereas Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) achieves fine spatial detail with limited temporal coverage. Spatiotemporal fusion methods present a viable solution to balance this trade-off, but these approaches are applied only to optical remote sensing and have not yet been successfully adapted to radar backscatter data. In this study, we propose the Spatiotemporal Radar Backscatter Data Fusion (SRBDF) method, a multi-source C-band active microwave data fusion technique that can integrate Sentinel-1 and Advanced Scatterometer (ASCAT) observations. SRBDF generates a high-resolution daily backscatter dataset for monitoring surface melt dynamics at the Larsen C and George VI Ice Shelves throughout 2018–2021 melt seasons. The fused dataset preserves spatial details from Sentinel-1, while maintaining the daily frequency of ASCAT. Across the Larsen C and George VI Ice Shelves, SRBDF melt/freeze detection shows overall consistency approaching or above 0.90 with Sentinel-1 and ASCAT. High-resolution daily observations reveal an extreme melt season during 2019–2020, when melt occurrence was more than 50 % above the previous season. Pronounced melt was observed on Larsen C and George VI ice shelves driven by foehn winds and sustained warm air advection from low-speed northerly winds, respectively. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of SRBDF in capturing Antarctic ice shelf surface melt variability and its potential for broader applications in polar surface process research.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: C2D2: Matching UAV images with cycle-consistency and channel-separation for joint detector and descriptor
abstract: Accurate feature matching in Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) imagery is fundamental to earth observation applications. Although jointly learning keypoint detectors and descriptors has become standard practice, existing methods face inherent challenges: keypoint repeatability and descriptor reliability optimize for different visual properties, while patch-based training losses impose locality constraints that limit global geometric consistency. This paper presents C2D2, a network that addresses these limitations through two key innovations. First, a Channel Separation Module (CSM) reduces cross-task interference by enabling task-specific channel emphasis. Second, a cycle consistency loss enforces global geometric constraints beyond local patches, enhancing descriptor robustness with minimal additional training overhead. Extensive evaluation on public benchmarks and a challenging UAV dataset demonstrates improvements on most evaluated metrics: 4.4% higher detector repeatability on HPatches and up to 7.3% improvement in localization recall on the Aachen Day–Night benchmark. These results , achieved with only 0.49M parameters, establish C2D2 as an efficient solution within the sparse feature learning family for demanding remote sensing applications.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: A SIF-Constrained Noah-MP land surface model for simulating water use efficiency and drought Resilience: Application in a Semi-Arid Basin
abstract: Land surface models (LSMs) systematically overestimate evapotranspiration (ET) in water-limited ecosystems due to inadequate representation of plant physiological water stress, undermining reliable water resource projections. We introduce a novel, mechanistic integration of solar-induced fluorescence (SIF) directly into the Ball-Berry stomatal resistance scheme of WRF-Hydro/Noah-MP. In the absence of eddy covariance flux tower measurements within the basin, model evaluation is conducted through inter-comparison with multiple independent gridded reference products (MODIS, GLEAM, GLDAS), and results are interpreted as physically consistent shifts in model behaviour rather than validated improvements in absolute accuracy. The methodology is designed to be transferable, relying only on publicly available SIF products and the widely used Noah–MP model. We developed a self-calibrating SIF factor (0–1) from GOSIF v2 to modulate the net photosynthesis rate, thereby coupling observed photosynthetic activity to stomatal resistance and transpiration. This SIF-enhanced model was applied to the Awash Basin, Ethiopia (2000–2024), and evaluated through inter-comparison with MODIS, GLEAM, and GLDAS. SIF integration increases consistency with the multi–product ensemble: mean annual ET decreased by 36.1 % (from 8.45 to 5.40 mm day⁻ 1 , p < 0.001), thereby reducing the ET discrepancy relative to the ensemble of satellite–based reference products (with α = 0.10 calibrated for this basin). The transpiration fraction of ET increased most during the critical dry season (+7.0 %, p < 0.001), reflecting more realistic water-conservation behaviour. Consequently, Water Use Efficiency (WUE) increased under both normal and drought conditions, and the SIF-constrained Model showed substantially smaller WUE losses during drought than the Control (a 5 % decline versus a 13 % decline, respectively), consistent with a more water-conservative stomatal strategy that reduces transpiration by a greater proportion than photosynthesis under stress. This simulated response aligns with observed plant behaviour in water-limited ecosystems, yielding a drought resilience index of 0.95, compared with 0.87 for the Control. Monthly flux correlations confirmed strong carbon–water coupling (GPP-ET r = 0.93), while annual-scale analysis revealed a developing trade-off in which high-productivity years were least efficient (WUE-ET r = -0.88). Furthermore, unsupervised clustering of SIF-constrained WUE and resilience outputs yielded the first physiologically based agroecological zonation of the basin. We identified four distinct functional zones, including a productive but drought-vulnerable core (21,425 km 2 , WUE = 2.49 g C kg⁻ 1 H 2 O) and resilient but inefficient lowlands (8,175 km 2 , WUE = 0.05 g C kg⁻ 1 H 2 O). This scalable SIF-informed physiological constraint framework reduces a structural LSM bias, yielding more credible ecohydrological projections and providing dynamic, plant-informed targets for climate-resilient land and water planning.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Time-series framework integrating rainfall and satellite soil moisture for multi-scale urban flood risk assessment
abstract: Urban floods are increasing as localized extreme rainfall intensifies under climate change and impervious surfaces expand with urbanization. However, pre-event hydro-surface conditions that govern runoff generation remain difficult to quantify. This study proposes a time-series framework that integrates hourly rainfall data from the Korea Meteorological Administration and 3-hourly NASA SMAP Level 4 soil moisture data for eight urban flood events in Korea since 2020. The flood potential index (FPI) is defined as the sum of standardized indicators representing short-term rainfall intensity, antecedent rainfall, root-zone soil moisture, and dynamic imperviousness. Dynamic imperviousness was estimated from the time-lag relationship between the surface and root-zone soil moisture to capture the time-varying infiltration-response conditions beyond static land cover assumptions. Data were analyzed over a − 14 to + 1 day window relative to each event. The FPI time series was computed for 27 combinations of short-term rainfall (1, 3, and 6 h), antecedent rainfall (1, 3, and 5 days), and lag time (3, 6, and 9 h) to evaluate the duration above the top 95% threshold, peak intensity ratio, and lead time. Longer rainfall windows increased persistence, whereas shorter windows with a 3-day antecedent rainfall enhanced relative amplification. The proposed framework provides an interpretable, satellite-informed basis for hydro-surface risk screening rather than a standalone flood prediction model.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Referring Remote Sensing Image Segmentation method based on Scene-Aware Guided Network model
abstract: Referring Remote Sensing Image Segmentation (RRSIS) aims to achieve accurate segmentation of objects in remote sensing images under the guidance of natural language expression. However, existing RRSIS approaches are limited to pixel-level cognitive abilities, failing to effectively handle the diverse geographical features inherent in remote sensing imagery, which significantly impairs their segmentation performance across different geographical scenes. To address this issue, this article proposes a Scene-Aware Guided Network (SAGNet) model. The proposed SAGNet incorporates a Scene-Contextual Text Guided (SCTG) module that integrates scene understanding, text-guided enhancement, and frequency domain processing to leverage scene understanding for achieving more complete and accurate segmentation across different geographical scenes with varying land cover characteristics, and a Context-Rich Adaptive Feature Transform (CRAFT) module that dynamically generates frequency domain filters to capture distinctive textural and spatial patterns, enhance global context modeling, and improve cross-scene feature representation for complex remote sensing imagery. To extend RRSIS applications, we construct a new remote sensing referring segmentation dataset named LandRef containing 14,391 image-caption-mask triplets across diverse geographical environments. Experimental evaluation on RefSegRS, RRSIS-D, and LandRef datasets reveals that the proposed SAGNet method consistently outperforms existing RRSIS approaches. By utilizing scene cognition to guide semantic expression adaptation in diverse scenarios, SAGNet achieves mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) improvements ranging from 0.79% to 3.76% across all three datasets. The dataset and code are available at https://github.com/taloen920/SAGNet.git .
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: A two-stage machine learning framework for Chl-a reconstruction and short-term prediction in eutrophic lakes using GOCI observations
abstract: Harmful algal blooms (HABs) in eutrophic lakes threaten aquatic ecosystems and public health, but short-term chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) prediction remains challenging because satellite observations are often discontinuous and bloom dynamics are regulated by interacting environmental and ecological factors. This study developed a two-stage Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) framework for satellite-derived Chl-a reconstruction and short-term prediction in Lake Taihu. The first-stage model (XGBoost_Interp) reconstructed Chl-a on dates without valid GOCI/GOCI-II retrievals and generated a continuous daily Chl-a series for 2011–2024, achieving good performance (R 2 = 0.83, RMSE = 5.72 μg/L, MAPE = 9.16%). Using the reconstructed series and environmental variables, the second-stage model (XGBoost_Pred) predicted subsequent Chl-a with comparable accuracy (R 2 = 0.83, RMSE = 5.62 μg/L, MAPE = 8.97%). However, independent validation from January to March 2025 showed lower accuracy (R 2 = 0.69, RMSE = 9.45 μg/L) and some overestimation, suggesting that further calibration and evaluation are still needed when valid satellite observations are unavailable for extended periods. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) identified wind speed, temperature, atmospheric pressure, day of year, and antecedent Chl-a as important predictors. After lake-specific recalibration, the framework also performed well in Lake Chaohu, indicating its practical potential for other large eutrophic lakes. Nevertheless, broader application requires further validation with nutrient-related variables, multi-sensor data, high-frequency field observations, and more lakes with different environmental conditions.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Reproducible mapping of marine biodiversity using autonomous surface vehicles and deep learning
abstract: Monitoring shallow-water marine ecosystems requires precise, low-cost and reproducible methods, yet traditional diver-based surveys are labor-intensive, subject to observer bias and limited in spatial coverage. In this study, we present an autonomous framework that integrates deep learning techniques with open-source data acquisition platforms to overcome these challenges. Our approach uses a transformer-based model to classify different coral morphotypes, seagrass species and benthic habitats. This model is trained on the publicly available Seatizen Atlas image dataset . Data were collected using low-cost autonomous surface vehicles (ASVs) equipped with action cameras, differential GNSS receivers, single-beam echosounders and inertial measurement units. The ASVs provide precise geolocation, depth and attitude measurements, synchronized with image timestamps and embedded as standardized metadata, ensuring interoperability and reproducibility. Beyond image classification, the ASVs enable bathymetric surveys and photogrammetric reconstruction for three-dimensional mapping of surveyed areas. Field validation at Réunion Island and Aldabra Atoll demonstrates that this framework delivers cost-effective, non-invasive and standardized monitoring, while automating laborious annotation tasks and increasing survey scalability. By combining open-source datasets, AI models and versatile ASV functionalities, this methodology supports reproducible ecological assessments and informs conservation decisions.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Label-efficient mapping of unregulated waste dumps via mixed supervision with feature masked recovery
abstract: Mapping unregulated solid waste dumps from remote sensing imagery is important for environmental risk assessment and sustainable development monitoring, but remains constrained by the high cost of pixel-level annotation.
