Weakly supervised semantic segmentation (WSSS) with image-level labels reduces annotation effort, yet often suffers from incomplete object activation, especially for waste dumps with irregular morphology, variable object scales, and visually confusing backgrounds. To address this problem, we propose a label-efficient mixed-supervision framework that uses image-level labels as semantic regularization and a small fraction of pixel-level masks as spatial anchors. The framework adopts an asymmetric design: the semantic learning stream regularizes backbone representations during training, while the spatial grounding stream learns the final segmentation path. During inference, the auxiliary semantic stream is removed, enabling direct segmentation without CAM-to-pseudo-label refinement or separate segmentation-network retraining. Within the semantic learning stream, the proposed SAM-FMR module combines an adopted Slice-and-Merge (SAM) strategy with Feature Masked Recovery (FMR). SAM preserves local details through slice-level processing, whereas FMR applies structured masking in the high-level feature space to encourage context-aware feature learning and more spatially distributed semantic responses. The framework further provides modular interfaces for interchangeable CAM-based weak-supervision modules and backbone-adaptive segmentation heads. Experiments on the newly constructed YREB dataset and the enhanced Global Dumpsite benchmark show that the proposed method improves over few-shot, pure weakly supervised, and semi-supervised label-efficient baselines under spatially independent validation, cross-dataset transfer, and conventional patch-level benchmarks. With only 1% pixel-level annotations, it reaches nearly 90% of the same-framework fully supervised reference, demonstrating a favorable trade-off between dense-annotation cost and segmentation performance. The datasets and source code are publicly available.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: BLB_TVI: A hyperspectral triangular index for satellite-scale characterization of rice bacterial leaf blight severity
abstract: Bacterial leaf blight (BLB) is among the most destructive rice diseases in Asia. Although hyperspectral remote sensing has shown strong potential for crop disease detection, most existing studies focus on leaf-, canopy-, or UAV-scale disease assessment, and a BLB-specific hyperspectral index for satellite-scale severity characterization remains lacking. To address this gap, we developed a BLB-specific hyperspectral triangular vegetation index (BLB_TVI) from Zhuhai-1 imagery within a cross-scale framework integrating ground survey data and UAV observations. A satellite-pixel-consistent severity reference, termed the Rice Bacterial Leaf Blight Index (RBLBI), was constructed within this framework to bridge the mismatch between field observations and 10 m satellite pixels. The NDVI-based UAV classification achieved high accuracy, and the derived RBLBI was strongly correlated with the ground-based disease index (DI) (R 2 = 0.76). Among the tested indices, the optimal BLB_TVI, defined by the 686, 806, and 880 nm bands, showed the strongest relationship with RBLBI (R 2 = 0.77) and remained strongly associated with DI (R 2 = 0.73). In an independent cross-year and cross-site dataset collected in 2025, BLB_TVI also maintained a strong association with DI (R 2 = 0.70), indicating promising transferability. These results indicate that BLB_TVI provides an interpretable hyperspectral approach for satellite-scale BLB severity characterization.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Individual urban street tree detection and species-level mapping from street-view images and GIS data
abstract: Accurate urban street tree recognition is crucial for ecological management. Street-view images offer a unique pedestrian perspective, capturing details often missed by remote sensing imagery. Current street tree recognition methods using street-view images are limited by scarce labeled data and high manual annotation costs. To address these challenges, we propose a novel urban street tree recognition and mapping method that enables accurate instance-level mapping of street trees. The method supports species identification where sufficient visual distinction exists. First, we design a two-stage street tree recognition method. In stage one, an object detection model is used to extract individual tree regions from street-view images, decoupling tree detection from species classification. In stage two, tree species are classified using a model pre-trained on open-source tree species datasets and fine-tuned with web-sourced labeled images, achieving annotation cost reduction. Second, StreetTreeMapper reduces duplicate detections by integrating street-view image features with OpenStreetMap’s geographic constraints, achieving precise tree instance mapping. To validate our proposed method, we construct a street tree dataset from New York, Zhuhai, and Seoul. Experimental results validate the overall effectiveness of our proposed method in both tree recognition and mapping. Through decoupled detection and classification, our method achieves a 2.7% to 11.4% increase in average precision compared to state-of-the-art models on Zhuhai datasets. The StreetTreeMapper achieves instance-level tree mapping with median errors of 4.5 m (New York), 4.8 m (Seoul), and 2.9 m (Zhuhai), reaching minimum observed localization errors of 0.21 m, 0.13 m, and less than 0.001 m, respectively. Our method enables automated detection and species identification of street trees. These capabilities provide valuable data support and decision-making foundations for smart city development and sustainable ecological maintenance.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Spatiotemporal bias in OCO-2 XCO2 retrievals relative to TCCON observations
abstract: Accurate monitoring of atmospheric CO₂ concentrations is essential for understanding carbon dynamics and informing climate-mitigation strategies. This study examines the seasonal variability of satellite-based XCO2 retrievals from NASA's OCO-2 mission relative to ground-based TCCON XCO2 measurements over ten years (2014-2024) across 17 global TCCON sites. The study distinguished between two satellite observation modes, nadir and glint, and assessed how seasonal variations in satellite-derived environmental parameters – normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI), soil surface moisture (SSM), land-surface temperature (LST), and evapotranspiration (ET) – relate to statistical characteristics of the XCO₂ bias. In addition, we evaluated the temporal dynamics of the bias across the dominant land-cover types surrounding each site. Our results identify a latitude-dependent bias in nadir retrievals across Northern Hemisphere sites, with strong associations between nadir bias and land-cover at TCCON sites located > 45°N (R2 = 0.95) and between 0-45°N (R2 = 0.78). This work provides novel insights into the temporal dynamics of satellite XCO2 bias relative to ground measurements and demonstrates distinct behaviors across observation modes that have not been reported previously. These findings are crucial for improving the accuracy of global CO2 mapping and for strengthening the reliability of carbon flux models.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: A high-resolution interchange classification model enhanced by multi-scale geometric structural feature fusion
abstract: High-accuracy classification of interchange structures from remote sensing imagery is crucial for urban transportation planning, intelligent transportation systems, and autonomous driving technologies. However, current research on classifying high-resolution remote sensing images of interchanges remains limited, particularly due to the lack of dedicated high-resolution datasets. In addition, existing GIS databases often suffer from incompleteness, lack of structural semantic labels, and limited timeliness, motivating the need for automated interchange classification from remote sensing imagery. To address this issue, this study constructs a high-resolution interchange classification dataset (HRIC dataset) using Gaofen-2 and Jilin-1 satellite imagery with a spatial resolution of 0.5–0.75 m. The dataset covers six common types of urban interchanges, including cloverleaf interchange, diamond interchange, roundabout interchange, T-interchange, trumpet interchange, and turbine interchange. Based on this dataset, we evaluate the performance of multiple deep learning models on the interchange classification task and propose a structural feature–enhanced classification framework tailored for accurate interchange recognition. The framework incorporates core structural modeling concepts from the StarInterchange module into the ResNet18 backbone to strengthen structural feature representation, while integrating the ELA attention mechanism to enhance sensitivity to local features. Experimental results demonstrate that the optimized model achieves strong performance in identifying various interchange structures, reaching an overall classification accuracy of 79.10%. This study provides an effective method for the automatic recognition and analysis of complex transportation infrastructure and lays a foundation for future research on road segmentation and topological structure extraction.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: From flood extent mapping to mechanism-aware flood products: integrating flood type classification into satellite-based flood monitoring
abstract: Flood type information is critical for effective flood risk management because dominant flood types are associated with distinct hydrodynamic behaviour, contamination pathways, and recovery trajectories. However, most operational flood mapping products provide only binary inundation extent, offering limited information for interpreting the dominant flood type and its likely impact characteristics. Existing flood type classification approaches rely predominantly on hydrometeorological observations and modelling, which are often unavailable in data-scarce regions and can be unstable in mechanism-complex environments such as estuarine deltas, urban river corridors, and coastal cities. To address these limitations, this study proposes a multi-CNN framework that integrates flood type classification directly into satellite-based flood mapping. The framework first uses a U-Net model for flood extent segmentation and then applies a CNN-based classifier for scene-level flood type identification by combining satellite imagery with auxiliary topographic and hydrological-context features, including DEM information and water connectivity ratios. Several CNN architectures were compared for flood type classification, with Inception-ResNet selected based on its performance–complexity trade-offs. To support model training and evaluation, this study introduces the World Flood Type (WFT) dataset, a new multi-event flood dataset containing 464 flood scenes from 120 flood events across 48 countries. Results show effective performance in both inundation segmentation and flood type classification. The U-Net model achieved 83.8% overall accuracy on an independent test dataset, while the final Inception-ResNet-based classifier achieved 93.0% scene-level overall accuracy and a scene-level macro-F1 score of 0.73 under dominant-mechanism conditions. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of extending conventional flood extent products with scene-level attribution of dominant flood types using remotely sensed imagery and ancillary geospatial data, thereby providing more decision-relevant information for emergency response and post-disaster assessment.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: The impacts of cover crop biomass on satellite-based detectability of cover crops in Maryland
abstract: Cover crop adoption in the U.S. has increased over the past decades, increasing the need to quantify their performance and environmental benefits. While remote sensing (RS)-based approaches for detecting cover crop presence have been developed, there has been limited research on how cover crops with varied biomass and management practices influence detectability. Using unique field-level cover crop presence and biomass datasets in Maryland, U.S., we investigated how RS-based detectability changes for cover crops with varied aboveground biomass, planting, and termination dates. Specifically, we proposed a time-integrated satellite-based greenness feature from Harmonized Landsat-8 and Sentinel-2 (HLS) time series from 2017 to 2021 to estimate biomass of cover crops and evaluated their detectability using a phenology-based cover crop detection framework. The impacts of cover crop planting and termination dates on cover crop biomass were also analyzed. Our results demonstrated that Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) estimated biomass with higher accuracy compared to other vegetation indices, and the time-integrated model estimated biomass with higher accuracy than the single-date “snapshot” linear model (R 2 from 0.53 to 0.66 and RMSE from 922 kg/ha to 747 kg/ha). While the snapshot models were species sensitive, the time-integrated models showed strong robustness across different species. Detectability increased with cover crop biomass, as detected cover crops averaged 963.3 ± 719.5 kg/ha compared to 297.2 ± 209.0 kg/ha for non-detected cover crops. Detection accuracy reached 96.1% for fields exceeding 500 kg/ha, compared with an overall accuracy of 62.7%. Earlier planting and later termination increased biomass and detectability, with biomass rising by 4.14 kg/ha/day (p < 0.01). This study demonstrates how management practices affect cover crop biomass and detectability via satellite time series and provides insights that can inform management of cover crops and monitoring of their effects on agroecosystems.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Satellite evidence of reduced resistance and resilience to water stress after antecedent fire across a rainfall gradient in northern Australia
abstract: As the climate warms, fire and water stress are becoming more frequent and intense, making interactions between them more likely. While controlled field experiments in forests suggested that low-severity burns can influence drought responses, these findings may not apply to fire-prone savannas and shrublands, where large, variable-intensity fires and recurrent water stress dominate. Therefore, landscape-scale effects of fire on ecosystem responses to water stress in these savannas and shrublands remain poorly understood. Here, we focused on the North Australian Tropical Transect (NATT), where fire and water-stress events occur frequently across a 1,600 mm rainfall gradient spanning mesic woody savannas to semi-arid grasslands, and arid shrublands. Water-stress events were classified as fire-affected when fire occurred either during the water-stress period or within a 12-month antecedent window, and as fire-free otherwise. Ecosystem responses were quantified using satellite-derived gross primary productivity (GPP) from the Global OCO-2 Solar-Induced Fluorescence (GOSIF) product. Resistance was defined as the proportional change in GPP during the stress event relative to a multi-year climatological baseline, while resilience was defined as the relative recovery of GPP one year after the event compared with the same baseline. After accounting for water-stress severity and duration, fire-affected events showed lower resistance (−0.02 to −0.03) and resilience (−0.04 to −0.10) than fire-free events (p < 0.001), with resilience showing the greater reduction. Spatially, fire-associated declines were greatest in highly flammable hummock grasslands and arid shrublands, while woody savannas showed comparatively smaller responses. Late dry-season fires were consistently associated with larger immediate productivity declines and slower post-stress recovery than early dry-season burns. These findings extend previous savanna fire studies beyond site-scale and single-disturbance approaches by assessing ecosystem resistance and resilience under interacting fire–water stress conditions across multiple hydroclimatic zones and vegetation types.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: A PROSPECT-guided multi-task learning hybrid framework for simultaneous retrieval of leaf chlorophyll and carotenoids
abstract: Leaf chlorophyll (Chl) and carotenoids (Cxc) jointly govern light harvesting and photoprotection. However, concurrent retrieval from leaf reflectance remains challenging because Cxc absorption is weaker and strongly overlaps with Chl in the visible range. This spectral challenge, together with the physiological coordination between Chl and Cxc, motivates a multi-task learning (MTL) formulation for joint retrieval. Here, we propose a PROSPECT-guided MTL framework for the joint retrieval of leaf Chl and Cxc from 400–911 nm reflectance. The model is trained on PROSPECT-5 simulations and adopts a shared backbone with two pigment-specific branches. It is evaluated on five in-situ datasets (ANGERS, NX, BM, XS, and JTL; n = 680), benchmarked against separate single-task networks (STL), partial least squares regression (PLSR) and PROSPECT-based lookup-table inversion (PHY). Across datasets, the proposed MTL model consistently outperforms STL, PLSR and PHY for Chl and improves Cxc retrieval in most cases. In pooled evaluation, the RMSE for Chl is reduced by 32%, 13% and 28% compared with STL, PLSR and PHY, respectively. For Cxc, the corresponding reductions are 4%, 16% and 14%. On the public ANGERS benchmark, the model achieves an RMSE of 5.56 μg/cm 2 for Chl (R 2 = 0.93) and 2.39 μg/cm 2 for Cxc (R 2 = 0.78), yielding performance competitive with prior reflectance-based reports. PROSPECT-referenced occlusion analysis further suggests that, relative to STL, MTL induces more complementary wavelength reliance between the two tasks within pigment-sensitive regions. Overall, the PROSPECT–MTL framework enables accurate and robust reflectance-only joint retrieval of Chl and Cxc across datasets. These results provide a leaf-level basis for future canopy-scale and sensor-scale extensions in pigment-informed vegetation monitoring.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: LC-SLab — An object-based deep learning framework for large-scale land cover classification from satellite imagery and sparse in-situ labels
abstract: Large-scale land cover maps generated using deep learning play a critical role in data-driven analysis and decision-making across a wide range of Earth science applications. Open in-situ datasets from principled land cover surveys offer a scalable alternative to manual annotation for training such models. However, their sparse spatial coverage leads to fragmented and noisy predictions when used with existing deep learning-based land cover mapping approaches. A promising direction to address this issue is object-based classification, which assigns labels to semantically coherent image regions rather than individual pixels, thereby imposing a minimum mapping unit that controls spatial fragmentation. Despite this potential, object-based methods remain underexplored in deep learning-based land cover mapping pipelines, especially in the context of medium-resolution imagery and sparse supervision. To address this gap, we propose LC-SLab, the first deep learning framework for systematically exploring object-based deep learning methods for large-scale land cover classification under sparse supervision. LC-SLab supports both input-level aggregation via graph neural networks, and output-level aggregation by postprocessing results from established semantic segmentation models. Additionally, we incorporate features from a large pre-trained network to improve performance on small datasets. We evaluate the framework on annual Sentinel-2 composites with sparse LUCAS labels, focusing on the tradeoff between accuracy and fragmentation, as well as sensitivity to dataset size. Our results show that object-based methods can match or exceed the accuracy of common pixel-wise models while producing substantially more coherent maps. Input-level aggregation proves more robust on smaller datasets, whereas output-level aggregation performs best with more data. Several configurations of LC-SLab also outperform existing land cover products, highlighting the framework’s practical utility.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Integrating UAV image time-series with multi-source environmental features for sequential wildfire spread prediction
abstract: High-resolution UAV observations provide a novel perspective for monitoring wildfire dynamics. This study explores a new approach for wildfire prediction by integrating high-precision, multi-source spatial data. We introduce 3DConv-U-Net, a deep learning model designed to capture spatiotemporal spread patterns. The architecture uses a 3D convolutional backbone to process continuous fire sequences and a separate encoder for environmental factors. To address the scarcity of real-world data, we developed a simulation pipeline to generate minute-level synthetic dataset. This allows the model to learn the physical rules of fire spread at a high temporal resolution. Experimental results show that the model generalizes effectively from 30 m simulation data to 1 m UAV observations. Our approach achieves higher performance with a Sorensen index of 0.959 and a Jaccard index of 0.921. Notably, the model demonstrates improvements in computational complexity and inference for lightweight optimization. Compared to the Transformer-based model, it reduces the parameter count by 70% and achieves an efficient inference time of 47.8 ms/batch, providing a practical tool for real-time edge computing. This work demonstrates that data-driven models can maintain spatial consistency across different scales. The results can support continuous wildfire monitoring and more reliable emergency decision-making.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Extreme climate effects on the occurrence and frequency of glacial debris flows: evidence from the Parlung Tsangpo Basin, Southeastern Tibetan Plateau
abstract: Under ongoing climate change, glacial debris flows are becoming a more important cryospheric hazard in high mountain areas, yet the effects of extreme climate on their activity remain insufficiently understood. This study investigates the spatiotemporal relationships between extreme climate and glacial debris-flow activity in the Parlung Tsangpo Basin, southeastern Tibetan Plateau, over the four decades from 1985 to 2024. Specifically, an inventory of glacial debris-flow activity was compiled using historical spaceborne photographs and Landsat imagery, and seven extreme temperature and precipitation indices were derived from two gridded meteorological datasets. The contributions of extreme climate indices to glacial debris-flow occurrence probability and frequency were then modeled separately at the decadal scale using logistic and zero-truncated negative binomial regression models, and their spatial correspondence with hotspots of the dominant extreme climate indices was finally examined. The results show that extreme warming and precipitation exert differentiated effects on glacial debris-flow activity. Temporally, the warm spell duration index (WSDI) makes the strongest contribution to glacial debris-flow occurrence probability (2.16%), whereas the maximum consecutive 5-day precipitation amount (Rx5day) contributes most strongly to glacial debris-flow frequency (2.57%). Spatially, WSDI hotspots exhibit little overlap with glacial debris-flow hotspots, whereas Rx5day hotspots display much stronger co-location. Overall, the study highlights that prolonged warm extremes mainly enhance long-term predisposition, while multi-day precipitation extremes are more closely associated with triggering conditions, implying that regional hazard assessment and early warning of glacial debris flows should account for both short-term extreme wet conditions and preceding periods of sustained anomalous warmth.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Generation of high-precision precipitable water vapor products from morphed integrated microwave imagery
abstract: Water vapor is a key component in regulating Earth’s climate system, and precise monitoring of its variability is essential for advancing weather forecasting and climate research. While the Morphed Integrated Microwave Imagery at the Cooperative Institute for Meteorological Satellite Studies (MIMIC) provides near real-time, high-resolution estimates of Precipitable Water Vapor (PWV), its utility is constrained by notable inaccuracies and systematic biases. To address these limitations, this study introduces a hybrid calibration framework combining Spherical Cap Harmonic Analysis (SCHA) with Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) to enhance the accuracy of MIMIC-derived PWV. The resulting dataset offers high-precision PWV estimates over North America spanning 2016–2024. Validation against Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) PWV measurements demonstrates substantial improvements, with root mean square errors (RMSEs) reduced from 4.1 mm to 1.6 mm for the 0.25° resolution product and from 4.1 mm to 1.4 mm for the 0.02° product—representing accuracy gains of 61% and 66% over the original MIMIC PWV. The optimized PWV exhibits negligible bias relative to GNSS data and improved spatial and temporal consistency. Additionally, the hybrid approach effectively mitigates common artifacts in the original MIMIC products, including striping, shot noise, land–water boundary discontinuities, and excessive spatial smoothing. Further validation using radiosonde observations and ERA5 PWV yields RMSEs of 2.2–2.3 mm (0.25°) and 2.1–2.3 mm (0.02°), corresponding to 44–49% and 41–55% improvements. This work significantly enhances the reliability of MIMIC PWV data, providing a robust, high-quality resource for weather and climate applications.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Pioneering Test-Time training for robust Fine-Grained chlorophyll-a retrieval from Sentinel-2: Unveiling China’s lake eutrophication dynamics (2018–2025)
abstract: Remote sensing retrieval of lake chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) concentration is essential for eutrophication assessment and water quality management, yet conventional models suffer severe degradation in large-scale, long-term monitoring due to domain shifts arising from inconsistent atmospheric correction (regional aerosol variability) and spatiotemporal heterogeneity in aquatic optical properties. This study pioneers Test-Time Training (TTT) for robust lake Chl-a retrieval. The TTT dual-task architecture—a primary regression head paired with a self-supervised spectral reconstruction head—enables real-time adaptation to test-domain distributions without retraining, effectively compensating for residual atmospheric errors and regional apparent optical properties (AOP) distortions. Based on the proposed algorithm, this study comprehensively analyzed the spatiotemporal evolution of Chl-a in 2,621 lakes (≥1 km 2 ) in China from 2018 to 2025. The results showed the proposed model achieved superior performance in Chl-a retrieval ( R 2 = 0.79, RMSE = 9.99 μg/L), outperforming conventional machine learning approaches by approximately 28 %-36 % and underscoring its robustness in optically complex inland waters. National Chl-a distribution exhibits a clear east-high, west-low pattern, with mean concentrations of 31.29 μg/L in the Eastern Plain versus 13.83 μg/L on the Tibetan Plateau. Regional analysis indicated that most regions exhibited a downward trend in Chl-a concentrations, suggesting an improvement in water quality. Bloom risk assessment, based on over 170,000 observations, indicates that the Eastern Plain lakes face “extremely high risk” (44.7 % bloom occurrence), requiring targeted management. The proposed lake Chl-a remote sensing retrieval algorithm provides a new paradigm for fine-grained global water quality monitoring and spatiotemporal analysis, holding landmark significance for global water environment surveillance and proactive management. The code is available at https://github.com/KustAIRS/SR-TTA .
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Self-supervised spectral unmixing using scene-aware deep priors
abstract: High spectral resolution of hyperspectral sensors facilitates the detailed identification of material, but the coarse spatial resolution affects accurate interpretation. In this regard, spectral unmixing techniques attempt to estimate the constituent materials (endmembers) and their fractional areas (abundances) within a pixel’s instantaneous field of view (IFOV). However, many existing methods optimize denoising, endmember detection, and abundance estimation separately, which can limit robustness under noise and spectral variability. The current study proposes a self-supervised deep learning framework for joint hyperspectral unmixing and denoising. A noise-aware probabilistic encoding strategy is adopted to model a structured latent space to implicitly detect the endmembers. Further, the proposed encoding scheme and regularizations ensure spatio-spectral fidelity to improve robustness to noise. Additionally, a contrastive learning mechanism is incorporated to improve latent separability and robustness to spectral variability. The framework also integrates available partial endmember priors when present and employs a policy-based adaptive refinement mechanism to update endmember estimates under complex noise and mixing conditions. In addition, a learnable loss-balancing strategy is introduced to reduce manual tuning and stabilize optimization. Experiments on synthetic and real hyperspectral datasets demonstrate strong and balanced performance across reconstruction accuracy, spectral fidelity, and clustering quality, indicating the effectiveness of the proposed framework for practical hyperspectral unmixing.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of grasshopper habitats under future climate projections, vegetation growth, and land use change
abstract: Grasshopper outbreaks pose a persistent threat to grassland ecosystems and livestock production, yet large-scale monitoring of their suitable habitats under future climate change remains challenging due to complex interactions among climate, vegetation, and land use. Consequently, this study, taking China’s grasslands as the research area, explores the relationships between grasshoppers, host plants, and the environment and constructs habitat monitoring indicators using future climate, land use, and topographic data. Building on this, an ensemble model comprising Random Forest, eXtreme Gradient Boosting, and Light Gradient Boosting Machine is established to monitor the grasshopper suitable habitats under four Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, SSP3-7.0, and SSP5-8.5) from 2021 to 2100. Results indicate that elevation, temperature seasonality, slope, and precipitation during the nymph and egg stages significantly influence grasshopper occurrence. Moreover, elevation, temperature seasonality, precipitation seasonality, slope, precipitation during the growth period, and isothermality are major contributors to host plant distribution. Suitable habitats are projected to remain concentrated in Inner Mongolia, northern Shaanxi, southern Gansu, Qinghai, and northern Xinjiang, with pronounced regional shifts over time. Low emission scenarios (SSP1-2.6) consistently possess the smallest and declining extent of most suitable habitats, whereas high emission pathways have the largest habitat, potentially creating environmental conditions that are more favorable for grasshopper persistence and expansion. The results provide spatially explicit insights for early warning, targeted monitoring, and sustainable grassland pest management in a warming world.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Quantifying methane emissions from large coal mine using Sentinel-5 Precursor satellite data and Gaussian plume model
abstract: Coal mining methane is a major contributor to anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions in China. However, point-source emission data for Chinese coal mining areas remain scarce. Current bottom-up emission inventories suffer from significant uncertainties due to incomplete or inaccurate activity data and emission factors. This study presents a satellite-based methodology to quantify methane emissions from large coal mines, utilizing Gaussian plume model and observations from the Copernicus Sentinel-5 Precursor TROPOspheric Monitoring Instrument (TROPOMI-S5P), in which mixed plume effects of multiple point sources are considered. Applied to four typical underground and open-pit coal mining areas in China, we identify 18 effective TROPOMI-S5P methane plume enhancements, with emission rates ranging from 49.15 ± 19.43 t/d (Xiheishan mining area in Xinjiang) to 694.07 ± 58.66 t/d (Haerwusu-Heidaigou coal mine cluster in Inner Mongolia). Overall, the interannual variability of the estimated methane emissions is generally consistent with that of the coal production in the mining area. Uncertainty in individual plume-derived estimates ranges from 8.45 % to 41.01 %, primarily attributable to wind field data. Our satellite-derived estimates align closely with calculations using regionally refined emission factors, yet fall substantially below global inventories like Emissions Database for Global Atmospheric Research v8.0 (EDGARv8.0) and Global Fuel Exploitation Inventory (GFEI). This discrepancy may stem from outdated emission factors, evolving mining practices, observational capabilities, and sampling bias. This study highlights the critical role of satellite monitoring in validating and refining emission inventories, providing actionable insights for methane emission quantification and targeted mitigation in the coal mining sector.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Enabling maize mapping in double-cropping regions of Argentina and Brazil without ground reference data by leveraging multiple satellite platforms
abstract: Large-scale maize mapping is challenging due to the lack of field-level datasets, which were essential for training machine learning models. The United States (US) provides abundant in-situ labels and national maize maps while Argentina and Brazil offered limited data and double-cropping further complicates mapping. In this study, we propose a survey-free method for maize mapping in Argentina and Brazil, with cropping intensity considered. We first pre-trained a maize classifier on US cornfields using Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation (GEDI) Relative Height (RH) metrics and Sentinel-2 imagery, then transferred this model to Argentina and Brazil to produce candidate maize labels at peak growth. We distinguished maize from other crops using phenology-based empirical thresholds. These high-confidence labels were then used to train a Random Forest model. Finally, we validated the maps with Google Street View (GSV) imagery and benchmark maps. Our framework produced 18,481 maize and 15,725 non-maize labels in Argentina and 2,125 first-season maize, 7,406 s-season maize and 7,643 non-maize in Brazil. Evaluation of our maize maps against GSV images showed satisfactory agreement, with accuracies around 90 %. The maps also aligned well with benchmark maps, exhibiting 91 % accuracy for Argentina and 88 % for Brazil. Our proposed frameworks can enhance maize mapping where field surveys are challenging.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: An integrated picture fuzzy entropy–MAIRCA–TOPSIS framework for sustainable soil suitability evaluation
abstract: Effective soil and land site selection is essential for sustainable agriculture, which aligns with the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 2 - Zero Hunger. Ensuring food security and enhancing agricultural productivity require innovative approaches to identify suitable soils that account for diverse, interdependent properties. Nevertheless, many essential soil characteristics cannot be measured through numerical values. This limitation poses a significant challenge to selecting soils to maximize agricultural production. To address these challenges, this study proposes an integrated decision-making framework that combines entropy measures, multi-attribute ideal-real comparative assessment (MAIRCA), and technique for order of preference by similarity to ideal solution (TOPSIS) techniques under a picture fuzzy environment. Moreover, a novel distance measure is defined to improve the robustness of the model. The proposed method is applied to assess soil samples collected from various agricultural lands by considering important physicochemical properties analyzed in a laboratory setting. The methodology finds the most suitable soils for cultivating staple and economically significant crops such as paddy, legumes, ragi, maize, groundnut, and sugarcane. Furthermore, comprehensive validation including rank correlation analysis, rank-difference evaluation, and graphical comparison demonstrates strong agreement with established MCDM methods such as TOPSIS and ARAS, which confirm the methodological soundness of the proposed approach. In addition, a sensitivity analysis was conducted using 1000 random perturbations of criteria weights, and it reveals extremely high rank stability, further attesting to the model’s reliability under realistic uncertainties.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: SuperDove satellite detection of matter-loaded windrows with a focus on extreme environmental events
abstract: Matter-loaded windrows are high-density submesoscale accumulation structures that form on the ocean surface and are often associated with extreme environmental events. This study presents a framework for windrow detection using a UNet deep-learning model applied to Planet SuperDove (PSD) 8-band satellite imagery (FLODAS). The model is trained on hand-annotated cases representing a variety of windrows and evaluated using complementary performance metrics, demonstrating consistent detection across independent scenes, while also revealing scene-specific patterns of false positives. Spectral analysis and classification based on the spectral angle distance metric is used to examine the potential for discriminating floating matter types using the PSD bands. Limited ground-truth data and the incomplete spectral characterisation of floating matter currently constrain classification performance. Application of the framework in the Aegean Sea enabled the identification of surface matter accumulations linked to storm-driven runoff and riverine discharge. The results demonstrate the potential of the framework to support in situ sampling and debris-removal operations, as well as short-term assessments of matter transport and windrow dynamics. Overall, the proposed framework represents a proof-of-concept step towards the development of operational detection systems for surface matter and marine debris accumulations.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: A transferable framework for roof vegetation mapping across tropical cities based on open-source multimodal data and morphology-aware UDASS
abstract: Green roofs play a vital role in urban sustainability, offering substantial environmental, ecological, and social benefits. However, automated roof vegetation extraction mostly relies on costly high-resolution data, with limited investigations in Global South cities. Existing methods insufficiently fuse multimodal priors and overlook domain adaptation, thereby constraining extraction accuracy and cross-regional generalization. This work presents a transferable open-source data-driven framework for cross-domain multimodal extraction and analysis of roof vegetation. Specifically, we introduce a multimodal transformer encoder to fuse Google imagery, Sentinel-2-derived products and OpenStreetMap building footprints at the feature level to improve extraction accuracy. We then propose an unsupervised domain-adaptive semantic segmentation (UDASS) model with morphology-aware pseudo-label correction to improve cross-domain generalization cost-effectively. Validated across six Southeast Asian cities, our framework achieves an F1-score of 81.71% for supervised source domain extraction and up to 70.85% for UDASS. Further validation on four additional cities spanning East Africa, South America, West Asia, and South Asia verifies its strong cross-regional generalization ability. Finally, approximately 297 ha of roof vegetation are detected across the six Southeast Asian cities, mainly on low-to-mid-rise buildings with distinct regional disparities and diverse vegetation intensity. This study delivers the first large-scale dataset on roof vegetation and green roofs for tropical Southeast Asia, establishes a cost-effective and scalable multimodal paradigm for cross-regional monitoring, and supports evidence-based green roof planning and analysis.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Urban digital twin for environmentally sensitive mobility planning: conceptual framework and application in pilot region Leipzig
abstract: This study presents the development and pilot implementation of a conceptual, practice-oriented Urban Digital Twin (UDT) used for environmentally sensitive traffic management within the pilot region of Leipzig (Germany). The UDT uses modular traffic simulations (SUMO), real-time sensor data and floating car data to create dynamic, near-real-time models of intermodal urban mobility systems and to evaluate mobility measures. Through a collaborative, co-creative development process involving municipal stakeholders, the study focuses on people-centred design and scenario-based simulations to assess the potential impact of transport strategies under upcoming air pollution limits. The Leipzig case serves as a test environment for validating the technical feasibility, participatory governance and transferability of the UDT approach. The results show the potential of UDTs to support responsive, data-driven decision-making using the developed workflow manager. In doing so, this study provides a transferable methodological basis for cities that want to implement an intelligent, sustainable and socially inclusive mobility transformation using digital twin technology.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: HeightCLIP: A vision-language network for height estimation from monocular remote sensing imagery
abstract: Accurate height estimation from monocular remote sensing imagery is a fundamental task with broad applications in urban planning and management. However, existing vision-based methods rely solely on visual features, which limits their ability to fully exploit height-related semantic information. Vision-language models, e.g., CLIP, offer a promising alternative by leveraging multimodal information, yet directly adapting them to height regression remains challenging due to their weak perception of continuous numerical values. To overcome this limitation, we propose HeightCLIP , a novel vision-language framework tailored for height estimation from monocular remote sensing imagery. The task-adaptive textual prompts and image-side representations are optimized under height supervision to derive pixel-text similarity features for accurate height estimation. Specifically, we design an interval-based prompting strategy that integrates learnable context tokens and a fixed natural language template with parameterized interval values, allowing CLIP to better comprehend height-related semantics. In addition, we incorporate a reciprocal cross-attention fusion mechanism to facilitate bidirectional interaction between visual and textual features, thereby improving cross-modal feature integration. Finally, building upon this enriched feature space, we impose cross-modal consistency constraints to ensure pixel-level correspondence between height descriptions and visual features, providing more informative representations for subsequent height prediction. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets i.e., Vaihingen, Potsdam, and Data Fusion Contest 2019 (DFC2019), demonstrate that HeightCLIP achieves competitive or superior performance compared with existing state-of-the-art methods, and comprehensive ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of each proposed component. The source code will be made available at https://github.com/songtaowhu/HeightCLIP .
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: MFRXG: A multi-feature stacking ensemble RF-XGBoost model for total nitrogen retrieval in the Yellow River from Landsat 8/9 data
abstract: Total nitrogen (TN) is a key indicator for assessing eutrophication in aquatic systems, and its concentration dynamics are influenced by a combination of hydrometeorological factors, terrain, and other pollution sources. However, traditional retrieval models based solely on remote sensing reflectance often suffer from limited generalization capability. This study develops a multi-feature stacked random forest (RF)-extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) algorithm (MFRXG) based on field TN data from automatic stations along the Yellow River (YR). The MFRXG integrates Landsat 8/9 satellite data, ERA5 hydrometeorological data, and terrain data to estimate the TN concentration in YR. Using an independent validation dataset in 2025, MFRXG demonstrates robust prediction accuracy and stability, with a coefficient of determination (R 2 ) of 0.75, a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.53 mg/L, and a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.31 mg/L, outperforming multiple linear regression (MLR), support vector regression (SVR), artificial neural networks (ANN), RF, and XGBoost. Subsequently, the spatiotemporal changes of TN concentration in YR are investigated from 2015 to 2025. Results show that spatially, TN concentrations exhibit a fluctuating pattern with a generally increasing gradient from the upstream to the downstream of the YR. Temporally, over the past decade, TN concentrations along the main stream show an overall slight upward trend, which is primarily attributable to changes in concentration contributions from upstream areas. Overall, the proposed modeling approach provides effective technical support for long-term and dynamic monitoring of TN concentration changes in YR and fills the gaps in spatial and temporal coverage and assessment efficiency of traditional monitoring methods.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: DINO-Pheno-Cluster: Integrating few-shot foundation models and UAV time-series for spatiotemporal growth and functional characterization of alfalfa
abstract: Precise characterization of alfalfa growth dynamics is essential for breeding accessions with superior regrowth capacity, persistence, and yield stability. However, traditional plot level and coarse scale observations suffer from low signal to noise ratios particularly before canopy closure when phenotypic data are strongly affected by weeds and soil background. Moreover, existing studies rarely capture the dynamic mechanisms of crop development across the entire growth cycle. To address this, the DINO-Pheno-Cluster framework is introduced as a foundation model driven and mechanism decomposed phenotyping approach. This decoupled framework first utilizes DINO-XMem, a few-shot individual plant segmentation network based on DINOv3 and a dual memory mechanism. It subsequently applies parameterized dynamic modeling guided by growth process knowledge. Validation utilized high frequency Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) imagery from 12 time points across three growing seasons covering 127 alfalfa accessions. DINO-XMem achieved an 89.54% mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) under a 10-shot setting and maintained 86.77% under extreme 1-shot conditions. It successfully resolved dense canopy oversegmentation outperforming fully supervised baselines by 4.08% to 11.97% in mIoU. Crucially, the extracted high purity time series trajectories were parameterized into specific biological indicators including maximum growth rate, comprehensive regeneration index, and seasonal stability index. Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) clustering based on these mechanistic traits identified four distinct functional ideotypes comprising High yield/High regrowth, Upright/Sparse, High stability/Persistent, and Short/Dense, all validated by ground measured biomass. This workflow establishes a precision screening tool for multi harvest crops advancing crop phenomics toward process level analysis.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: PLGF-NET: A Physics-Guided Local-Global fusion network for GNSS-R high wind speed retrieval
abstract: Accurate global sea surface wind speed retrieval under high-wind conditions (> 15 m/s) remains a persistent bottleneck for spaceborne Global Navigation Satellite System Reflectometry (GNSS-R). Conventional data-driven models often experience severe performance degradation in these regimes due to inherent physical limitations, including long-tail data distributions, low signal-to-noise ratios (SNR), and scattering signal saturation. To transcend these limitations, this study proposes the Physics-Guided Local-Global Fusion Network (PLGF-NET), establishing a novel physics-data dual-driven paradigm. At the data level, a Comprehensive Difficulty Score (CDS) is introduced to quantify the intrinsic physical complexity of Delay-Doppler Maps (DDMs). This metric drives a difficulty-aware hierarchical sampling strategy that rectifies long-tail biases and dynamically mines the scarce, high-wind scattering signatures. Within the network, a Physics-Guided Spatial Attention (PGSA) mechanism translates specular reflection theory into a structural inductive bias. This enforces a rigorous feature purification process, locking the receptive field onto the effective scattering window while suppressing peripheral thermal noise. Furthermore, geophysical consistency is guaranteed through a selective regularization mechanism governed by Sample Prediction Difficulty (SPD). Rather than applying uniform constraints, this approach adaptively enforces Geophysical Model Function (GMF) constraints exclusively on high-uncertainty samples, providing a robust physical anchor against signal saturation. Comprehensive evaluations demonstrate the exceptional robustness of PLGF-NET. The framework achieves a state-of-the-art overall root mean square error (RMSE) of 1.38 m/s and drastically compresses the high-wind RMSE to 2.40 m/s, effectively correcting systematic negative biases. Ultimately, this scalable and physically interpretable architecture provides a highly reliable Earth observation tool for high-wind marine environment monitoring.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Earth Observation–Based Machine learning for operational forecasting of harmful algal blooms in the Arabian Gulf and Sea of Oman
abstract: Harmful algal blooms (HABs) pose increasing risks to coastal ecosystems, fisheries, and desalination infrastructure in the Arabian Gulf and Sea of Oman. Forecasting bloom occurrence remains challenging due to strong spatial variability in physical forcing and biological response. Here, we develop a physics-informed machine-learning framework to forecast HAB probability using satellite Earth observation data and reanalysis-derived environmental predictors over the period 2002–2024. Bloom events are defined using region-specific, seasonally varying chlorophyll thresholds derived from training data, and a Random Forest classifier is used to estimate bloom probability at 8-day resolution. Operational probability thresholds are calibrated using historical data (2002–2020) and applied unchanged to independent evaluation (2021–2022) and strictly forward (2023–2024) periods. The model demonstrated moderate classification skill during the independent evaluation period (F1 = 0.46–0.67) and strong forward operational performance, achieving F1 scores of 0.79–0.97 across the study regions. Permutation importance analysis showed that chlorophyll anomaly contributed most strongly to forecast performance across regions, indicating that deviations from seasonal biomass conditions are strongly associated with bloom detection skill, while physical variables provide complementary predictive information. These findings demonstrate that a biomass-informed, Earth observation–based framework enables robust and operationally stable detection of harmful algal blooms across hydrographically complex marginal seas, supporting its application as an early-warning system for HAB monitoring and management in the Arabian Gulf and Sea of Oman.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Fusing very high-resolution aerial imagery with Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 time series improves multi-year orchard type classification
abstract: Accurate mapping of perennial orchards is essential for agricultural management but remains challenging due to spatially discontinuous canopies and subtle phenological differences. This study presents an operational, application-oriented framework that integrates annual Very High-Resolution (VHR) aerial imagery (0.2 m) with monthly Sentinel-1 Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and Sentinel-2 optical time series to classify twelve orchard types across Israel from 2018 to 2023. By utilizing a multi-year dataset rather than a single seasonal cycle, we specifically evaluate model generalization and temporal robustness against inter-annual variability in phenology and imaging conditions. The dataset includes 106,413 labeled parcel-year samples from 19,950 parcels. We evaluate three model families: (i) satellite-only, (ii) VHR-only, and (iii) a multimodal mid-fusion deep-learning model (integrating spatial-structural and spectral-temporal modalities), under the same-year and cross-year (leave-one-year-out) scenarios. The satellite stream is modeled with a Lightweight Temporal Attention Encoder (LTAE) to capture seasonal dynamics, while the VHR stream uses a Swin Transformer backbone to extract hierarchical spatial features from 0.2 m imagery. The fused model achieved the highest performance across all settings (same-year OA = 0.890 ± 0.009; cross-year OA = 0.881 ± 0.014), outperforming both satellite-only (0.83) and VHR-only models (same-year OA = 0.846; cross-year OA = 0.795). In the best-performing fused cross-year scenario, class-wise F1-scores ranged from 0.71 for apple to 0.99 for banana. Fusion provided the largest gains in early-stage orchards (ages 1–3), where sparse canopy cover weakens spectral signals, but VHR imagery reveals planting geometry. Per-class analyses show that fusion benefits decrease with increasing mean NDVI, highlighting strong gains for sparse or deciduous orchards and minimal gains for dense evergreens. Overall, the results demonstrate that phenological time series and VHR spatial structure are highly complementary, enabling robust, operational orchard-type mapping and informing cost-aware workflows that selectively prioritize VHR acquisitions for young or low-NDVI orchards.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Identification and classification of risk zones for Calliptamus italicus based on remote sensing and ensemble modeling: considering population density and habitat suitability
abstract: Locust outbreaks remain a major challenge to global ecological and environmental security. Calliptamus italicus is the most common migratory locust in the China-Kazakhstan border region. Although relevant countries are actively carrying out control, the excessively large control area has become an important burden. Previous studies have mapped its potential suitable areas, but most studies used only a single model and focused only on suitability changes. Limited attention has been paid to the effect of density on population distribution. This study identifies risk zones by integrating potential suitable areas with population density. It aims to enhance suitable habitat prediction and is of great significance for improving locust control. Based on five categories of Earth observation data and field-surveyed occurrence and density data, this study constructed a regional risk zoning framework using nine models, geographical detector, and path analysis. The ensemble model yielded an AUC value of 0.98, outperforming previous studies in this region. The suitable areas of Calliptamus italicus showed a radial spatial pattern expanding outward from highly suitable areas. Seasonal temperature and precipitation, vegetation condition, and soil texture had the highest explanatory power for regional locust density, and formed multiple impact pathways. Risk zones were distributed in the northern part of the study area and the transboundary continuous grassland belt, and gradually extended toward the central region, showing an overall banded or mosaic spatial pattern. A spatial mismatch existed between suitable areas and risk zones, highlighting the complementary value of field-measured density data in locust risk assessment. This framework helps provide a new perspective for pest management and control under climate change.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Beyond fidelity: Rethinking realism through human behavior in VR city modeling LOD design
abstract: This study redefines realism in virtual reality (VR) city modeling by proposing a perception-driven Level of Detail (LOD) framework informed by human gaze behavior. Challenging the conventional assumption that higher fidelity equates to greater realism, the study systematically investigates the interplay of Feature Complexity (FC), Appearance (AP), and Semantics (SE) in achieving "cognitive realism." Using eye-tracking technology integrated with VR, we conducted experiments in Guangzhou’s Xianfeng Community to identify LOD configurations that most closely align with real-world gaze distribution. Results reveal that the High Feature Complexity, Mid Appearance, Low Semantics (H-M-L) combination optimizes both global gaze patterns and perceptual coherence, outperforming higher semantic density configurations. The study also introduces an open-source tool for analyzing gaze behavior in urban VR environments, providing a scalable solution for immersive urban design research. These findings establish a foundation for advancing human-centric design in VR city modeling, emphasizing perceptual realism over technical fidelity to better align virtual environments with real-world human cognition. This work further positions VR-based perception-driven modeling as a key enabler for Urban Digital Twins, supporting the transition from static 3D models to dynamic, multi-source-data decision-making platforms.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: An interpretable Earth observation framework for estimating lake dissolved organic carbon in Sweden using Sentinel-2 and ERA5-Land data
abstract: Inland-water dissolved organic carbon (DOC) is a key regulator of aquatic carbon cycling and water quality, yet it remains difficult to observe at the spatial and temporal scales targeted by Earth observation (EO). This study developed an interpretable machine learning (ML) framework to estimate lake DOC and interpret model behavior across Sweden using Sentinel-2 MultiSpectral Instrument (MSI) reflectance (RS), ERA5-Land environmental variables (E), and geographic features (G). Using 1,595 spatiotemporal match-ups from 349 lake locations during the period 2017–2024, this study benchmarked five regression algorithms across four feature combinations. XGBoost with the full E + RS + G configuration achieved the best estimation performance (RMSE ≈ 2.46 mg C L −1 ; Bias ≈ −1.6 %) and enabled 10 m quarterly DOC estimation and mapping for examining spatiotemporal changes in Swedish lakes. Robustness was further evaluated using a held-out test set, spatially separated validation, interpolation, and coordinate-only baselines to assess potential spatial confounding. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis indicated that DOC predictability in the Sweden-wide dataset is strongly spatially structured: geographic features capture broad-scale spatial context, while vegetation, hydroclimatic variables, and visible-to-near-infrared reflectance provide more directly interpretable process-related signals. Overall, the framework provides an operational EO–ML workflow for DOC estimation in Sweden, with explicit robustness tests to assess the respective roles of auxiliary spatial context and EO–environmental predictors.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: BQEL-Net: A bimodal quantitative ensemble learning network with uncertainty-aware for vectorized extraction of martian impact craters from bimodal catalogic-and-quantitative dataset (BCQDS)
abstract: Current research on bimodal extraction of Martian impact craters, which integrates satellite imagery and digital elevation models (DEMs), remains limited to the object level, with no existing reports about addressing both pixel-level and irregularly vectorized extraction. Furthermore, there is a lack of open-source bimodal datasets that include statistics (such as crater count, area and volume) for Martian impact craters, and no deep learning approaches have been reported for simultaneous extraction and quantitative analysis of Martian impact craters. To address these gaps, this study is the first to create and release a bimodal catalogic and quantitative dataset (BCQDS), combining DEM and satellite imagery with topographic landscape pattern indices. We also propose an innovative bimodal quantitative ensemble learning network (BQEL-Net) with uncertainty-aware paradigm designed for pixel-level, vectorized and quantitative extraction for Martian impact craters from BCQDS. BQEL-Net uses an uncertainty-aware Bayesian ensemble learning strategy (UBELS) by combining multiple strong segmentors confidence and pixel-level confidence to enhance robustness and accuracy; the proposed bimodal coordinate channel attention (BC 2 AM) aligns bimodal features in the latent space, making them complementary; and a newly developed quantitative statistics module (QSM) with a pioneer quantitative task loss function, enabling the simultaneous extraction of up to 140 quantitative indices. Experiments conducted using MOLA data within the BCQDS demonstrated that BQEL-Net achieves a maximum MIoU of 0.858. Ablation studies confirmed that the bimodal structure, BC 2 AM, UBELS and QSM contribute MIoU gains. This work pioneers a crater catalog with 3D geometric morphology to support quantitative studies of Martian surface evolution.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Spatially varying NDVI–stand structure relationships in Scots pine forests across Poland using HLS, LiDAR metrics and GGP-GAM
abstract: Satellite-derived vegetation indices are widely used in forest monitoring, yet their interpretation is complicated by the fact that canopy reflectance integrates both environmental stress signals and structural variation in stands. This challenge is particularly important across broad ecological gradients, where relationships between optical metrics and stand attributes may be spatially non-stationary. Here, we analysed NDVI–stand structure relationships in Scots pine-dominated forests across the whole of Poland using 30 m HLSS30 imagery, LiDAR-derived stand metrics, and a Geographic Gaussian Process Generalised Additive Model (GGP-GAM). The study focused on closed-canopy, undisturbed Scots pine stands and examined annual NDVI variation in 2016–2022 across eight forest natural regions in relation to stand age, stand volume, top height, and the Relative Spacing Index (RSI). Mean NDVI showed persistent regional differentiation across Poland and ranged from 0.64 to 0.84. The proportion of NDVI variability explained by stand characteristics varied markedly among years and forest natural regions, indicating strong spatial and temporal heterogeneity in NDVI–structure relationships. In general, structural predictors explained a larger share of NDVI variation in years with more favourable moisture conditions, whereas in drought years this structural signal was less apparent, partly coinciding with lower and more compressed NDVI distributions. An illustrative regional analysis further showed that the direction and magnitude of the partial effects of stand attributes changed among years, demonstrating that the structural meaning of NDVI was not constant through time. The results show that NDVI should not be interpreted as a spatially invariant proxy of stand structure across heterogeneous forest landscapes. Instead, its information content depends on both regional context and annual moisture conditions. By combining harmonized optical time series, LiDAR-derived stand descriptors and spatially varying modelling, this study provides a framework for more robust interpretation of canopy greenness in large-area forest monitoring.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Divergent ecohydrological impacts of agricultural and urban expansions across global drylands
abstract: Global drylands face compounding threats from climate change and rapid human expansion, yet satellite observations paradoxically show widespread vegetation greening. This study investigates the divergent ecohydrological impacts of agricultural and urban expansions across 8,507 global dryland basins from 2000 to 2022. By integrating cloud-based, multi-source Earth observation data with a Spatial Durbin Model, we decouple the local footprints and spatial spillover effects of human land-use on surface water loss. The results unveil a pervasive Greening Illusion associated with cropland expansion, where gains in vegetation productivity are strictly sustained by the severe depletion of surface water bodies, affecting 43.33 % of the studied basins. In contrast, urban growth consistently triggers simultaneous ecological and hydrological degradation. Crucially, the spatial econometric analysis (spatial interaction coefficient ρ = 0.616) demonstrates that the indirect spatial spillover effect of agricultural expansion on water loss is significantly positive (+0.0584) and vastly overpowers its non-significant direct local footprint (‒0.0051) under the baseline k = 6 specification. This massive spatial contagion is structurally robust, exhibiting a 16.0-fold magnitude over the local footprint under physical basin contiguity, which validates a beggar-thy-neighbor dynamic, indicating that localized water withdrawals propagate severe water scarcity to hydrologically connected ecosystems. Our global functional diagnosis identifies 6,679 desiccated hotspots globally that have experienced near-complete surface water desiccation. These findings challenge the assumption that vegetation expansion universally benefits drylands and highlight the urgent need for integrated basin-scale governance, strict regulation of land conversion based on finite hydrological carrying capacities, and transboundary water-sharing frameworks to mitigate systemic ecohydrological risks.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Dual-polarization GNSS reflectometry for FYI–MYI sea ice type classification using microsatellite observations
abstract: Accurate sea ice type classification is essential for polar climate monitoring, ocean–climate interaction studies, and safe navigation. Global Navigation Satellite System Reflectometry (GNSS-R) provides all-weather, high-temporal-resolution sea ice observations with low-power bistatic microwave measurements. The hypothesis of this study is that dual circular polarization GNSS-R observations from small satellites, which simultaneously capture left-hand circularly polarized (LHCP) and right-hand circularly polarized (RHCP) reflected signals, provide additional information for characterizing sea ice scattering properties. Using dual-polarization observations from the Tianmu-1 satellite constellation, we extract features from Delay Doppler Maps (DDMs) and perform sea ice type classification with an eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model. Results show that incorporating dual-polarization features improves performance compared with LHCP-only observations. In the Arctic, first-year ice (FYI) and multi-year ice (MYI) are classified with recall rates of 74.79 % and 69.04 %, with an overall accuracy of 74.29 %. In the Antarctic, FYI and MYI recall rates are 73.64 % and 74.85 %, respectively, with an overall accuracy of 73.71 %. MYI recall improves by approximately 1.7 % in the Arctic and 4.5 % in the Antarctic, while maintaining stable FYI performance. The performance in the Arctic is affected by attitude maneuvers in latitudes > 80°N. These results demonstrate that dual circular polarization GNSS-R provides complementary information that enhances sea ice type classification and supports its potential for next-generation GNSS-R missions.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: A partially supervised joint segmentation method for farmland and rural roads from single-class annotated remote sensing datasets
abstract: Accurate segmentation of co-existing land-cover objects in high-resolution remote sensing imagery is essential for precision agriculture and rural planning. Although multi-class datasets are increasingly available, many high-quality annotations remain task-specific, where only a single target class is labeled and other co-occurring objects are treated as background. Jointly exploiting such heterogeneous single-class datasets introduces supervision ambiguity, resulting in pseudo-background interference, feature conflicts, and unstable optimization. To address these challenges, we propose RSFRNet, a partially supervised joint segmentation framework for farmland and rural road extraction from mutually exclusive single-class annotations. The key idea of RSFRNet is to explicitly match different types of conflicts in this setting with corresponding network and optimization designs. First, considering that roads are dominated by thin linear structures whereas farmland is characterized by large homogeneous regions, we design a Filtering-based Feature-wise Linear Modulation module (F-FiLM) to adapt decoder features to class-specific structural patterns. Second, to reduce the interference caused by unlabeled co-existing objects being treated as background, we introduce a Learnable Class Codebook (L-Codebook), which uses class prototypes to refine encoder representations before decoding. Third, to alleviate inconsistent parameter updates caused by heterogeneous single-class supervision, we introduce PSL-PCGrad to correct conflicting gradients during joint training. In addition, task-aware loss constraints are used to preserve road connectivity and farmland regional integrity. In this way, RSFRNet addresses partially supervised farmland–road joint segmentation from feature adaptation, semantic purification, and optimization stabilization perspectives. Experiments on FarmSeg-VL and WHU-RuR + show that RSFRNet achieves the best evaluated performance, reaching 74.04 % mIoU with balanced farmland and road IoU. These results highlight the effectiveness of RSFRNet for partially supervised farmland–road joint segmentation under mutually exclusive single-class annotations and suggest its potential for related single-class annotation scenarios.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Corrigendum to “Spatiotemporal dynamics of solar photovoltaics development and ecological implications in Japan from cropland to forest” [Int. J. Appl. Earth Obs. Geoinf. 150 (2026) 105348]
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: A new approach for comprehensive and spatiotemporally comparable Eco-Environmental quality assessment of surface coal Mines: MiecoI
abstract: Achieving sustainable management of surface coal mines requires comprehensive and comparable eco-environmental quality (EEQ) assessment methods. This is particularly important across diverse regions. However, existing remote sensing-based indices are generally developed for individual mining areas and fail to account for mining-specific disturbances like atmospheric coal dust, thus lacking regional comparability. This study proposes a comprehensive and spatiotemporally comparable Mine Eco-environmental Quality Index (MiecoI), featuring three innovations: (1) a partitioned assessment system integrating land (vegetation and soil), water, and atmospheric factors by separately processing water and atmospheric component, overcoming the limitations of land-only assessment. (2) A standardized methodology applicable to multiple scenarios that establishes data-driven thresholds from a representative dataset and applying data standardization along with feature extraction, achieving comparable EEQ across various mines. (3) An efficient cloud-deployable computational approach for automated, large-area monitoring. The results demonstrate that: (1) MiecoI exhibited high reliability through integration of 11 indicators, with high correlation coefficients in terrestrial and non-terrestrial areas. (2) Compared to the existing indices, MiecoI demonstrated superior sensitivity to environmental degradation, with scores decreasing by 14.7 % in highly disturbed zones (stope), and spatial alignment with actual boundaries confirms its accuracy. (3) The methodology effectively compares EEQ across different countries and varied climatic and topographic regions, identifying ecological vulnerability and recovery dynamics. By providing a reliable and comparable assessment, MiecoI offers clear guidance for targeted ecological restoration and supports sustainable mining advancement.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: A near-real-time and unsupervised framework for grain crop harvest detection using sentinel-2 imagery: the reaped index (RI) and automated thresholding
abstract: Monitoring grain harvest events is crucial for crop management, yield estimation, and food security. Timely detection supports machinery allocation and mitigates risks from extreme weather. However, most existing studies rely on dense time series or labeled data, limiting real-time applications. This study proposes an unsupervised, index-based thresholding framework using Sentinel-2 imagery for major grain crops (paddy rice, maize, and wheat). A new Reaped Index (RI) was developed to distinguish harvested from unharvested fields based on their spectral differences. An adaptive thresholding algorithm addresses class imbalance across the early and late harvest stages. The framework was validated in Wuchang and Huaxian (China) and central Iowa (US), achieving F1 scores of 85–98 %, outperforming existing unsupervised approaches and vegetation indices. Therefore, this is a novel method for near-real-time harvest event detection, enabling label-free, rapid, and large-scale monitoring to support agricultural management under increasing weather risks.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: V-BUILD: A graph Transformer-based decision framework for selective updating of vector building data
abstract: Keeping vector building databases current requires deciding which database operations should be applied, rather than merely detecting binary geometric differences. Minor discrepancies caused by acquisition noise, representation style, or cartographic generalization may trigger unnecessary updates when using hand-tuned geometric thresholds. We present V-BUILD, a hybrid decision framework that assigns each matched building unit one of four operations: addition, deletion, replacement, or preservation. Deterministic rules handle existential decisions, while a geometry-aware graph Transformer learns the more ambiguous morphological decisions between replacement and preservation directly in the vector domain. The model encodes 1:1 to m:n matching relationships via Unified Correspondence Graphs and uses Adaptive Multi-stream Fusion to integrate node-, edge-, and graph-level geometric descriptors. Experiments on Amsterdam TOP10NL, Hamburg LoD1, and Mercer County OSM data, together with a difficult Amsterdam subset, show that V-BUILD performs well in within-domain evaluations on both authoritative and crowdsourced vector data, while leave-one-domain-out analysis indicates that direct cross-source transfer remains challenging under strong domain shift. On Amsterdam, V-BUILD achieves the best Replacement F1 of 89.44 %; on Mercer, it obtains the best Macro F1 of 88.51 %, outperforming the strongest GNN baseline by 4.22 percentage points; and on the difficult Amsterdam subset, it achieves a 4.51-percentage-point higher Replacement F1 than the strongest GNN baseline, with the associated reduction in paired sample-level errors confirmed by a two-sided exact McNemar test. These results indicate that V-BUILD reduces dependence on manually tuned geometric decision thresholds and provides a practical decision module for incremental vector building database updating.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Early detection of rice bacterial leaf blight disease using canopy hyperspectral data and machine learning
abstract: Bacterial leaf blight (BLB) remains a major biotic constraint to global rice production, requiring faster and scalable detection methods than conventional field scouting to minimise yield losses. Early detection of BLB is essential for timely intervention and yield protection, yet very few studies have examined the use of remote sensing, particularly during the early growth phase of the rice crop. This study evaluated the potential of canopy-level hyperspectral data for identifying BLB in early vegetative phase.
