title: DATerra: Boundary and structure aware domain adaptation for cross-regional terraced parcel extraction
abstract: Irregular agricultural parcels, particularly terraced fields, exhibit complex geometries and fine-scale boundaries that are highly sensitive to cross-regional variations in imaging conditions and landscape patterns. Although unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) has shown promise for remote sensing segmentation under domain shifts, most existing methods primarily focus on semantic alignment while failing to adequately preserve boundary geometry and parcel-level structural consistency, often leading to boundary adhesion and distorted parcel delineation in target domains. To address these limitations, we propose DATerra, a boundary and structure aware domain adaptation framework for cross-regional terraced parcel extraction. The framework couples two architecture-level boundary-modeling modules with two training-level structure-preserving strategies: (i) Boundary-Guided Attention Fusion (BGAF), which injects geometry-aware cues into multi-scale feature learning; (ii) Boundary-aware Uncertainty-guided Gating (BUDG), which selectively refines ambiguous boundary regions while preserving reliable parcel interiors; and (iii) Parcel Structural Consistency (PSC), together with Structure-Aware ClassMix (SA-ClassMix), which promotes stable parcel predictions under partial target-domain observations and preserves parcel–boundary structural units during cross-domain mixing. Extensive experiments on the GTPBD-China benchmark, covering four geographic regions and twelve cross-domain transfer scenarios, demonstrate that DATerra substantially improves boundary delineation and object-level parcel integrity. On average, DATerra improves OIS and ODS by 14.00 and 10.76 percentage points, respectively, while reducing GUC and GTC by 20.14 and 9.98 points compared with the runner-up methods. Pixel-level metrics are also consistently improved, with an average gain of 1.23%. These results highlight the importance of explicitly modeling boundary geometry and structural consistency for robust cross-regional terraced parcel extraction.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Context-aware quantile baselines for disturbance detection in non-stationary short-rotation forest plantations
abstract: Disturbances such as pests, diseases, fire, windthrow, and drought are increasingly affecting forests and require near-real-time monitoring from satellite observations. Existing near-real-time methods often detect anomalies relative to historical vegetation index (VI) baselines based on periodic, parametric, or autoregressive models, which can be difficult to apply in short-rotation plantations with strongly non-stationary canopy dynamics. We introduce the FOrest plantation Canopy ALert system (FOCAL), a monitoring framework designed for relatively homogeneous, intensively managed short-rotation plantations that combines pixel-level Quantile Regression Forest baseline prediction with rule-based detection of persistent negative anomalies. For each new Sentinel-2 acquisition, FOCAL first predicts the range of VI values expected under undisturbed conditions from stand age, management variables, environmental conditions, acquisition geometry, and recent VI observations. A disturbance alert is then issued when observed VI values fall below the lower bound of this predicted contextual range for consecutive acquisitions. FOCAL was evaluated using 118 Eucalyptus plantation stands in Brazil affected by confirmed disturbance events, 141 undisturbed reference stands, and a controlled mortality-patch experiment. Using NDVI, FOCAL achieved a mean class accuracy of 0.78 and a binary F1-score of 0.76, outperforming benchmark time-series methods. Detection was particularly strong for fire (100%) and severe water stress (84%), and mortality patches as small as 12 × 12 m were identified. These results demonstrate FOCAL’s potential for disturbance detection in intensively managed Eucalyptus plantations.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: An RTE-guided mixture-of-experts framework for AMSR2 passive microwave soil moisture retrieval
abstract: Systematic biases remain evident in the JAXA AMSR2 soil moisture product, particularly in densely vegetated and arid regions where vegetation, surface roughness, and soil emission interact nonlinearly. This study developed an RTE-guided mixture-of-experts (MoE) framework for AMSR2 soil moisture retrieval by combining iterative proxy-label refinement with a gated end-to-end MoE network trained on 14-channel brightness temperatures. Global data from 2020 were used for proxy-label refinement and model training. Temporally independent AMSR2 data from 2024 were used for cross-year proxy-reference consistency evaluation, and representative seasonal datasets from 2023 were used to assess seasonal robustness. Independent validation was conducted using International Soil Moisture Network (ISMN) in situ observations. In the pooled ISMN comparison, the proposed method reduced MAE from 0.048 to 0.034 m 3 /m 3 and RMSE from 0.068 to 0.046 m 3 /m 3 relative to the JAXA product, with ubRMSE = 0.046 m 3 /m 3 , R = 0.825, and R-anom = 0.709. The refined-label MoE also outperformed the MoE trained directly on JAXA-initialized labels, reducing MAE from 0.039 to 0.034 m 3 /m 3 and RMSE from 0.055 to 0.046 m 3 /m 3 . Regionally, MAE and RMSE decreased from 0.058 to 0.041 m 3 /m 3 and from 0.093 to 0.055 m 3 /m 3 over the tropical LABFLUX network, and from 0.029 to 0.025 m 3 /m 3 and from 0.047 to 0.033 m 3 /m 3 over the semi-arid REMEDHUS network. In the 2024 proxy-reference consistency evaluation, the 14-channel configuration achieved MAE = 0.012 m 3 /m 3 and R = 0.936, indicating high emulation fidelity rather than independent accuracy. These results suggest that the proposed framework improves agreement with in situ observations while maintaining strong proxy-reference consistency.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Multimodal loess cave extraction using LMUNet-RCAM: Integrating hillshade and RGB features with local attention mechanisms
abstract: Loess caves (LCs), a typical type of micro-landform widely distributed across the Chinese Loess Plateau, constitute a significant geological hazard. Accurate identification of LCs is essential for mitigating risks to human life, infrastructure, and environment. However, the complex morphology and subtle topographic expression of LCs present substantial challenges for reliable detection. This study proposes LMUNet-RCAM, an improved global–local feature enhancement network that integrates hillshade information derived from Digital Elevation Models (DEMs) to improve representation robustness. To address the irregular spatial patterns of LCs, the network incorporates novel Local Transformer mMoBA(LM) to refine feature representations prior to their input into the U-Net backbone, thereby expanding the effective receptive field in both global and local contexts. Furthermore, a Recurrent Convolutional Attention Module (RCAM) is introduced to enhance spatial and channel-wise semantic discrimination. Within RCAM, Gated-Swin-RNN (G-S-R) is employed to reconstruct local feature sequences, improving network stability under complex terrain conditions. Extensive experiments on test area demonstrate that LMUNet-RCAM consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art semantic segmentation methods in LCs detection.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Vegetation canopy height retrieval in complex mountainous regions based on data calibration and CNN model
abstract: Vegetation canopy height is a vital metric for quantifying aboveground biomass, evaluating ecosystem integrity, and informing forest management strategies, playing a pivotal role in climate change mitigation and sustainable forestry. However, accurate estimation of canopy height faces three major challenges: topographic complexity in mountainous regions, landscape spatial heterogeneity, and inherent limitations of spaceborne LiDAR systems (e.g., GEDI) in detecting low-stature vegetation. This study proposes a regional calibration approach for GEDI-derived height labels and integrates the calibrated labels with multi-source remote sensing data to retrieve canopy height at 10 m resolution. Key findings demonstrate that: (1) The calibration model that couples Random Forest Regression and Multiple Linear Regression can effectively mitigate GEDI’s overestimation of low-stature vegetation and provide reliable label data for subsequent canopy height mapping; (2) Among all feature combinations, optical imagery emerged as the most influential contributor to model performance, significantly improving predictive accuracy when included; (3) The optimized model achieves a mean absolute error (MAE) of 2.26 m against field measurements, showing strong consistency with airborne LiDAR validation (MAE = 2.63 m). Qualitative evaluations highlight the model’s heightened sensitivity to diverse land cover types, enabling more precise delineation of vegetation boundaries. The calibrated height labels further improve the characterization of canopy height across forest, shrub, and grassland areas. These results demonstrate the potential of GEDI label calibration combined with multi-source remote sensing data for large-scale canopy height mapping in complex mountainous regions.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Learning instance-level semantic Gaussian representations for occlusion-aware urban scene reconstruction from UAV imagery
abstract: UAV-based earth observation provides an efficient and flexible means for detailed urban geospatial modeling and digital twin construction. However, in complex urban environments, foreground occlusions caused by trees, vegetation, and other clutter frequently lead to incomplete structures, contaminated textures, and inconsistent observations across views, thereby reducing the quality and usability of reconstructed urban products. Existing methods still struggle in such scenarios, not only because of severe occlusion itself, but also because they lack a representation at the instance level that can explicitly distinguish target urban structures from occluding interference in 3D space. Without such a representation, Gaussian primitives tend to become entangled across semantic regions, which limits reliable separation between target urban structures and occluders, accurate boundary delineation, and consistent urban scene reconstruction across views from UAV imagery. To address this issue, this paper proposes a semantic Gaussian learning framework at the instance level, enhanced by foundation priors, for urban scene reconstruction from UAV imagery. Specifically, high-level semantic, segmentation, and structural priors extracted from vision foundation models are introduced to guide semantic Gaussian representation learning at the instance level in 3D space. On this basis, an Instance-level Semantic Gaussian Module is designed to inject prior-enhanced semantics into Gaussian primitives, enabling more discriminative representation learning at the instance level. Furthermore, a Prior-guided Interaction Module is developed to establish effective collaboration between visual prior features and 3D Gaussian representations, so that RGB appearance semantics and 3D spatial structure can be jointly encoded within a unified semantic and structural representation. Benefiting from this design, the learned Gaussian representation provides a reliable basis for instance separation, missing-region localization, and consistent urban scene reconstruction across views under severe occlusions. Experimental results on multiple datasets demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms representative baselines in instance separation accuracy, boundary quality, and rendering consistency. The results further show that the proposed representation effectively alleviates instance boundary overlap and category confusion, while improving the completeness, consistency, and usability of urban geospatial products derived from UAV imagery.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Challenges in heating demand modelling based on the Kleczków district in Wrocław, Poland
abstract: Positive Energy Districts (PEDs) are a cornerstone of the European Union’s climate neutrality agenda, aiming to create urban areas that are energy-efficient, energy-flexible, and capable of producing an annual surplus of renewable energy. This study assesses the potential for establishing a PED in the Kleczków district of Wrocław, Poland, as part of the DigiTwins4PEDs project. A high-resolution 3D LoD2 (Level of Detail) CityGML building model of Kleczków district was generated and the SimStadt energy simulation platform was employed to simulate annual and monthly heating demand. Model performance was evaluated using the simulation-to-measurement ratio for annual heating demand, complemented by the Normalized Mean Bias Error (NMBE) and the Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE). The aggregated district-level simulation-to-measurement ratio was 84.1 %, with an NMBE of − 15.9 %, while the annual building-level MAPE for residential buildings reached 42.4 %. Key challenges included incomplete building attribute data, typology mismatches between German and modern Polish standards, sparse and aggregated consumption data, and limitations in modelling complex non-residential buildings. The study demonstrates that integrating detailed 3D city models with urban energy simulations is a viable approach for PED feasibility analysis and can guide targeted retrofitting, renewable integration, and energy flexibility strategies in diverse European urban contexts. However, robust calibration requires access to localised building-physics parameters and occupancy-usage profiles, without which PED-oriented energy modelling outputs may significantly deviate from real-world performance.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Automated conversion of unstructured mesh models to structured parametric CAD models for architectural applications
abstract: Parametric models are foundational to Building Information Modeling (BIM) and digital construction, enabling efficient design, analysis, and lifecycle management. However, most 3D building models reconstructed from real-world data sources — such as 3D scanning, photogrammetry, or format conversion — are represented as unstructured mesh models. Although these meshes accurately capture geometric shape, they typically lack the parametric constraints, design intent, and procedural history inherent to native BIM objects. This semantic deficiency severely limits their direct applicability in workflows that require model editing, parametric adjustment, or semantic interpretation. To address this challenge, this paper presents an automated framework for semantic lifting of unstructured architectural mesh models into structured, procedural parametric CAD models. The proposed pipeline first analyzes the geometric and topological characteristics of the input mesh and employs a deep learning-based module to predict a plausible sequence of CAD modeling operations. Subsequently, a 2D parametric profile abstraction and parameterization module processes the geometric regions involved in the predicted operations, transforming them into constrained and editable 2D parametric profiles composed of basic geometric primitives, such as lines, arcs, and circles. Finally, a parameterization-driven reconstruction module executes the recovered operation sequence and parametric planar profiles within a CAD environment to procedurally regenerate a structured solid model with full parametric editability. Extensive experiments on diverse architectural datasets demonstrate the robustness of the proposed approach, showing that it can generate parametric CAD models that closely match the original mesh geometry while supporting reliable parameter-driven editing. This research provides an effective pathway for the semantic lifting of mesh-based building models, enabling their reuse in BIM reconstruction, digital twins, and architectural analysis applications.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: A two-stage transformer framework for reconstructing hourly 1 km all-weather land surface temperature using cross-scale transfer learning
abstract: High spatiotemporal resolution land surface temperature (LST) reconstruction is essential for analyzing land-atmosphere interactions and thermal environmental dynamics. Thermal infrared observations, the primary source of regional and global LST, are affected by cloud contamination, scale discrepancies, and distribution shifts. Meanwhile, reconstruction methods struggle to provide both hourly continuity and kilometer-scale detail, and cross-scale fusion often causes spatial over-smoothing. To address these limitations, we propose ST-LSTrans, a two-stage Transformer framework for reconstructing regional hourly 1 km all-weather LST. It uses cross-scale transfer learning with global pre-training on hourly ∼6.25 km CLDAS LST to capture regional thermodynamic evolution and local fine-tuning on four-times-daily 1000 m MODIS LST to recover kilometer-scale thermal heterogeneity. A KL divergence constraint is introduced to reduce distribution shifts and spatial over-smoothing during cross-scale fusion. Validation results based on multi-source datasets show that the global pre-training stage achieved an average RMSE of 1.13 K, while the local fine-tuning stage achieved an average RMSE of 1.06 K, with the minimum RMSE reaching 0.87 K. Independent Landsat validation showed that the reconstructed product achieved a scene-averaged RMSE of 2.98 K and improved upon the original CLDAS background field. Additional evaluations against VIIRS VNP21, which is generated using an independent temperature-emissivity separation algorithm, confirmed the cross-sensor consistency of the reconstructed LST. Ground-based observations further demonstrated that ST-LSTrans preserved realistic diurnal temperature cycle characteristics under both clear-sky and persistent cloudy conditions. SHAP analysis further revealed scale-dependent transitions in LST driving mechanisms from coarse-scale atmospheric forcing to kilometer-scale terrain and land surface controls. This study provides a unified and interpretable modelling framework for high spatiotemporal resolution LST reconstruction and driving mechanism analysis.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Editorial Board
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: AdaGeo-SR: Geo-semantic-guided super-resolution of sentinel-2 imagery with AlphaEarth foundation priors
abstract: Remote sensing image super-resolution is an important approach for enhancing the spatial detail of Earth observation data. In super-resolving Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery from 10 m to 2.5 m, conventional single-image super-resolution (SISR) methods are largely constrained by purely pixel-driven mechanisms. As a result, they often produce structural discontinuities, blurred edges, and chromatic artifacts when reconstructing complex human-made objects such as narrow roads and farmland boundaries during cross-scale detail reconstruction. To address these limitations, this study proposes a geo-semantic-guided remote sensing super-resolution framework, termed AdaGeo-SR. The framework incorporates dense spatial feature maps extracted from AlphaEarth Foundation (AEF) as geo-semantic priors, providing additional geo-semantic and topological cues for the reconstruction process. To better leverage high-level semantic features, we further design a degradation-simulation-based feature balancing mechanism. By introducing specific degradation conditions during training, this mechanism encourages the network to reduce its over-reliance on the original pixel cues, thereby enhancing its use of external geo-semantic priors. Experiments on the OpenSR-Test and WorldStrat benchmarks show that AdaGeo-SR effectively suppresses structural distortions and hallucination artifacts while maintaining reasonable spectral consistency, leading to improved local geometric coherence. In addition, downstream road extraction experiments using SAM_Road on the NAIP test set further demonstrate that the super-resolved images produced by the proposed framework help reduce mask fragmentation and topological discontinuities. These results highlight the potential of the proposed framework for downstream structure-sensitive tasks and support the generation of structurally more reliable 2.5 m imagery for practical remote sensing applications.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Biophysical effects of afforestation on local land surface temperature in china: A comprehensive analysis incorporating forest age and afforestation intensity
abstract: Afforestation changes the surface biogeochemical and biophysical processes and thus affects land surface temperature (LST). The historic studies on the LST effect of afforestation ignored the variation of energy exchange caused by the difference in forest structure such as LAI, vegetation fraction, and canopy height that is directly related to forest age. In this study, we constructed a model of the Land Surface Temperature Effect from Afforestation (LSTEA) considering forest age and afforestation intensity for different climate zones in China and then analyzed the biophysical effects on LST from historical and future afforestation in China. Results showed that (1) the LSTEA model revealed significant spatial and seasonal variability, with minimal warming effects in winter and pronounced cooling effects in other seasons. (2) from 1990 to 2020, the total national afforestation area reached 71.44 × 10 4 km 2 , of which 78.2 % originated from cropland and 12 % from grassland. The current afforestation has induced a grid-/national cooling effect of −0.35 ℃/-0.29 ℃ in summer and −0.26 ℃/-0.21 ℃ in winter by 2021. (3) The projected afforestation initiatives are projected to induce progressively intensifying cooling effects during 2030–2100. By 2100, it will bring a summer grid-/national cooling effect of −1.29 ℃/-0.51 ℃, −0.90 ℃/-0.35 ℃ and −0.75 ℃/-0.28 ℃ under the SSP-RCP2.6, SSP2-RCP4.5 and SSP5-RCP8.5 scenario respectively. The projected years of 2060 in SSP1-RCP2.6, 2070 in SSP-RCP4.5, and SSP-RCP8.5 will be the time that the maximum of LST effects in the near decades. Our study highlights the important role of afforestation as a mitigation strategy for climate change.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: A spatiotemporal reconstruction framework for GRACE/GRACE-FO-derived groundwater storage anomalies based on historical phase-constrained gap filling and physics-guided global–local downscaling
abstract: Observations from the Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment (GRACE) and GRACE Follow-On (GRACE-FO) provide essential information on terrestrial water storage anomalies (TWSA), from which groundwater storage anomalies (GWSA) can be derived. However, the approximately 11-month mission gap and the coarse spatial resolution of the original products constrain their application in regional groundwater monitoring and water-resource assessment. This study developed an integrated spatiotemporal reconstruction framework for the Three-North Region of China by combining historical phase-constrained gap filling with physics-guided global–local downscaling. First, a Kling-Gupta Efficiency-based singular spectrum analysis method (KGC-SSA) was developed to reconstruct the mission gap without external forcing data. Second, a physics-guided global–local-residual geographically weighted extreme gradient boosting framework (GLR-GWXGB) was developed to downscale GWSA to 1 km under grid-wise coarse-scale consistency constraints. KGC-SSA yielded a mean ensemble reconstruction spread of 0.06 cm during the mission gap and performed broadly comparably to benchmark methods. Relative to the global benchmark model, GLR-GWXGB improved internal validation performance, preserved regional-scale consistency with the original GRACE-derived GWSA, and enhanced local spatial detail. Correlations with groundwater observations improved at more than 70% of monitoring sites. The reconstructed 1 km product further captured persistent groundwater-storage decline during 2002–2022, with intensified depletion after approximately 2012, while retaining the dominant long-term and seasonal characteristics of the original series. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides a robust approach for generating temporally continuous and spatially refined groundwater-storage information from GRACE/GRACE-FO observations.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Adaptive background suppression-based plume identification, emission estimation, and ground validation of coal mine methane in Changzhi, Shanxi, China
abstract: This study developed a coal mine methane remote-sensing monitoring framework centered on adaptive background suppression using high-spatial-resolution multispectral data from Sentinel-2. The framework integrates methane column enhancement retrieval, automated plume detection, and emission flux estimation. Specifically, bilateral filtering and the multi-band single-pass (MBSP) method were used to retrieve methane column enhancements; a methane plume detection algorithm combining NDVI-based stratification, adaptive segmentation, morphological processing, and wind-field constraints was developed; and coal mine methane emission fluxes were quantified using the integrated mass enhancement (IME) method. Application to a pilot coal enterprise in Changzhi during 2024 demonstrated that the proposed framework effectively reduced weak vegetation-background effects and heterogeneous high-intensity interference while preserving plume topological consistency. Sentinel-2 also provided an observation frequency more than eight times higher than that of EMIT. The mean satellite-derived emission rate for the pilot enterprise was 1023.57 ± 266.84 kg ⋅ h − 1 , with a mean relative deviation of 14.47% from ground-based measurements. The relatively large deviations and daily-scale fluctuations observed during some periods were mainly attributed to uncertainties associated with the spectral resolution of Sentinel-2, surface heterogeneity, algorithm parameter settings, and ERA5 wind-field data. A comparison with the EDGAR inventory revealed broad consistency in regional spatial emission patterns. However, the higher-resolution Sentinel-2 data detected potential coal-related emission signals in several grid cells absent from EDGAR, accounting for 22.2% of the potential emission grids identified in Changzhi. On a regional scale, EDGAR’s annual emission estimate for Changzhi was 32.11% higher than the Sentinel-2 annualized estimate derived in this study.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Kinematic pattern interpretation of railway-corridor deformation from InSAR time series with transfer learning-based TCN
abstract: Railway-corridor deformation monitoring requires timely identification of localized displacement anomalies and characterization of their temporal evolution. Time-series Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) provides spatially dense and high-precision displacement observations from repeated SAR acquisitions, but InSAR-based railway studies have largely remained rate-centered, leaving the kinematic information embedded in displacement time series insufficiently exploited. This study develops a kinematic interpretation framework that integrates InSAR displacement time series, transfer learning-based Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) classification, and multi-source environmental data to characterize railway-corridor deformation in terms of its occurrence, temporal evolution, and environmental context. Sentinel-1 images acquired from January 2022 to December 2024 were processed to retrieve LOS displacement rates and displacement time series along the Kunming–Yuxi section of the China–Laos Railway. To reduce dependence on labeled InSAR samples, a transfer learning strategy was adopted, in which the TCN was pre-trained using simulated displacement sequences and fine-tuned with labeled InSAR observations to classify six kinematic patterns: stable, linear, step, piecewise linear, power-law, and undefined. The corridor is generally stable, with a mean displacement rate of −0.26 mm/year and stable points accounting for 77.96% of observations. Linear and step patterns account for 12.66% and 7.87%, respectively. Strong subsidence zones, where the localized displacement rate reaches −28.43 mm/year, are dominated by linear deformation. Pattern-based interpretation further shows that non-stable deformation is associated with Quaternary unconsolidated sediments, paddy soils, fine-grained soil textures, and urban expansion areas. These results indicate that InSAR-derived kinematic patterns provide an effective interpretive layer for linking railway-corridor displacement, temporal evolution, and environmental context.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Relaxing the clear-sky assumption: Cloud-tolerant spatiotemporal fusion via mask-guided feature modulation and temporal-memory collaboration
abstract: The precise characterization of dynamic Earth surface processes relies on time-series remote sensing imagery with both high spatial fidelity and frequent temporal coverage. While spatiotemporal fusion (STF) bridges this resolution trade-off by integrating complementary observations, its practical application remains constrained by the idealized ”clear-sky assumption”. This requirement often favors the selection of temporally distant cloud-free acquisitions over temporally closer but cloud-contaminated observations, potentially reducing the relevance of reference information. To address this limitation, we propose CloudSTF, a robust framework designed to achieve high-fidelity reconstruction by effectively exploiting partially occluded observations. Our approach employs a Mask-guided Multi-scale Swin Transformer (M 2 ST) encoder to capture cloud spatial patterns and suppress noise propagation during feature extraction. This is coupled with a Cross-temporal Memory-guided Fusion (CTMF) module that adaptively integrates temporal trends with textural details retrieved from a spatio-temporal memory bank. To validate this paradigm, we introduce the Global Cloud-shrouded Regions (GCR-STF) benchmark, a geographically distributed dataset comprising 24 representative agricultural and urban sites across six continents. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CloudSTF consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods. Additional assessments across varying cloud densities and diverse landscapes further demonstrate the robustness and applicability of CloudSTF under realistic cloud-contaminated conditions. These results suggest that CloudSTF provides a reliable solution for continuous Earth monitoring in realistic, cloud-prone environments. Source code and the GCR-STF benchmark are available at https://github.com/Sichen-Lu/CloudSTF .
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Estimating supraglacial lake bottom ablation rates by integrating ICESat-2 repeat track data and multi-temporal sentinel-2 imagery
abstract: Supraglacial lakes are widely distributed across the Greenland Ice Sheet (GrIS) each summer. The resulting meltwater-enhanced ablation effect plays a critical role in understanding the GrIS surface mass balance but remains poorly quantified. Inspired by the insight that longer meltwater persistence leads to stronger meltwater-enhanced ablation, this study proposes a novel method to directly estimate supraglacial lake bottom ablation rates at centimeter-per-day scale using satellite observations. First, we map multi-temporal supraglacial lake extents from Sentinel-2 imagery to estimate cumulative meltwater-covered days. Then, we derive ablation depths at the lake bottom and surrounding bare ice by differencing ICESat-2 repeat track data acquired before and during the melt season. Next, we perform linear fitting between lake bottom ablation depths and cumulative meltwater-covered days along the ICESat-2 tracks to calculate both the lake bottom ablation rate and the bare ice ablation rate. Finally, we evaluate the magnitude of the meltwater-enhanced ablation effect. We apply this method to 26 supraglacial lakes across the GrIS and identify a positive linear relationship between lake bottom ablation depths and cumulative water-covered days (mean Pearson correlation coefficient r = 0.70 ± 0.14, p < 0.001). The fitted mean lake bottom ablation rate (4.50 ± 1.15 cm/day) significantly exceeds the mean bare ice ablation rate (1.98 ± 0.52 cm/day). Meltwater in supraglacial lakes therefore enhances ablation rate by ∼ 1.3 ± 0.5 times, with values ranging from 0.6 to 2.4, consistent with previous field measurements (1.1–1.4 times) and numerical model simulations (1.1–1.7 times). In summary, this study provides a first quantitative satellite-based estimate of meltwater-enhanced ablation across the GrIS under varying ablation intensities, and may improve our understanding of GrIS surface melt process.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Enhanced early warning of extreme river discharge events in the Yangtze River Basin using atmospheric circulation signals
abstract: Early warning of extreme river discharge events (ERDEs) is crucial for water resources management and disaster reduction in the Yangtze River Basin (YRB), yet substantial uncertainty remains in their prediction. This study proposes a novel strategy to enhance ERDE early warning by detecting its associated atmospheric circulation signals. We develop DetRF, a machine learning model that integrates anomaly detection with a balanced random forest ensemble. DetRF was trained and validated using ERA5 reanalysis data from 2000 to 2019 and independently applied to 2020–2024, with its early warning performance evaluated against satellite-based precipitation and reanalysis river discharge data. Across eight subregions of the YRB, DetRF effectively detects ERDE-related atmospheric circulation signals, achieving mean recall, precision, and F1 score values of 0.756, 0.506, and 0.576, respectively, and consistently outperforming benchmark machine learning models. The detected signals accurately capture key synoptic features associated with hydrological extremes, including the positions and intensities of troughs, vortices, and cyclones, as well as moisture transport. More than 99% of the detected signals are followed by precipitation within five days, while persistent precipitation occurs in over 67% of cases across both local and upstream regions. More importantly, an average of 93.8% of DetRF-detected circulation signals are followed by at least one ERDE within the subsequent five days. These findings establish a direct link between specific atmospheric circulation signals and subsequent hydrological extremes, offering a new pathway for extending ERDE early warning beyond conventional hydrological prediction. The proposed framework is particularly promising for regions where hydrological observations are sparse.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: A Targeted–Refined Framework for wind turbine detection integrating AlphaEarth Foundations and high-resolution multispectral satellite imagery
abstract: The rapid expansion of clean energy systems, particularly wind and solar power, has made large-scale monitoring of related infrastructure using satellite remote sensing increasingly important yet challenging. Conventional wind turbine detection approaches rely on pixel-level analysis of high-resolution imagery or sliding-window strategies. These methods often suffer from computational redundancy, low efficiency, and high false-positive rates, making them inadequate for supporting large-area surveys and operational monitoring. To address these limitations, this study proposes a Targeted–Refined framework based on AlphaEarth Foundations. First, a wind turbine sample database was constructed for model training and evaluation in Tianjin. In the Targeted Candidate Screening stage, a lightweight multi-layer perceptron classifier exploits the geospatial representations provided by AEF, enabling rapid identification of candidate regions while reducing the search space to approximately 5% of the original image patches. In the Refined Detection stage, high-resolution Jilin-1 satellite imagery is incorporated, and a YOLO model performs precise detection within the candidate regions. Experimental results show that the proposed framework achieves a recall of 96.85%, a precision of 98.41%, and an F1-score of 97.63% on the Tianjin test set. Furthermore, the trained model is directly applied to the plains of the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei region (excluding Tianjin) for cross-regional evaluation, where it identifies 1,580 wind turbines with an F1-score of 91.33%, demonstrating strong generalization capability. Overall, this framework provides an efficient and scalable solution for detecting large-scale, spatially sparse objects, and offers a practical approach for infrastructure inventory and monitoring of wind farms and similar assets.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Multi-angular assessment of early-season defoliation: Evaluating the sensitivity of vegetation indices to NPV visibility in temperate broadleaved forests
abstract: Early-season forest decline in temperate broadleaved stands often lacks detectable biochemical stress signals, manifesting primarily through reduced foliage density and increased visibility of non-photosynthetic vegetation (NPV). This study investigated the spectral separability of green leaves and NPV components under varying levels of canopy defoliation. Using a crane platform, we collected in situ leaf- and canopy-level spectrometer measurements alongside co-aligned photography to quantify the visible fraction of NPV. We analyzed the multi-angular reflectance characteristics and evaluated 35 vegetation indices (VIs) —including green biomass metrics and specialized NPV indices —using Random Forest to identify optimal spectral and geometric configurations. Sunlit young foliage exhibited high forward scatter, creating a nadir reflectance minimum. At canopy level, a nadir minimum was driven by the gap distribution resulting from sustainable forest management practices. Consequently, the optimal viewing angle for top-ranking VIs (e.g., SNC BAO , Ctr 2 , mNDVI 705 ) was near the hotspot geometry, minimizing shadowing and forest floor interference. While the total visible fraction of NPV remained mostly insensitive to viewing angles, its shaded proportion varied. VIs targeting green vegetation via red-edge and NIR domains consistently outperformed dedicated NPV indices based on SWIR cellulose and lignin absorption. This is attributed to low upper-canopy SWIR transmittance, which obscured the signals of the largely shaded NPV fraction. Top-performing VIs achieved R 2 = 0.92 for NPV visibility prediction, improving by 21 % over the best SWIR indices and 11 % over the nadir view. To accurately detect initial defoliation and overcome forest floor interference, adopting off-nadir viewing geometries is advantageous for capturing the optimal signal.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Analysis of intraday urban thermal anisotropy and downward shortwave radiation through UAV experiment and coupled model
abstract: The pronounced thermal radiation anisotropy observed in rapidly urbanizing areas arises from the complex interplay of solar downward shortwave radiation (DSWR), building geometry, and local topography. To address this, we propose a novel framework, termed GRay-AU3SM-IRT, for the analysis of urban thermal anisotropy (UTA). The study was conducted in a representative mountainous city in Chongqing, China. A specific 0.4 × 0.4 km 2 area, characterized by buildings and terrain on 10° slopes, was selected for analysis at hourly resolution. The simulations showed strong agreement with measured data, achieving a root mean square error below 0.46 K and a coefficient of determination exceeding 0.79. The analysis reveals that UTA shows pronounced diurnal variations: it intensifies gradually in the morning, peaks at solar noon with clear hotspot formation, and generates secondary hotspots in the afternoon due to changing solar azimuth and slope effects. The morning striped distribution pattern caused by building geometry diminishes with declining solar irradiance and disappears by afternoon. Diurnal trends in the UTA Effect (UTAE), directional brightness temperature (DBT), DBT Effect (DBTE), and DSWR are generally aligned. Notably, UTAE and DBTE peak before DSWR, while both maximum and minimum DBT peak later. The proposed framework offers key advantages: precise multi-lap UAV navigation, minimized motion artifacts, consistent temporal sampling via adaptive velocity control, gap-filling through simulation, and spatio-temporal outlier correction. It provides critical data for angle normalization and correction across diverse urban environments.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Unsupervised soft-min fusion of multi-sensor turbidity products using Gaussian mixture models
abstract: Turbidity is a key indicator of water quality and particulate dynamics, making its accurate monitoring essential for aquatic ecosystem management. While satellite remote sensing enables large-scale turbidity observation, products derived from different sensors often exhibit inconsistencies due to differences in spectral responses, residual atmospheric effects, and viewing geometries. Effectively integrating such multi-source data in the absence of ground truth remains a significant challenge. Here, we propose Gaussian mixture model-based soft-min (GMMS), a fully unsupervised fusion framework in which neither model construction nor weight estimation relies on ground-truth turbidity observations. GMMS integrates Gaussian mixture modeling with a soft-min weighting strategy to identify latent error-structure contexts and adaptively assign sensor weights according to relative residual stability. By exploiting inter-sensor error characteristics, the framework enables context-aware data fusion. At the overall scale, GMMS significantly outperforms triple collocation (TC) and extended triple collocation for maximized correlation (ETCC) ( p < 0.05). Compared with in situ turbidity observations, GMMS increases the correlation coefficient from 0.798 to 0.841 and reduces the RMSE from 16.849 to 15.921 TU. Site-level evaluations further indicate enhanced robustness and reduced performance variability across monitoring stations. Simulation experiments confirm that GMMS achieves the greatest and most stable performance gains under conditions of moderate-to-high error-structure separability. Overall, GMMS provides an interpretable and transferable unsupervised fusion framework for improving multi-source satellite-derived turbidity estimates in complex riverine environments.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Remote-sensing-assisted and in situ-constrained reconstruction of 4-hourly chlorophyll-a dynamics in inland lakes using vision Mamba and temporal attention
abstract: Chlorophyll a (Chl-a) is widely used to indicate eutrophication and bloom risk in inland waters, but daily Sentinel-3 observations alone cannot resolve transient sub-daily variability represented in partially observed 4-hourly in situ Chl-a records. This study therefore develops VGTA (Vision Mamba–GKOA–TCN-Attention), a staged remote-sensing-assisted and in situ-constrained framework that integrates daily Sentinel-3 OLCI-derived priors with partially observed 4-hourly in situ Chl-a sequences and binary observation masks. A 20-dimensional OLCI-derived feature space provides spectral–spatial priors for Chl-a estimation and bloom-risk state identification. GKOA optimizes TCN-Attention to reconstruct masked values within partially observed 4-hourly in situ Chl-a sequences. Vision Mamba outperformed CNN– and Transformer-based models in Chl-a estimation, achieving 94.8% accuracy, a Macro-F1 score of 0.909, and a Bloom-F1 score of 0.870. Ablation experiments confirmed the contributions of bidirectional contextual modeling, positional embedding, selective state-space modeling, and gating. Under Missing Completely at Random, block-missing, and real missing scenarios, GTA improved reconstruction performance by 12.71–55.54% relative to the best baseline models. Uncertainty increased once continuous gaps reached seven days, defining a practical boundary of data-driven reconstruction. Chl-a fluctuations and bloom-risk transitions can unfold within a day, and daily satellite snapshots may blur their timing or miss short events. Reconstruction of masked time steps within partially observed 4-hourly in situ Chl-a sequences can support earlier identification of bloom-risk transitions, more timely field sampling and management responses, and temporally finer monitoring of inland waters.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Reference-anchored envelope modelling for predicting tree mortality hotspots driven by drought
abstract: Predicting tree mortality hotspots driven by drought remains challenging, since vulnerability to drought is strongly influenced by climate, landform, and substrate. We propose a novel reference-anchored, quantile-envelope susceptibility model-implemented through a reproducible workflow- that exports mortality-resemblance (high-risk) environments from three confirmed tree-mortality footprints (training AOIs), based on semi-arid conifer and evergreen sclerophyllous forests in Cyprus, to produce wide screening layers. The approach combines (i) physiographic similarity derived from AOI-calibrated envelopes for slope, multi-scale topographic position and curvature (broad quantiles; majority-rule), (ii) exposure constraints via circular aspect windows, warm-season solar loading (April-September) and substrate (lithology) filtering, (iii) a drought severity gate (SPEI-12 (Standardized Precipitation-Evapotranspiration Index-12) ≤ -1.4), and (iv) Landsat event-year spectral collapse relative to a fixed 3-year pre-event baseline, coupled with a year + 1 persistence rule to suppress transient stress. Our within-AOI evaluation (forest-only) showed substantial representativeness (coverage 70.49–85.35%), while recovering most reference mortality pixels (recall 67.62–100%). In 2025, two independent mortality sites were identified in Cyprus, coinciding with exceptional drought (SPEI < -2) and a sharp decline in the Normalized Burn Ratio (NBR) consistent with foliage browning, and occurring within high-risk zones as mapped in the final risk map. As a plausibility check, both 2025 sites fell within pre-mapped high-risk zones, with 83.50% and 82.69% of their forested area exceeding HEAT ≥ 0.60 and mean risk scores of 84.91% and 75.55%, respectively. With 18.88% of Cyprus’s total forest flagged as high-risk, the probability of this co-occurrence being random is p ≈ 0.036 (binomial test). Anchoring calibration to local mortality footprints makes the approach readily transferable to other regions with documented events.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Bridging cloud-induced gaps in MODIS leaf area index products using high-frequency geostationary satellite observations
abstract: Leaf Area Index (LAI) is a fundamental variable for characterizing vegetation canopy structure and ecosystem functioning. However, persistent cloud contamination substantially constrains the spatiotemporal continuity of LAI products derived from polar-orbiting satellite observations. In contrast, geostationary satellites provide dense temporal sampling, offering a valuable observational basis for filling data gaps in polar-orbiting satellite products. To bridge this observational gap, this study develops an observation-complementary framework that integrates high-frequency Himawari-8 Advanced Himawari Imager (AHI) observations with MODIS LAI products to achieve LAI reconstruction in cloud-prone regions. Within this framework, AHI observations are first used to retrieve LAI at a spatial resolution of 2 km using a Random Forest model trained with a high-quality MODIS-based benchmark dataset, and are then downscaled to 500 m using MODIS-derived spatial texture information. The reconstructed AHI LAI is subsequently integrated into low-quality or missing MODIS pixels to generate a fused AHI-MODIS LAI dataset over China. Validation against in-situ measurements and cross-comparison results show that the fused product maintains reasonable numerical consistency and stable temporal trajectories. Data availability increases from 70.70% to 90.90% under the 4-day compositing cycle. These results indicate that geostationary-polar-orbiting observation complementarity provides a practical pathway for improving the continuity and usability of optical LAI products in persistently cloudy regions, while remaining subject to the constraints of optical observations and cross-scale reconstruction assumptions.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Atmospheric restoration is a prerequisite for sub-pixel fire mapping: A smoke-robust protocol across five fire regions
abstract: Wildfires exert profound impacts on global ecosystems; however, accurate satellite-based burn area extraction is frequently confounded by the inherent mixed-pixel issue and complex atmospheric conditions. Although sub-pixel mapping (SPM) can resolve the mixed pixel issue, the extent to which its extraction accuracy depends on initial atmospheric preprocessing under diverse haze and smoke conditions remains poorly quantified. Furthermore, the conditions under which such preprocessing remains effective, and the boundary of its operational envelope, are not well understood. This study introduces a Smoke-Robust Sub-pixel Mapping (SRSPM) protocol to systematically diagnose atmospheric preprocessing efficacy prior to SPM. Using both simulated and real atmospheric states across five distinct fire regions, we systematically evaluate the sensitivity of sub-pixel fire perimeter delineation to different levels of haze contamination. Our findings demonstrate that atmospheric scattering inherently degrades the spatial allocation capabilities of SPM, leading to severe omission errors. Restoring contaminated spectral signals is shown to be essential, rather than merely beneficial, for accurate mapping when haze contamination is substantial. Crucially, our quantitative diagnosis reveals the operational limits of the SRSPM protocol: the dehazing benefit grows with haze intensity and remains substantial up to the strongest simulated contamination ( w = 1); in one region it turns positive only beyond w ≈0.73, delineating the quantitative envelope of the SRSPM protocol. Overall, this work establishes the SRSPM protocol as a practical diagnostic tool for quantifying the interaction between atmospheric correction and sub-pixel spatial allocation, providing empirical guidance for operational disaster monitoring in complex atmospheric environments.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: 160 Years of Etna summit craters through a photogrammetry-based time machine
abstract: This study presents a quantitative, multi-temporal assessment of Etna’s summit morpho-structural evolution, spanning a 160-year (1865–2024) period. We integrated historical topographic maps with modern, high-resolution remote sensing data, including Unoccupied Aerial System surveys. Dataset-specific validation and statistical error propagation yielded root mean square errors ranging from decametric values for the earliest cartographic sources to metric values for the post-2020 datasets. The resulting topographic time series was interpreted alongside geological observations and previously published geodetic analyses. This integrated reconstruction documents the transition from a predominantly monocentric summit configuration to a highly dynamic polycentric system, and reveals contrasting morpho-structural behaviours among the four summit craters. VOR is characterized by recent constructive growth, BN and NEC by recurrent infilling followed by subsidence, whereas the SEC exhibits persistent constructive growth accompanied by progressive eastward expansion. These differences are consistent with variations in crater position, structural setting, shallow feeding-system configuration, and dominant eruptive style. The long-term evolution of the summit area is also consistent with the influence of the North-East and South Rift zones, and with published geodetic observations describing the seaward deformation of Etna’s eastern flank. Overall, the reconstructed evolution highlights the interaction between volcanic construction, structural controls, and gravitational deformation in shaping a continuously changing and asymmetric summit system. The proposed geospatial workflow provides a reproducible and transferable framework for integrating heterogeneous historical and modern topographic datasets and for investigating long-term morpho-structural change at other highly active volcanoes.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Elevation-dependent regulation of alpine vegetation productivity by snow cover and grazing on the Tibetan Plateau under a warming–wetting climate
abstract: Grassland productivity on the Tibetan Plateau (TP) is fundamental to regional carbon cycling and ecosystem functioning and is strongly regulated by snow dynamics and grazing under a changing climate. However, the mechanisms by which alpine grassland productivity responds to interacting climatic, cryospheric, and anthropogenic drivers remain poorly constrained. Here, we integrated long-term multi-source Earth observation data to quantify the spatiotemporal trends of grassland gross primary productivity (GPP) across the TP from 1982 to 2018 and examined the relationships between GPP and snow dynamics, climate, and grazing intensity, with an explicit emphasis on elevation-dependent controls. Our results reveal a pronounced nonlinear reorganization of GPP controls along elevation gradients, with a critical transition zone at mid-elevations (∼3500–4000 m). Within this zone, warming exerted the strongest positive association with GPP, while grazing intensity also showed a positive spatial association with GPP. In contrast, at higher elevations (>4500 m), snow dynamics emerged as dominant constraints on GPP. Structural equation modeling further indicates that snow cover duration showed the strongest negative total effect among the modeled environmental variables, whereas grazing intensity showed an elevation – dependent association with GPP, shifting from a positive spatial correlation at mid – elevations to a negative correlation at high elevations. Across all elevation zones, soil moisture-mediated pathways consistently exert stronger controls on GPP than soil temperature pathways, highlighting water availability as the more direct and dominant constraint on alpine grassland productivity. These findings demonstrate that elevation fundamentally regulates the spatial organization of ecosystem productivity controls on the TP and underscore the importance of explicitly accounting for cryosphere–biosphere–human interactions when assessing alpine carbon dynamics under a warming and wetting climate.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Active CO2 lidar extends satellite monitoring of urban fossil-fuel CO2 emissions to high-aerosol cities
abstract: Cities with high aerosol loading are critical yet underserved targets for satellite-based monitoring of urban fossil-fuel CO 2 (ffCO 2 ) emissions, because passive XCO 2 retrievals often suffer from severe data loss and aerosol-induced uncertainty under polluted conditions. Here, we evaluate whether spaceborne active CO 2 lidar can extend satellite carbon monitoring to such observationally challenging environments. We combine CO 2 observations from the DQ-1 Aerosol and Carbon Dioxide Lidar (ACDL) with Sentinel-5P/TROPOMI NO 2 retrievals to construct an active–passive framework. Near-synchronous ACDL–TROPOMI overpasses are used to derive city-specific ffCO 2 -to-NO x emission ratios, which are then applied to TROPOMI-derived daily NO x emissions to reconstruct observation-constrained ffCO 2 variability. Among the top 100 urban ffCO 2 emitters, high-AOD cities are concentrated in the Asia–Pacific region, and under polluted conditions, DQ-1 provides 201.6% and 107.8% more effective CO 2 observations than OCO-2 and OCO-3, respectively. Applications to six high-AOD cities in North China and India reveal physically interpretable seasonal variability, with monthly emission magnitudes broadly consistent with EDGAR and ODIAC inventories (r = 0.79–0.81). These results demonstrate that active CO 2 lidar, when combined with dense NO 2 observations, can provide an independent top-down constraint to support urban carbon monitoring and mitigation assessment in polluted cities where passive carbon satellites are most limited.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Topology-preserving river vectorization via HydroSAM and differentiable graph optimization under coarse labels
abstract: Accurate river-network extraction supports global hydrological management and environmental monitoring. Automated extraction from remote-sensing imagery remains challenging because river morphology is highly variable, fine tributaries have weak visual signals, canopy and infrastructure can obscure channels, and dense annotations are scarce or spatially incomplete. Conventional raster predictions can also be fragmented and lack structural continuity. We present HydroSAM, a three-stage framework for raster extraction and topology-aware vectorization. A frozen SAM 2 Hiera encoder is adapted with QV-LoRA and the proposed Directional Curvilinear Prior Injection (DCPI), while a gated Digital Elevation Model (DEM) branch contributes coarse-scale topographic context. Segmentation is produced in a zero-prompt setting by the native SAM 2 mask decoder. A graph-guided differentiable vectorization stage then converts probability maps into connected parametric river networks. We also present M2Hydro, a benchmark containing 7,947 high-resolution 4096 × 4096 source image-annotation pairs across China. In single-run tests, HydroSAM-MM attains an F1 of 0.6995 and clDice of 0.7753 on M2Hydro. The evaluations indicate that HydroSAM supports parameter-efficient adaptation and is more resilient to the evaluated cross-regional domain shift than the convolutional and Transformer baselines.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Geometry-aware dynamic convolutional network for instance-level segmentation of Martian landforms from high-resolution Digital Elevation Model-derived point clouds
abstract: Analysis and interpretation of Martian surface landforms is one of the key topics in deep-space research, offering insights into the planet’s geological evolution and history of water activity. Automated extraction of Martian landforms can greatly assist researchers in rapidly locating and analyzing regions of interest. Therefore, instance segmentation based on remote sensing data represents a promising direction for automation in planetary science. To address the challenges of indistinct landform boundaries and over-segmentation in Martian remote sensing scenes, we propose an end-to-end 3D deep learning instance segmentation framework based on dynamic convolution. In this framework, we incorporate geometric information prediction of Martian landforms to enhance the network’s perception of morphological characteristics, bluewhich improves the separation of adjacent same-class instances. During training, we introduce two feature-space constraints-“pull” and “push” forces-to reduce intra-instance variance while increasing inter-instance separability. The proposed geometry-aware dynamic convolution framework is evaluated on a self-constructed water-formed landform dataset, an impact crater dataset, and a rock dataset from Mars rover perspective and achieves AP of 41.9 ± 0.1%, 63.7 ± 0.3%, and 68.6 ± 0.2%, remaining competitive with recent transformer-based methods such as Mask3D while outperforming clustering- and dynamic-convolution-based baselines. This end-to-end framework provides valuable technical support for subsequent geomorphological interpretation and potential exploration on Mars.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: FGPMamba: Frequency-geometry prior-guided Mamba for building change detection
abstract: Building change detection (BCD) from high-resolution optical remote sensing imagery supports urban monitoring, land-use mapping, and construction progress assessment. However, in arid emerging-city environments, bare land, construction surfaces, concrete roofs, roads, and shadows may resemble changed buildings, resulting in pseudo changes, incomplete regions, and uncertain boundaries. This study proposes a frequency-geometry prior-guided Mamba network (FGPMamba) that combines global context modeling, phase-preserving frequency-domain feature recalibration, gradient-guided global–local fusion, and absolute-difference-based gradient refinement to exploit structural and boundary cues under appearance ambiguity. We also construct the African Desert Emerging-City Building Change Detection dataset (ADEC-CD) using 2018 and 2024 SuperView-2 imagery of Egypt’s New Administrative Capital. ADEC-CD adopts a geographically independent multi-zone split to reduce spatial leakage. On its geographically held-out test set, FGPMamba achieves mean F1, I o U 1 , Kappa, B-F1, and B-IoU scores of 87.49%, 77.76%, 86.70%, 64.78%, and 40.25%, respectively, over three independent runs. Under dataset-specific training and evaluation, FGPMamba also achieves the highest F1, B-F1, and B-IoU scores among the compared methods on SYSU-CD and HRCUS-CD. Controlled comparisons and feature-response analyses show that the proposed design improves pseudo-change suppression, changed-region completeness, and boundary reliability through frequency-dependent recalibration and boundary-concentrated refinement. These results indicate the potential of FGPMamba for construction monitoring in the study area and potentially similar arid environments. The code and dataset will be publicly available at: https://github.com/zjd1836/FGPMamba .
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: A spatially-adaptive automated sample generation framework via multi-source phenological fusion for large-scale crop mapping: demonstrated on peanuts in Shandong, China
abstract: Accurate regional-scale crop mapping is critical for agricultural monitoring but remains persistently hindered by two fundamental challenges: limited inter-class separability arising from the high spectral-temporal similarity of co-occurring crops, and a label scarcity bottleneck exacerbated by the spatial non-stationarity of crop phenology. To address these limitations, this study proposes a novel Spatially-Adaptive Automated Sample Generation (SAASG) framework. By integrating multi-source remote sensing data with an iterative transfer learning strategy, SAASG autonomously generates high-fidelity training samples across heterogeneous landscapes. The framework’s core innovations are twofold. First, we engineer a Multi-source Phenological Feature Curve (MPFC) that synergizes the orthogonal information of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) backscatter, the optical Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), and a newly developed Contrast-Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (CNDVI). The CNDVI employs a novel spectro-structural modulation mechanism specifically designed to resolve late-season asymptotic saturation. Second, we introduce a Spatially-Adaptive Iterative Domain Adaptation mechanism utilizing a grid-based migration strategy. This discretizes the region into local domains to iteratively propagate phenological knowledge, effectively minimizing domain shift errors through spatial ensemble constraints. Demonstrated on peanuts in Shandong Province, China, the SAASG-generated samples exhibit superior phenological fidelity (Sequence Consistency Score = 0.982 ± 0.008; DTW distance = 0.172 ± 0.050) and possess a statistical distribution statistically congruent with in-situ ground-truth data. Leveraging these automatically labeled samples, we produced a 10-m resolution provincial peanut map with robust accuracy (Overall Accuracy > 0.85) across diverse agro-ecological zones. Crucially, a controlled substitution test confirmed that the classifier trained solely on SAASG samples achieved performance comparable to one trained on labor-intensive field data (ΔOA < 3%). These results confirm that the proposed framework provides a physically interpretable and operationally scalable solution to the training data crisis, enabling reliable large-scale mapping in regions with limited ground observations.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: A multi-scale retrieval of three-dimensional ocean temperature by merging satellite and in situ observations
abstract: Ocean temperature is a key variable in ocean dynamics, exerting broad impacts on the climate and ecosystems. In this study, we develop a multi-scale Bayesian hierarchical modeling framework to retrieve the three-dimensional (3D) ocean temperature by combining satellite and in situ observations. The retrieval process consists of two steps. The first step is to map the subsurface temperature anomaly ( T a ) relative to a climatological seasonal cycle based on satellite-measured sea surface temperature anomaly (SSTA) and sea surface height anomaly (SSHA). The mapping function is estimated from a geographically and seasonally varying coefficient (GSVC) linear regression model to capture the varying mapping relationship caused by the variations of ocean context with space and season. The second step is to fuse the mapped T a with in situ observations under a Bayesian hierarchical modeling framework. This allows the data fusion to take into consideration the mapping errors of T a due to not only variations of T a independent of SSTA and SSHA but also uncertainties in the estimated mapping function. The above mapping-fusion procedure is conducted separately on large-scale and mesoscale ocean processes to account for their distinct characteristics. Application of our method to the Indian Ocean sector of the Southern Ocean yields more accurate retrieval of 3D ocean temperature than a state-of-the-art data product, based on independent in situ test data.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: InterMine: A foundation model-based multi-task interaction network for remote sensing interpretation of open-pit coal mining activity
abstract: The interpretation of open-pit coal mining activity is critical for resource management and ecological protection. It comprises two key tasks: extent extraction and fine-grained change detection. However, existing methods usually suffer from task separation, and their outputs cannot fully meet the requirements of interpretation. Therefore, this study proposes a foundation model-based multi-task interaction network (InterMine) to jointly perform open-pit mine extent extraction and fine-grained change detection. First, InterMine employs a Siamese foundation model as the encoder to enhance feature representation from images of complex open-pit coal mines and incorporates a channel-spatial feature reconstruction module to adapt the encoded features to meet the semantic and spatial requirements of the decoder. Second, a multi-task interaction mechanism is proposed to facilitate complementary information exchange between tasks. Finally, a consistency loss function based on hard-sample reweighting is designed to mitigate inconsistencies among multi-task outputs. InterMine is trained and evaluated on a self-constructed multi-temporal open-pit coal mining activity interpretation dataset (OMSet). Experimental results demonstrate that InterMine outperforms the compared methods. In particular, InterMine achieves F1-scores of 87.57 %, 83.68 %, and 79.43 % for open-pit mine extent extraction, excavation change detection, and reclamation change detection, respectively, outperforming the comparison methods by 1.89 ∼ 5.29, 3.04 ∼ 7.83, and 2.79 ∼ 7.42 percentage points, respectively. This work provides both technical and data support for open-pit coal mine monitoring. OMSet and the code of InterMine have been made publicly available at https://figshare.com/s/03c029d8e4846faef69f .
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Detection of soil moisture variations beneath an asphalt layer using L-band SAR
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR)-based soil moisture retrieval has primarily focused on bare or vegetated surfaces, whereas asphalt generally considered a highly attenuating medium that limits the detection of subsurface soil. Here, we used an L-band SAR sensor in a microwave anechoic chamber to characterize the detectable depth through asphalt and its controlling factors, and further quantitatively investigate the responses of interferometric phase, coherence, and closure phase to infiltration-induced variations in subsurface soil moisture. Results show subsurface echoes remain detectable through at least 9 cm of asphalt using an L-band Mini-SAR, while modeling indicates that increasing transmit power and antenna aperture could extend detectable depth beyond 30 cm. The InSAR observables exhibited distinct responses to infiltration-induced subsurface moisture variations. The mean interferometric phase decreased linearly with increasing soil volumetric water content (VWC) ( r = - 0.992 ), with an average phase shift of approximately 0.53° per 1 % increase in VWC. Spatial analysis further revealed a strong correspondence between regions of reduced coherence and nonzero closure phase and the infiltration-affected area. Overall, this study provides theoretical and methodological support for improving the subsurface detectability of airborne and vehicle-based L-band SAR sensors and for InSAR-based detection of soil moisture variations beneath asphalt layers.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Density-dominated aggregation and spatiotemporal differentiation of yellow sea green tides revealed by long term observations
abstract: Green tides dominated by Ulva prolifera have bloomed in the Yellow Sea since 2008, posing persistent threats to coastal ecosystems. While multiple indicators (including bloom extent, pixel area, coverage area, and biomass) have been used to characterize bloom dynamics, their inconsistent use may obscure assessments of bloom intensity and spatiotemporal variability, leaving their variations across spatial perspectives poorly understood and limiting their practical utility for green tide management. Here, we investigate how the interannual dynamics of Yellow Sea green tides during 2008–2024 differ when evaluated in terms of biomass rather than bloom extent, and the spatial patterns underlying these differences. The annual biomass variability peaked at 3.6 times the long-term average, exceeding the 2.0 times observed for bloom extent. This indicates increasingly dense and aggregated U. prolifera distributions and an underestimation of interannual bloom intensity by bloom extent. In the Subei Bank Front (SBF) perspective, MODIS observations show that U. prolifera first appear near the SBF in early May. U. prolifera biomass in the northern region closely tracked annual biomass across the Yellow Sea, making it the dominant contributor to interannual bloom variability, while the southern region accounted for only 17 %. From the nearshore perspective (within 20 km of the coastline), nearshore green tide biomass has largely remained below the 2008 level (49.90 kt) over the past 16 years, except in 2015 (53.54 kt) and 2019 (70.33 kt), which exceeded it by 7 % and 41 %. The cross-validation identified the annual biomass series excluding the 20 km coastal zone and the region north of the SBF as robust proxies for annual mean biomass under data gaps, with the former yielding a substitution error of 8 %. These findings provide critical quantitative evidence for Yellow Sea green tide monitoring and sustainable coastal ecosystem management in support of SDG 14.2.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Fine-scale annual mapping and dynamic monitoring of shrub encroachment in alpine grasslands by integrating Sentinel-2 phenological features with Sentinel-1 structural information
abstract: Shrub encroachment can alter forage resources, soil–water processes, and landscape configuration in alpine grasslands, yet annual mapping remains challenging because shrub and herbaceous canopies converge spectrally and many apparent changes occur in diffuse ecotones. We developed a 10-m annual mapping framework integrating Sentinel-2 phenology, Sentinel-1 synthetic aperture radar (SAR) time-series information, and topographic covariates to distinguish shrubland from grassland in Maqu County on the northeastern Tibetan Plateau from 2018 to 2024. A learned SAR-derived shrubland-grassland discrimination score (SGDS) was constructed from annual Sentinel-1 descriptors using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO)-regularized logistic regression to improve shrubland-grassland discrimination. In the 2024 benchmark experiment, the selected random forest (RF) configuration reduced classification error by approximately 17% relative to optical-only RF. SGDS outperformed the tested conventional SAR indices and the full SAR-statistics feature set, and adding SGDS increased RF accuracy from 91.26% to 92.47%. When the selected workflow was applied independently to each mapping year, annual overall accuracies ranged from 91.6% to 95.8%, based on the same 500 temporally screened reference locations spatially separated from the model-development samples. Nominal mapped shrubland area increased from 392.3 km2 in 2018 to 648.2 km2 in 2022 before declining to 560.4 km2 in 2024. Confidence and boundary-sensitivity analyses showed that the pronounced 2020–2021 increase was largely associated with low-confidence ecotonal pixels and decreased from + 96.91 to + 6.09 km2 as the mapped-class confidence threshold increased from 0.60 to 0.80, whereas the 2022–2024 decline remained negative under all tested confidence and boundary screens. Mapped shrubland area showed an apparent positive association with annual mean temperature, but this relationship was not robust after detrending and should be considered preliminary given the seven-year record. Overall, integrating learned SAR structural information with optical phenology improved annual shrubland-grassland mapping and provided a more reliable basis for interpreting mapped dynamics, with potential for locally calibrated application in comparable alpine regions.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: A framework for inversion and assimilation of deep-sea mirror ocean acoustic tomography observations
abstract: The deep ocean plays a critical role in the global climate system. However, satellite Earth observation is limited to the sea surface, while in-situ measurements struggle to achieve synchronous coverage over vast oceanic areas. Ocean Acoustic Tomography (OAT) is an essential method for retrieving large-scale interior ocean parameters; however, its path-integral nature leads to high-dimensional and ill-posed inverse problems when applied to the deep ocean. To address this, this paper develops a unified modular framework for the inversion and assimilation of acoustic remote sensing data, specifically designed for Mirror OAT (MOAT) in the deep sea. Through a configurable dimensionality reduction representation, the framework regularizes the ill-posed inverse problem in a low-dimensional space, enabling a stable and efficient numerical solution. High-resolution ocean model-based simulation experiments are conducted to evaluate its performance. Results show that the inversion module reconstructs 3-D flow fields via a “section-to-plane” two-step method, with inversion errors below 0.15 m/s over most of the water column relative to the true fields from the high-resolution ocean model. The assimilation module integrates observations using an Ensemble Kalman Filter based on a low-dimensional subspace, improving the analysis field accuracy by approximately 35 % compared to the background field. Further sensitivity experiments indicate that the assimilation method exhibits superior robustness against observation noise, while the inversion method offers higher computational efficiency by requiring neither an ensemble of model forecasts nor sequential cycling. Parameter analyses provide a basis for selecting the appropriate approach under different scenarios. This study provides a complete workflow, from methodology to numerical validation, for efficient and accurate estimation of deep-sea interior states from MOAT observations. It may serve as a reference for the design and operational application of deep-sea 3-D remote sensing observation systems.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Integrated remote sensing and geotechnical investigations of the 2022 Jiujiawan mudstone landslide in Xining city, China: from deformation monitoring to failure mechanisms
abstract: Mudstone landslides are widespread worldwide, with their initiation and evolution mainly governed by the coupled effects of rock mass microstructure and hydromechanical behavior. However, the linkage between Earth observation (EO)-derived deformation signals and microscale weakening mechanisms remains poorly constrained.
